title: Returning Real Madrid star faces risk of falling behind in the pecking order amid AS Roma interest
description: Endrick returned to Real Madrid this summer on the back of a stellar loan spell at Olympique Lyon, with many expecting him to play a key role for Los Blancos in the season ahead.However, in the early ...
fullText:
Endrick returned to Real Madrid this summer on the back of a stellar loan spell at Olympique Lyon, with many expecting him to play a key role for Los Blancos in the season ahead.

However, in the early days of pre-season, things are not looking good for Endrick, who will have to cope with more competition than he would have expected.

A recent report from Gazzetta Dello Sport has given comprehensive insights into Endrick’s tricky situation at Real Madrid, heading into the new season.

Endrick will undergo key conditioning from Mourinho in coming weeks. (Photo by Ira L. Black/Getty Images)

According to the report, Endrick’s characteristics do not appear entirely compatible with Real Madrid’s new project under Jose Mourinho.

The Portuguese coach, aside from Kylian Mbappe, was on the lookout for a different kind of striker, a more physical presence better suited to his tactical ideas.

He found exactly that in Carlos Espi, the young forward who signed this week and impressed on his debut against Fiorentina.

That leaves Endrick as something of an awkward fit. His profile does not align neatly with what Mourinho wants from his forwards, and in an attacking line already boasting Mbappe, Vinicius Jr, Brahim Diaz and Rodrygo, the Brazilian could find himself well down the pecking order.

Endrick will reportedly undergo an evaluation from Mourinho in the coming days, a process that could prove decisive in determining his immediate future at the Bernabeu.

AS Roma are interested in Endrick. (Photo by Dan Mullan/Getty Images)

The danger for Endrick is clear. Should he slip down the order, he risks receiving few or even no minutes, a scenario that could ultimately force Real Madrid to consider sanctioning a loan move.

That possibility has not gone unnoticed elsewhere. Roma have been monitoring Endrick for over a month, with the Brazilian a genuine target for the Serie A side.

Coach Gian Piero Gasperini is a firm admirer, viewing him not just as a central striker but also as a player capable of operating on either flank.

Roma’s sporting director even travelled to Madrid recently to gauge the feasibility of a deal and assess Real Madrid’s willingness to let the player leave.

The Italians are keen to include an option to buy, much like Como did in the Nico Paz deal, to avoid the risk of developing Endrick only to lose him later.

For now, though, Endrick’s fate rests on his evaluation under Mourinho, with a pivotal few weeks ahead.

title: ‘Unbelievably Sad’ — Jason Whitlock Left Unimpressed With Cam Newton’s Bizarre Strip Club Admission
description: Cam Newton finds himself back in the headlines for a bizarre confession about his trips to strip clubs. In a resurfaced clip from the “Funky Friday” podcast, the former NFL MVP claimed that he never visited strip clubs because of the women.
fullText:
Cam Newton finds himself back in the headlines for a bizarre confession about his trips to strip clubs.

In a resurfaced clip from the “Funky Friday” podcast, the former NFL MVP claimed that he never visited strip clubs because of the women. This admission did not sit well with analyst and commentator Jason Whitlock.

Newton explained that he went to strip clubs to compete with other men and see who could spend the most money.

“I never went to a strip club for women. I always went to strip clubs for guys,” Newton said back in Dec. 2024. “I’m a competitor. I wasn’t gonna spend no money if I didn’t see nobody else spending no money.

“As soon as I see somebody thinking that they’ve got money… ‘Okay, you spending five? I’mma spend six. If you gonna spend 10, I’mma spend 15.’ We’re gonna have a rain off.”

Newton treated the experience like another competition.

“That’s my whole thing, I don’t go to strip clubs for chicks even though I want decoration. I was a competitor and still am a competitor… That 15 you making, I’mma spend my 15 and I’mma make it back easy,” he said.

REDRAFT THE ENTIRE NFL: PFN’s FREE NFL Ultimate Redraft Simulator

After the resurfaced clip went viral on X, it caught the attention of Whitlock, who had a pretty blunt reaction.

“Unbelievably sad,” Whitlock wrote.

Newton had an 11-year NFL career, most of which he spent with the Carolina Panthers. He was a three-time Pro Bowler who totaled 32,382 passing yards, 194 passing touchdowns, and 123 interceptions, while also rushing for 5,628 yards and 75 scores on the ground.

Recently, ESPN laid off Newton as a result of the network’s major shake-up involving several high-profile personalities. Newton, who usually appeared alongside Stephen A. Smith on “First Take” was among several departures.

BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN’s FREE NFL Mock Draft Simulator

The 37-year-old joined ESPN in October 2024 and had signed a multi-year extension last August that expanded his role, so the news was a bit of a surprise.

Newton wasn’t the only big name affected. ESPN also moved on from NFL analyst Ryan Clark, NFL Network insider Tom Pelissero, and longtime baseball broadcaster Karl Ravech among others. ESPN chairman Jimmy Pitaro explained that the layoffs were a result of the company’s recent acquisition of NFL Network.

“Over the past several months, we’ve made significant progress integrating the NFL assets that we acquired into ESPN…” Pitaro wrote in an internal memo. “As a result, we had to make some difficult decisions about job impacts that we will be communicating today.

“While most of the job impacts are tied to the acquisition, we will also notify colleagues in other parts of the company today that their positions have been impacted.”

While Newton is no longer at ESPN, he still has his own podcast, “4th & 1,” which he co-hosts with Omari “Peggy” Collins.

This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network.

title: Details: José Mourinho’s plan for Jude Bellingham at Real Madrid
description: An insight into the plans of new Real Madrid head coach José Mourinho for midfield standout Jude Bellingham has this weekend been provided.This comes amid the understanding that the Englishman will b...
fullText:
An insight into the plans of new Real Madrid head coach José Mourinho for midfield standout Jude Bellingham has this weekend been provided.

This comes amid the understanding that the Englishman will be utilised in his favoured position under the watch of his new headmaster.

Bellingham is of course yet to report back to Spain’s capital this summer. Following his exploits on the international stage at the World Cup, the former Borussia Dortmund man has been afforded an extended break.

In his absence, the aforementioned Mourinho has shown his hand in pre-season friendly fixtures, making use of a 4-2-3-1 formation across all three of Los Blancos’ outings.

At the heart of these line-ups has been Arda Güler, afforded the free role in the no.10 position. And the Turk has taken full advantage of his chance, impressing in the attacking midfield berth to date.

If the latest word stemming from Spain is anything to go by, however, then Arda need not get too comfortable in this spot.

As per a report from Diario AS this weekend:

‘The number ten position will go to Jude Bellingham. Who, if he’s been watching the friendlies, is starting to understand what’s expected of him. Güler is leaving him clues along the way.’

Mourinho, a huge fan of Arda, will in turn attempt to find a different role for the 21-year-old, who will also act as backup for Bellingham in the ’10’ this season.

title: Nets front-office executive speaks on Egor Demin's current form
description: Brooklyn Nets guard Egor Demin showed plenty of growth this summer in Brooklyn's summer circuit and a Nets front-office executive discussed his play.
fullText:
Brooklyn Nets guard Egor Demin had a solid rookie season with enough promising elements to it that many people in the Nets fanbase were wondering what he would do to improve. Brooklyn believed in Demin's ability to grow as a three-point shooter, but they were also asking him to take the next step in his game and it seems that the front office is taking notice of his work.

"He’s a lot more comfortable going into Year 2. I think from the pre-draft process, all the way through his rookie year, we probably over-indexed on his three-point shot too much," a Nets front-office executive said of Demin, per Keith Smith of Spotrac. Demin did not shoot the three-ball well during his one-and-done year at BYU, but it seemed like improving his shot was Brooklyn's main priority with him and he finished last season shooting 38.5% from deep.

"I mean Egor, his trainers, our front office, our coaches, everyone. You saw out here (at Summer League), that he was getting downhill more. This year is about putting him in even better spots to shine as an all-around player," the Nets front-office executive continued on Demin, per Smith. As the exec alluded to, Demin spent most of his time during the summer circuit trying to get to the rim thanks to his added bulk.

Demin, 20, finished his rookie season with averages of 10.3 points, 3.2 rebounds, and 3.3 assists per game while shooting 39.9% from the field and attempting just 1.3 free-throws per game. During Brooklyn's summer circuit in which the team participated in the California Classic and Las Vegas Summer League, Demin averaged 21.8 points, 5.2 rebounds, 3.8 assists, and 1.8 steals per game while shooting 47.3% from the floor and 28.9% from three-point land.

While Demin had more responsibility as part of Brooklyn's summer league team, he will be heading into next season with forwards Michael Porter Jr. and Julius Randle leading the way on offense. However, that veteran duo will need someone to stretch the floor and potentially create rim pressure to allow the offense to be more efficient so Demin's growth this offseason could be key to the Nets' success next year.

This article originally appeared on Nets Wire: Nets front-office executive speaks on Egor Demin's current form

title: Atlanta Braves Shifting Focus In Starter Market With Tarik Skubal Off The Board
description: The Braves have expressed strong interest in Detroit Tigers' starter Casey Mize ahead of the deadline tomorrow.
fullText:
The Atlanta Braves had been known as one of the primary contenders willing to throw their chips in for frontline starter Tarik Skubal before the trade deadline. But after Saturday night, a pivot will now need to be made.

In a classic notion of expectation turned to reality, the Los Angeles Dodgers were the team to secure Skubal from the Detroit Tigers for the remainder of this season, trading off three prospects in a blockbuster move and trumping the Braves’ hopes of securing the left-hander.

Atlanta had been seen as one of the real players for him, according to Jon Heyman of the NY Post, especially with how much help another starting pitcher would bring to this team. But now with Skubal off the market, the Braves only have just over 24 hours to make their move for another.

In fact, they are focusing their sights on a starting pitcher in Detroit.

With Skubal now off the board, the Braves have expressed strong interest in Tigers starting pitcher Casey Mize, per Pat Ragazzo of Athlon Sports.

The Tigers recently made their potential desires to move Mize known when they scratched him from his Friday start against the Athletics, as a non-injury precaution ahead of the deadline.

At the time, no trade appeared to be imminent for Mize, per . But with the Braves now likely looking to be much more aggressive after missing on Skubal, they are definitely a team to keep an eye on in the sweepstakes for him.

This season, Mize has seen two trips to the injured list and has dealt with a nagging groin issue. But when he is on the mound, he has proved to be one of the league’s most productive starters.

Mize has recorded the best numbers of his career this season, posting a 2.70 ERA and 4.47 strikeout to walk ratio. In 16 starts this year, his 2.9 fWAR already marks a career-high.

The 29-year-old starter has dealt with a decent sum of injuries over the past couple of years, which includes hamstring and groin issues, but has not dealt with anything arm-related since he underwent Tommy John surgery in 2022.

The addition of Mize to the Braves’ rotation would provide them with an efficient starter to rely on, which has been hard to come by for the team this season.

Chris Sale has continued to be the team’s ace, but the supporting cast around him has not been as efficient. The Braves placed Reynaldo López on the injured list this morning, while Bryce Elder has dropped off after a strong start to the season. Martín Pérez and Grant Holmes have both been solid in their roles, but are not exactly the frontline starters you trust wholeheartedly in the postseason.

Adding Mize to the mix would give the Braves another arm to trust down the stretch with much upside to him. Mize is set to be a free agent at the end of the season.

title: Lions duo exit Sunday practice early to be evaluated for injuries
description: A pair of Detroit Lions exited Sunday's practice early to be evaluated for potential injuries.
fullText:
A pair of Detroit Lions exited Sunday's training camp practice early to be evaluated for potential injuries.

Per Detroit Lions senior writer and insider Tim Twentyman, rookie defensive end Derrick Moore (groin) and tight end Miles Kitselman (leg) both exited practice early to be evaluated for potential injuries.

The Lions selected Moore in the second round of the 2026 NFL Draft with the No. 44 overall pick, trading up with the New York Jets in order to do so. The 6-foot-3, 260-pound EDGE had 30 tackles and 10 sacks last season at Michigan. The Baltimore, Md., native also added 10.5 tackles for loss, three pass breakups, two forced fumbles and one fumble recovery in 2025.

Moore registered 95 tackles, 21 sacks, eight passes defended and three forced fumbles in his Michigan career.

The following players left practice early today to be evaluated for potential injuries:

TE Miles Kitselman (leg)

DE Derrick Moore (groin)

— Tim Twentyman (@ttwentyman) August 2, 2026

The Lions inked Miles Kitselman as one of its nine undrafted free agent signings in May. Kitselman, a 6-foot-5, 251-pound tight end, caught 50 passes for 572 yards and six scores during his college career, including 26 grabs for 253 yards and a pair of scores last season at Tennessee.

On the positive end of the equation, defensive back Christian Izien made his training camp debut with the Lions after being sidelined on the NFI with the flu. Lions starting left guard Christian Mahogany is also now off the NFI, returning to the fold last Friday.

Per Pride of Detroit's Jeremy Reisman, guard Ben Bartch and EDGE Payton Turner were among those that didn't practice on Sunday. Rookie offensive tackle Blake Miller also appeared to be limited on Sunday. Miller went through walkthroughs and individual drills, but he did not take any full-team reps and was not participating in 1-on-1s.

Larry Borom and Miles Frazier split time at right tackle with the first-team offense.

title: Dodgers visit Tigers Aug. 28-30: Will Tarik Skubal pitch in series?
description: Whether Tarik Skubal pitches against the Tigers at Comerica Park later this month will depend on manager Dave Roberts' starting pitching plans.
fullText:
Tarik Skubal will return to Detroit later this month, and not just to pick up his belongings.

The Los Angeles Dodgers play the Tigers at Comerica Park on Aug. 28-30, which will mark the return of Detroit's now-former ace and two-time reigning Cy Young winner.

Skubal was traded from the Tigers to the Dodgers on Sunday in a blockbuster move ahead of Monday's trade deadline.

Skubal, 29, is expected to make his first start for the Dodgers against the Chicago Cubs at Wrigley Field on Tuesday. The question Tigers fans want to know: Would that put him line to start against Detroit at Comerica Park?

The simple answer is: Stay tuned.

If he starts Tuesday and the Dodgers stick to pitching him every five games, then he would just miss the Tigers series (assuming the Dodgers don't have any rainouts). But the Dodgers also have three days off between now and then, so if they decide to pitch Skubal every five days, then he would be in line to start against the Tigers, the team that drafted him in the ninth round of the 2018 draft and developed him into one of the best pitchers in the game.

If Skubal pitches every five games: Tuesday at Cubs, Aug. 10 vs. Royals, Aug. 15 vs. Brewers, Aug. 21 vs. Pirates, Aug. 27 at Braves

If Skubal pitches every five days: Tuesday at Cubs, Aug. 9 at Diamondbacks, Aug. 14 vs. Brewers, Aug. 19 at Rockies, Aug. 25 at Braves, Aug. 30 at Tigers

Of course, the Dodgers could do a combination of both days and games between starts for Skubal. If they value making his starts at Dodger Stadium (why wouldn't they), the every-five-games scenario lines up much better.

Skubal made his last start for the Tigers at Comerica Park on Wednesday, allowing three runs on four hits in 6⅔ innings against the Baltimore Orioles in a game the Tigers lost, 10-9, in 12 innings after leading 7-0.

Skubal left in the seventh inning to a standing ovation from Tigers fans.

This article originally appeared on The Detroit News: Dodgers visit Tigers Aug. 28-30: Will Tarik Skubal pitch in series?

title: WNBA trade deadline tracker: Live rumors, news, updates before 2026 deadline
description: The Sporting News is tracking rumors and updates from the WNBA trade deadline. Follow along for full updates.
fullText:
WNBA trade deadline tracker: Live rumors, news, updates before 2026 deadline originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The WNBA is heading into the home stretch, as the trade deadline signals the final months of the regular season.

With the WNBA playoff picture pretty clear-cut, given that there is a significant gap between the eighth and ninth teams in the standings, many of the trade deadline moves could be more for playoff positioning with eyes on the postseason run.

The question becomes which teams at the top of the standings feel good about their playoff-caliber rosters, and which ones feel as though they need to add upgrades. Additionally, a team like the Golden State Valkyries may aim to be aggressive in their first season of contention.

A few big names, however, could be on the move because they are playing on expiring contracts, with Kelsey Plum and even Napheesa Collier set to hit free agency after the season. Of course, there could also be some surprise players on the move that might change the race for a WNBA championship.

The Sporting News is tracking rumors and updates from the WNBA trade deadline. Follow along for full updates.

MORE: 9 WNBA players most likely to be traded

After heading to The Valley to join the Phoenix Mercury, Plum will reportedly be present at the team's game on Monday night in Chicago. For now, it's uncertain whether or not Phoenix's new star will suit up for the team on the hardwood tomorrow. She last appeared for Los Angeles on June 21.

After a few weeks of being in trade talks, former Las Vegas Aces and Los Angeles Sparks star Kelsey Plum is heading south to join the Phoenix Mercury. In exchange, 25-year-old guard Monique Akoa Makani, a 2027 first-round pick, and a 2028 second-rounder are heading to the City of Angels.

The Sun are trading second-year forward Aneesah Morrow to the Toronto Tempo for a 2028 second-round pick and the rights to Maria Kilundikova. Morrow was the No. 7 pick in last year's draft and is coming off back-to-back 21-point games after her return from injury.

The Liberty discussed trading for second-year Sun forward Aneesah Morrow, Madeline Kenney reports, but those talks have since "cooled off." Morrow recently returned from injury and is averaging 11.6 points per game for Connecticut.

With Kelsey Plum a pending free agent, the Sparks are "asking for the world" in trade talks, Ramona Shelburne reports. Plum, averaging close to 24 points per game, isn't expected to re-sign with L.A., making a trade likely at the deadline.

The expansion Toronto team has reportedly sent both the Sun and the Sparks offers including first-round picks for a young post player. With the Tempo in the bottom five in the WNBA standings, any deal is more likely to include the 2028 first-round pick than in 2027.

According to Costabile, the disappointing Mercury may look to take on the next 2.5 years of Smith's deal in order to land the forward. Smith is the reigning Defensive Player of the Year who is averaging just 3.8 points per game in a down year and may need a change of scenery halfway through her first season in Dallas.

Plum's status as a rental means she is expected to be on the move, especially since she doesn't seem to want to return to Los Angeles next year. The 31-year-old is averaging a career-high 23.9 points and 6.4 rebounds so far this year and has made five straight All-Star games.

From PHO: G Monique Akoa Makani, 2027 first-round pick, 2028 second-round pick

title: Jordan Walsh breaks down how extension impacts pressure, role with Boston Celtics
description: "It does give a level of security, and a level of belief that the ...organization has for me," said Walsh.
fullText:
It is not just Boston Celtics big man Neemias Queta who has been breathing easier after signing a contract extension this summer among the Celtics youth movement. Forward Jordan Walsh also got a financial vote of confidence from Boston President of Basketball Operations Brad Stevens earlier in the 2026 NBA offseason as well, to the tune of three years and a total of $15 million fresh on the heels of the team picking up the team option on the last season of his rookie deal.

"It was great," said Walsh of the extension in a recent interview with NBC Sports Boston reporter Chis Forsberg. "I think it's perfect for me at the moment. I feel like ... it does give a level of security, and a level of belief that the ...organization has for me."

"So I think it's a big step," he added. "I think it will propel my growth to a different level, because now I'm here with the Celtics ... Now it feels like – not that it didn't feel real before, but now it feels more real – more secure, more like I'm in it, you know? And so I think that's the greatest peace of mind that it gave me; that's the biggest thing."

"I think it's a new starting point, checkpoint for my career," Walsh added. "I think that the first three years of my career was trying to prove that I could play in the league. And I think that I've proven that I can play in the league and I'm an NBA player."

"Now it's about getting better at the areas that I'm weak so that I can continue to get better and earn more and produce more, those types of things."

title: How golden Emma Finucane mastered the pressure to make Commonwealth Games history
description: Finucane became the first rider in 96 years to complete a Commonwealth Games sprint clean sweep
fullText:
Emma Finucane has spent much of the past two years learning how to live with expectation. In Glasgow, she discovered how to thrive under it.

The Welsh cyclist became the first rider in 96 years to complete a Commonwealth Games sprint clean sweep, winning gold in the time trial, sprint, team sprint and keirin.

Yet the significance of the achievement, she revealed, was not just the medals themselves but also the way she dealt with the pressure that came with them.

After winning three medals at Paris 2024, Finucane returned home as one of the most recognisable figures in Olympic sport.

With that status came a new challenge, the knowledge that every rival wanted to beat her.

“After Paris, I definitely felt like I had a target on my back,” she said. “But I’ve learned to embrace that.

“I’ve learned how to deal with it better and just focus on improving every day.

“After Paris, everything was a huge learning curve for me emotionally too.

“That week was really tough, and what I achieved was difficult to process. But going into these Games, I’ve learned how to handle pressure better and regulate my emotions more.”

That development was evident throughout a week in which Finucane appeared increasingly comfortable with her position as the rider to beat.

In the keirin final, she took the unusual decision to move to the front with two laps remaining, exposing herself to the slipstream of the riders behind her. It was a calculated risk that could have left her vulnerable in the closing stages.

The keirin is cycling’s answer to a chess match played at 70km/h: six riders circling behind a pacing bike before the tactical battle explodes into a final-lap sprint.

But Finucane had already taken control long before the final dash.

She controlled the race from the front and secured the fourth gold medal of a remarkable Games.

“I did feel the pressure, of course, especially with people talking about history and what could be achieved,” she said, before a quick shower and change of clothes so she could carry the Welsh flag at the closing ceremony.

“But as an athlete, you don’t really think about that in the moment. You’re just in your own bubble, focused on the next race.

“I knew I had a chance to do something special, but anything can happen in sprinting. I nearly didn’t even get through the semi-final, so it just shows you have to take it one race at a time.“I’m always thinking about the next thing, but I really want to stay in the moment now.

“That’s something I haven’t always been good at, but I’m trying to change that.”

Any suggestion that Finucane’s achievement came against diminished opposition was quickly dismissed by the quality of the riders she defeated.

Olympic champion Ellesse Andrews took silver while defending her title, Katy Marchant – her Olympic team sprint team-mate – finished fifth, while Sophie Capewell, the other member of that Team GB trio, failed to reach the final.

Finucane’s achievement also secured her a place in Welsh sporting history. She became the first Welsh woman to win four gold medals at a single Commonwealth Games, moving beyond para-sprinter Olivia Breen’s record as Wales’ most successful female athlete at the event.

The overall Welsh record remains with weightlifter David Morgan, whose haul of nine gold medals and three silver medals makes him the nation’s most decorated Commonwealth athlete.

“I just hope I’ve inspired people back home to get on a bike or into a velodrome,” she added.

“I’m so glad I found this sport – or maybe it found me. I absolutely love what I do.”

Away from the track, Finucane’s week also contained distracting questions about her partner Matt Richardson, who was forced to withdraw from the Commonwealth Games after suffering an injury.

Richardson, who controversially switched allegiance from Australia to Great Britain, had been expected to compete in Glasgow but was ruled out before the start of the competition.

Despite his absence, Finucane said his support — alongside that of her family — had been crucial throughout her historic week.

“My mum, dad, sister and her partner were all here, and my brother was watching from home,” she said. “My partner was even on FaceTime from Japan at 2am. That support network is everything to me.”

“My partner was even on FaceTime from Japan at 2am. That support network is everything to me. They love me no matter what, win or lose, and that takes all the pressure away.”

For now, though, Finucane is determined not to look too far ahead. First comes a holiday to Corfu before she narrows her focus on October's World Championships and then the 2028 Olympics.

“I just want to keep riding my bike, keep enjoying it, and keep improving," she added.

"I’m grateful for everything I’ve achieved, and I don’t take any of it for granted.”

title: Giants' game-by-game predictions for 2026 season in first year under John Harbaugh
description: Predicting how the New York Giants will fare in the 2026 NFL season.
fullText:
Giants' game-by-game predictions for 2026 season in first year under John Harbaugh originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The New York Giants are a team on the rise in the eyes of many. Things began to transform for the team last season when Jaxson Dart was inserted as the team's starting quarterback and the hiring of John Harbaugh as the team's new head coach this offseason was a sign that this organization means business.

The Giants have made the playoffs just once in the last decade and the team is 13-38 across the last three seasons. It was time for a culture change and if anyone can implement that in a positive way, it's Harbaugh, the long-time coach of the Baltimore Ravens.

The Giants will be a trendy dark-horse pick this season in a league where teams routinely go from worst to first in their divisions. The Philadelphia Eagles have won the division in each of the last two seasons, becoming the first team to win the division in back-to-back years since they did it back in 2003 and 2024.

Week 1: September 13 vs. Dallas Cowboys

What a way to open the season. The Giants will host the Cowboys on Sunday Night Football and this will be a great chance to start the Harbaugh era out with a bang. The Cowboys are going to get a trendy NFC pick to compete this season as well, so they will be up for this one.

A healthy Giants team with Dart, Malik Nabers and Cam Skattebo get the Harbaugh era off to a good start with the game being played at MetLife Stadium being the key factor.

Week 2: September 21 at Los Angeles Rams

The Giants go from a Sunday night game to a Monday night game. The Rams are going to be one of the best teams in the league this season and this young Giants team won't be ready for this kind of challenge just yet.

Week 3: September 27 vs. Tennessee Titans

The Giants have their first game that isn't on primetime television and against a Titans team that is still looking to create an identity with new head coach Robert Saleh. This game will be more competitive than some might expect but the Giants get out with the win.

Week 4: October 4 vs. Arizona Cardinals

This is where getting to play that last-place schedule can get teams off to a good start. The Cardinals appear to be one of the weaker teams in the league in 2026 with their new head coach Mike LaFleur and it's another game where the Giants get to play at home. That will be one of the biggest factors in the first quadrant of this season's schedule.

Week 5: October 11 at Washington Commanders

This is definitely a winnable game for the Giants, but the Commanders are a solid opponent with Jayden Daniels at quarterback, particularly on the road. It could go either way but the Commanders kick a game-winning field goal with just seconds left to take the first matchup between the teams this season.

Week 6: October 11 vs. New Orleans Saints

The Saints are a team, like the Giants, that many expect to be much better this season. But this is a game where the Giants' defense uses the noise of the home crowd to its advantage and forces the young quarterback Tyler Shough into a couple of mistakes that swing the result in their favor.

Week 7: October 25 at Houston Texans

This could be one of the biggest tests Dart faces this year as the Texans have arguably the best defense in the NFL. This one could be one of those 60-minute dogfights where in the end, the Texans' defense just makes it too difficult for the Giants to score many points.

Week 9: November 8 at Philadelphia Eagles

This is going to be one of the best games of the season. The Giants will be coming off their bye week and though they have to travel to Philly, this will be the third divisional matchup in a row for the Eagles, which comes right before their bye week.

They're going to be ready for a break and the Giants will be able to take advantage of that to steal one on the road.

Week 10: November 12 vs. Washington Commanders

It's a short week coming off a hard-fought win over the Eagles, but it's a home game. The Giants get one back on the Commanders here after an earlier loss.

Week 11: November 22 vs. Jacksonville Jaguars

The nice thing about playing on a Thursday night is having 10 days to rest before the next game. The Giants will then play host to the Jaguars, who were terrific last season, but several analysts believe they will take a step back this season after what many feel was a rough offseason for the team.

This game between inter-conference opponents feels like it has the makings for a shootout.

Week 12: November 29 at Indianapolis Colts

This will be the Giants' last game against the AFC South this season, and it will be one that Colts quarterback Daniel Jones has circled on his calendar. This will be his chance for some revenge against the team that drafted him and then later released him. Will he be healthy at that stage of the season?

If he is, he gets that measure of revenge against his former squad.

Week 13: December 6 vs. San Francisco 49ers

Any time you play the 49ers, the immediate question surrounds the health of their team. Kyle Shanahan seems to deal with more injuries than any coach in the league by a lot, but he always has his team disciplined and ready to play regardless. The Giants will take a loss in this game but it will be one of those defeats where they learn quite a bit about where they stand the rest of the way.

Week 14: December 3 at Seattle Seahawks

This has turned into a tough stretch in the schedule for the G-Men. A trip to Lumen Field to face the defending champions doesn't help.

Week 15: December 20 vs. Cleveland Browns

What was becoming such a promising season for the Giants has drastically turned following a three-game losing streak, but this matchup is just what the doctor ordered.

Whether it's Deshaun Watson, Shedeur Sanders, or someone else at quarterback for the Browns, this is a game where the trio of Brian Burns, Abdul Carter and Kayvon Thibodeaux takes over. The Giants register eight sacks in this game as they pound the Browns, a team Harbaugh knows a lot about beating.

Week 16: December 28 at Detroit Lions

The Giants get their second game of the season on Monday Night Football and it could easily be a playoff-like atmosphere in the Motor City. The Lions will be hungry for a win here and the Giants will find out again that they are just a notch below some of the top-flight NFC teams.

Week 17: January 3 at Dallas Cowboys

Just after the New Year, it's a Week 1 rematch in a game where playoff positioning at this stage of the season will be very important. The health of these two teams and whether or not there is anything to play for will make a big difference in this one, but assuming playoff spots could be on the line for both teams, the Giants come up short of the season sweep over the Cowboys.

Week 18: Date/Time TBD vs. Philadelphia Eagles

The Giants get to finish the season at home and have a chance to sweep the Eagles, something they have not done since 2007. Whether or not nine wins gets the Giants into the playoffs would be questionable, but they play spirited ball in this game to show that not only was Harbaugh the right choice as the team's head coach, but that the future is incredibly bright.

title: NFL insider shares stellar reviews of Myles Garrett, Trent McDuffie from camp
description: Albert Breer says Myles Garrett has been "better than advertised" and the Rams believe Trent McDuffie can be the best DB in football.
fullText:
There’s been a lot of hype surrounding Myles Garrett and Trent McDuffie as the Los Angeles Rams’ blockbuster additions this offseason. Garrett is the reigning Defensive Player of the Year and McDuffie is a two-time All-Pro, each making the Rams defense significantly better.

As exciting as those two newcomers are, it appears they’ve been even better than anticipated. Albert Breer of Sports Illustrated visited Rams training camp recently and he says Garrett has been better than advertised, fitting “in seamlessly.”

As for McDuffie, Breer wouldn’t be surprised if he’s a captain in his first season with the Rams, and that the team thinks he “can become perhaps the NFL’s best defensive back” in a similar role to what Jalen Ramsey played in L.A.

The buzz about the new guys is very real. Myles Garrett has been, believe it or not, better than advertised, has fit in seamlessly and should benefit from having a deep, loaded group of defensive linemen around him. And Trent McDuffie has checked every box, as a guy who can play field, boundary and slot corner, and is a tough, physical tone-setter—I wouldn’t be surprised if he’s a captain in his first year as a Ram. The team believes he can become perhaps the NFL’s best defensive back in a role not unlike the one that Jalen Ramsey (who, admittedly, is a bigger, more physically imposing player) played in Los Angeles. Those two guys alone should make a very significant difference, and that’s with all due respect to Jared Verse, who was part of the cost of getting Garrett.

The Rams were thrilled to acquire both players this offseason and it's easy to see why. Garrett is the unanimous best edge rusher in the NFL, and McDuffie is a premier cornerback – both in the slot and on the outside.

If they live up to expectations, Los Angeles' defense is going to be a terrifying unit.

title: Mets trade Freddy Peralta to the Rays for a trio of minor leaguers
description: Freddy Peralta is heading to Tampa, according to sources. After a brief but disappointing tenure with the Mets, the right-handed starter has been traded to the Tampa Bay Rays in exchange for three minor leaguers, pending a physical. He’s the second pitcher to be traded out of Queens this week, with left-hander A.J. Minter going to the Minnesota Twins late Thursday night.
fullText:
Freddy Peralta is heading to Tampa, according to sources.

After a brief but disappointing tenure with the Mets, the right-handed starter has been traded to the Tampa Bay Rays in exchange for three minor leaguers, pending a physical. He’s the second pitcher to be traded out of Queens this week, with left-hander A.J. Minter going to the Minnesota Twins late Thursday night. Clay Holmes, Luke Weaver, Brooks Raley and Huascar Brazobán are also expected to be traded ahead of Monday’s 6 p.m. ET trade deadline.

Peralta was acquired from the Milwaukee Brewers over the winter to lead the Mets’ rotation, but was never able to become the ace he had been over the last three seasons once in New York. It was a frustrating season for the 30-year-old Dominican. He’s healthy, and his stuff is still there, yet the results were dismal almost right from the start. He leaves the Mets with a 5-9 record and a 4.99 ERA over 22 starts.

Peralta’s 1.2 WAR this season is one of the worst among all qualified starters in baseball.

The Rays had interest in Holmes as well, who is pitching for Low-A Brooklyn on Sunday, while the Mets finished a series against the Miami Marlins at Citi Field. They sent two scouts to watch him pitch in Florida earlier this week. The top team in the AL East has been seeking pitching help to bolster an already solid rotation that has Drew Rasmussen, Shane McClanahan and Nick Martinez.

title: Liverpool transfer target could be heading to Saudi Pro League in mega money deal
description: Rayan transfer latest as Al Hilal step up plans for Bournemouth forwardAl Hilal are moving with intent in the market again, and their latest focus appears to be Bournemouth attacker Rayan, a player Li...
fullText:
Al Hilal are moving with intent in the market again, and their latest focus appears to be Bournemouth attacker Rayan, a player Liverpool have tracked in recent months. According to Globo Esporte, the Saudi Pro League side are preparing an approach as Simone Inzaghi shapes his squad for the 2026/27 season.

The 19-year-old has seen his profile rise sharply after an eye-catching first spell in the Premier League. Bournemouth’s recruitment has earned praise for spotting high-upside talent early, and Rayan now looks like another example of that model working. His performances have carried domestic impact and international attention, with his World Cup displays further strengthening the sense that he is one of Brazil’s standout young forwards.

The background to this one is important. Al Hilal are expected to make changes in attacking areas, and the report states Rayan is being lined up as the ideal long-term replacement for Malcom. The Brazilian winger is seemingly no longer central to Inzaghi’s plans, which has triggered work on succession planning rather than a short-term fix.

That approach fits the wider strategy often seen from Saudi clubs at the top end of the market, identifying premium targets and moving decisively. If Al Hilal formalise their interest, any deal would quickly become difficult for rivals, simply because of the financial strength they can bring to the table.

Liverpool’s admiration for emerging South American talent has been evident for some time, and recent recruitment underlined that trend. Rayan sits squarely in the bracket of player the club would monitor closely, young, technically gifted, and already proving capable of adapting to elite-level football.

Whether interest turns active is another matter. Liverpool under Andoni Iraola will have clear priorities and a defined structure to work within. Yet when a player of this age, trajectory and versatility becomes available, it tends to command attention. Even if there is no immediate move from Anfield, Al Hilal’s push could force a faster decision on whether to engage or step back.

For now, the strongest indication is that Al Hilal are serious and planning ahead. Bournemouth, meanwhile, are in the enviable position of holding a young asset whose value is moving only one way. Liverpool’s previous links ensure this is one to monitor closely as the window develops, especially if early contact from Saudi Arabia turns into a concrete offer.

title: National anthem performance at inaugural Women’s Pro Baseball League game goes viral for all the wrong reasons
description: 85-year-old Motown singer Martha Reeves performed the ‘Star-Spangled Banner’ at the historic women’s baseball game
fullText:
The Women’s Pro Baseball League commenced its first season Saturday as the New York Heights took on the Los Angeles Queens at Robin Roberts Stadium in Springfield, Illinois.

It was a historic game — ending in a 10-8 victory for the Queens — marking the first women’s professional baseball league in the U.S. in almost three decades.

Before that, though, the league’s big debut was nearly upstaged by a national anthem performance that quickly went viral for all the wrong reasons.

Classic Motown singer Martha Reeves, 85, took to the mound to perform the “Star-Spangled Banner” alongside two other female singers.

Reeves was the lead singer of Martha and the Vandellas, who were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1995.

However, Reeves’ vocals appeared very shaky as she warbled through the anthem and struggled with the song’s famous high notes.

As Reeves sang, cameras panned to the audience, many of whom were smiling or visibly struggling not to laugh. Notably, one of the actual players was seen screwing up her face in order to contain herself.

“Absolutely nothing could have prepared me for the national anthem at the first Women’s Pro Baseball League tonight,” one person captioned a clip of the performance on X, which has racked up more than three million views and 3,500 comments.

“I admire her ability to pick a key and just ignore it,” one commenter joked.

“Fergie can rest now, these women hold the throne,” wrote another, referencing the Black Eyed Peas singer’s infamous national anthem rendition at the 2018 NBA All-Star Game.

“Unfortunately, as singers age, especially women, their vocal chords thin and become more brittle. It's a tough song to sing for the best of singers, but this was just an unfortunate moment for all involved,” wrote a third in Reeves’s defence.

Someone who may be relieved to see the rendition is Patti LaBelle, who — just two weeks ago — faced ridicule for her own national anthem performance at the MLB All-Star Game.

LaBelle, 82, appeared to miss some lyrics and take some creative liberties with parts of the song, which did not go down well with fans on social media.

“Patti LaBelle is one of our greatest singers, however why people think they have to add their own twist to the National Anthem boggles my mind. Leave it alone. It was not meant to be sung with runs or ‘making it your own,’” one person on X argued after the performance.

The “Star-Spangled Banner” has a reputation for producing awkward renditions due to its exceptionally wide vocal range, treacherous melodic leaps, and the fact that it is usually performed in massive, echoey stadiums or televised globally for major sporting events.

Roseanne Barr, who famously drew criticism for her 1990 rendition, called the anthem “the hardest in the world” to sing after Ingrid Andress’s widely criticized 2024 performance.

title: Everton With £30m Bid For 19 G/A Star: Worth The Bid From The Toffees?
description: Everton have taken their interest in Baris Alper Yilmaz to the next stage after lodging a formal €35 million (£30 million) offer for the Galatasaray forward, according to Turkish outlet Sabah, as r...
fullText:
Everton have taken their interest in Baris Alper Yilmaz to the next stage after lodging a formal €35 million (£30 million) offer for the Galatasaray forward, according to Turkish outlet Sabah, as relayed by Give Me Sport. The report adds that Everton officials have travelled to Istanbul, where talks with the Turkish champions are now under way as the club attempt to secure an agreement before interest intensifies.

Yilmaz has sat on Everton‘s radar for several transfer windows, though this marks their first serious push. Galatasaray, however, aren’t under pressure to sell. The winger remains a key figure after another excellent campaign that helped the club retain the Super Lig title.

His numbers explain the growing attention. Across the 2025/26 Super Lig season, the Türkiye international scored eight goals and supplied 11 assists in 30 appearances. He produced another goal and two assists in 12 Champions League matches, proving he could make an impact against elite opposition rather than relying on domestic form alone.

One issue still hangs over negotiations. Galatasaray reportedly want closer to €50 million (£43 million), while Yilmaz already has Champions League football waiting if he stays in Istanbul.

SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA – JUNE 19: Baris Alper Yilmaz #21 of Turkiye reacts after the 0-1 loss during the FIFA World Cup 2026 Group D match between Türkiye and Paraguay at San Francisco Bay Area Stadium on June 19, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Richard Heathcote/Getty Images)

This interest feels logical. David Moyes has rebuilt Everton around pace, strength and relentless work without the ball, and Yilmaz offers all three. His recorded top speed of 22.49mph would make him the quickest player in Everton’s squad, adding another direct runner capable of stretching compact defences.

Timing matters too. Iliman Ndiaye continues to attract attention from Manchester United and Al-Hilal, with Everton believed to value the Senegal international at around £70 million. Bringing in another explosive attacker before any major departure would leave the club in a far stronger position during the closing weeks of the window.

A transfer at this price still poses risk. Premier League football demands different qualities every week, and Yilmaz hasn’t faced that challenge before. His final pass can drift at times, although his Champions League displays against clubs including Liverpool and Juventus showed composure under serious pressure.

T4O’s opinion: Everton’s opening offer looks well judged. Waiting would likely invite fresh competition and strengthen Galatasaray’s hand, especially with other Premier League clubs monitoring the player. Spending around £30 million on a 26-year-old who delivered eight goals and 11 assists in last season’s Super Lig, while covering several attacking positions and even filling in at right-back, feels like a calculated piece of business rather than an expensive gamble. Matching the reported €50 million valuation would change that conversation completely.

title: Take a look at Florida alumnus Christian Scott's 2026 MLB season stats
description: Take a look at how former Florida Gators and current New York Mets has performed in his second season of major league action.
fullText:
Former Florida baseball standout Christian Scott has had a strong showing during his 2026 campaign with the New York Mets so far.

Originally drafted by the Mets in the 5th round of the 2021 MLB Draft with the 142nd overall pick, the right-handed pitcher's ascent into big league ball hit a major roadblock in 2024, when he underwent a hybridized surgery that combined a traditional Tommy John ligament replacement with a stabilizing internal brace that caused him to miss all of the 2025 campaign.

Prior to his injury, Scott threw 47 1/3 innings for New York, posting an 0-3 record with a 4.56 ERA, 4.60 FIP and 1.20 WHIP while striking out 39 against 12 walks issued across that stretch for 0.4 fWAR. He had been a breakout prospect for the franchise up to that point, rising from unranked on the team's 2023 top 30 prospects list to No. 5 heading into 2024.

So far in 2026, Scott has not only picked up where he left off, he has also made some significant strides in several categories, putting up a 3-3 record with a tidy 2.99 ERA along with a solid 3.47 FIP and 1.24 WHIP over 69 1/3 innings of work for an fWAR of 1.5. While his walks per nine have regressed from 2.3 to 3.9, the Coconut Creek, Florida, native's home runs per nine have improved from 1.5 to 0.9 and strikeouts per nine have lept from 7.4 to 11.0.

According to Statcast, Scott's overall pitching run value ranks in the 63rd percentile among major league pitchers, with his fastball run value checking in the 76th percentile. His breaking ball and offspeed run values rate below average, coming in at 48th and 36th, respectively.

Scott's primary weapon is his four-seam fastball, which he employs half the time and sits just a hair above the MLB average at 95.4 mph; he also offers a cut fastball (17%) and barely used sinker (2%). His two breaking balls are a sweeper (22%) and curveball (6%), while the splitter (4%) represents his only offspeed offering.

The former Gator excels in several of Statcast's categories, checking into the 89th percentile in strikeout rate as well as his extension. Other areas where he rates higher than the average hurler are hard-hit percentage (77th), average exit velocity (74th), expected batting average (73rd) and barrel percentage (72nd), while his chase percentage (27th), walk percentage (25th) and groundball percentage (11th) land on the lower end of the scale.

The 27-year-old righty dealt with an injury this summer that shelved him on the injured list for a stint — a hip impingement that caused him to miss some time from mid to late June. Since then, he has maintained his spot in the rotation, putting up a 2.83 ERA, 2.96 FIP and 1.08 WHIP with 38 strikeouts and 11 walks over 28 2/3 innings.

Despite Scott's success this season, the Mets have floundered to a 47-65 record, landing them in the basement of the National League West division despite having the second-largest payroll in all of baseball.

Over 116 2/3 innings stretching across 24 appearances — all starts — Scott has posted a 3.63 ERA, 3.93 FIP and 1.23 WHIP for New York, amassing a 3-6 record along the way. So far, he has averaged 9.57 strikeouts against 3.24 walks per nine innings, along with 1.16 home runs per nine, and has accumulated a total of 2.0 fWAR.

title: 😍 For Friendship Day: football’s coolest bromances
description: As Franz Beckenbauer once so aptly sang: "Good friends can never be parted, good friends are never alone." What applies in life naturally applies in football too.So, to mark Friendship Day on August 2...
fullText:
As Franz Beckenbauer once so aptly sang: "Good friends can never be parted, good friends are never alone." What applies in life naturally applies in football too.

So, to mark Friendship Day on August 2, we’re taking a look at the best bromances our favorite sport has produced!

"Poldi and Schweini" are definitely the prime example of close friendships in German professional football. Ever since the 2006 World Cup at the latest, the two superstars have won the hearts of fans everywhere.

It’s not just on the pitch that Lionel Messi and his perfect partner from Uruguay have outstanding chemistry. Off the field too, the two South Americans share a deep friendship. So it’s hardly surprising that they now both play for Inter Miami.

📸 Rich Storry - 2026 Getty Images

It feels like the two Roma legends spent their entire careers together. Both in the Giallorossi shirt and in Italy’s azure blue jersey, they celebrated great success. They were always on the same wavelength when it came to humor, too.

The same goes for Mario Götze and Marco Reus. The two technically gifted players know each other inside out from their time at BVB and with the German national team. And on a personal level, the vibe just fits.

📸 Lars Baron - 2018 Getty Images

Shared stops in their careers create strong bonds. That’s true of hardly any duo more than this Belgian pair. They always lined up side by side for the national team, Chelsea, and Real Madrid. But their friendship goes back even further.

Even among fellow coaches, sparks can fly. That’s especially true of the relationship between Jürgen Klopp and David Wagner. When the current Germany head coach got married in 2005, Wagner was right there by his side as best man.

📸 OLI SCARFF - AFP or licensors

"Ibra" and his Brazilian buddy played together at Ajax, Inter, Barcelona, and PSG. Rumor has it they even shared an apartment in the Netherlands.

What fun those two were! As unstoppable trophy collectors and jokers, the Brazilians enchanted world football in the late ’90s and early 2000s.

There are only 15 months between the Dutchmen in age. So it’s no wonder they get along so well. At a young age, they stunned almost the entire European elite with Ajax.

Guti and Raúl did that more or less throughout their entire careers. Especially with Real Madrid, the friends collected plenty of trophies. It was only with the Spanish national team that success came once both of them were already gone.

📸 Denis Doyle - 2005 Getty Images

Now it’s your turn: Which football bromances did we forget? Let us know in the comments!

title: Packers OT Zach Tom changing name to Zach Bako-Bewele
description: The player wearing No. 50 for the Green Bay Packers will have a new name on the back of their uniform for the 2026 season.
fullText:
The player wearing No. 50 for the Green Bay Packers will have a new name on the back of their uniform for the 2026 season.

Offensive lineman Zach Tom is changing his name to Zach Bako-Bewele, the new last name representing a combination of his grandparents' Nigerian names. Per Rob Demovsky of ESPN, Bako is the last name of his dad’s mom, while Bewele is the last name of his dad’s dad.

The name change is active on the team's website and in the Packers locker room.

Here is the reasoning, via Matt Schneidman of The Athletic:

Zach Tom is no longer Zach Tom. He legally changed his name to Zach Bako-Bewele, a combination of his grandparents’ Nigerian last names.

“Especially when I start having kids, I want to have a name that I can pass down where it represents where they came from, where I came from.” pic.twitter.com/JDPkjnvhtU

— Matt Schneidman (@mattschneidman) August 2, 2026

Bako-Bewele, a 2022 draft pick of the Packers, has a given name of Zachary Miskom Tom by parents Michael and Vanessa Tom.

During his first four seasons in Green Bay, Bako-Bewele became the full-time starter at right tackle, signed a $88 million contract extension and established himself as one of the game's best right tackles. He is coming off an injury-riddled 2025 season but arrived at training camp healthy.

title: Former Pittsburgh running back exploring college football return
description: A former Pittsburgh football running back is looking to return to college for a fifth season.
fullText:
There’s a chance that former Pittsburgh running back Desmond Reid returns for a fifth season of college football.

According to On3’s Pete Nakos, Reid is exploring a return to college football after Colorado Judge Charlotte Sweeney ordered the NCAA to declare eligible all class of 2022 athletes who finished their four seasons this past spring.

Reid spent the previous two seasons with Pittsburgh, finishing the 2025 campaign with 278 yards and two touchdowns. He was limited to seven games by multiple injuries. Reid ended his Pitt tenure with 1,244 rushing yards and seven touchdowns to go along with 896 receiving yards and six scores.

MORE: Former FSU quarterback Thomas Castellanos plans to explore a potential return to college football

The Buffalo Bills signed Reid after he went undrafted in the 2026 NFL Draft. Buffalo released him, though, after he suffered an undisclosed injury at one of the team’s spring practices.

Prior to Reid’s time with Pittsburgh, he spent two seasons with Western Carolina and had his best season with that program in 2023, compiling 897 rushing yards and 13 touchdowns. He also caught 21 passes for 283 yards during that season.

In four collegiate seasons, Reid racked up 2,965 rushing yards and 24 touchdowns, while hauling in 117 passes for 1,391 yards and seven touchdowns.

The 2026 college football season is set to start in four weeks, so it remains to be seen if Reid goes back for a fifth year. He was part of the 2022 recruiting class and was a three-star recruit, per 247Sports Composite rankings.

Pittsburgh will open the 2026 season against Miami (Ohio) on Sept. 5 at 12:30 p.m. ET.

title: Washington basketball among top contenders for five-star 2027 forward
description: The Washington Huskies are among the top contenders for one of the nation's top power forwards in the 2027 class.
fullText:
Danny Sprinkle and the Washington Huskies have established themselves among the top suitors for five-star power forward Ahmed Nur, one of the nation's top big men in the 2027 class.

He's set to take an official visit to Washington in September, and has also set trips to Ole Miss and Syracuse for October, after taking one to Purdue in June. However, the Orange weren't mentioned in a recent report from Rivals' Jamie Shaw, which could bode well for Washington's standing with the promising prospect.

Ahmed Nur has surged onto the national scene with a strong summer thus far winning MVP in NBPA And leading Power 5 in the 3SSB circuit in scoring with 15.3 PPG.

The 6-9 wing's blend of guard skills, length, fluidity makes him a potential NBA draft pick down the line and pushes… https://t.co/WLMg1hSHkr pic.twitter.com/aQpVuf0zEb

Nur was named MVP at the NBPA Top 100 Camp in South Carolina in June, where he averaged 14.8 points and 7 rebounds per game, while shooting 58 percent from behind the three-point line.

"The 6-foot-8 talented dual-forward was aggressive finding scoring opportunities, whether in transition or from beyond the arc," 247Sports' Brandon Jenkins wrote of his performance at the 3SSB Circuit, another stop on the summer tour for the nation's elite prospects.

"He is comfortable stepping into rhythm jumpers from deep and attacking the basket with purpose off the dribble. As he continues to add strength to his frame, his game has the potential to reach higher levels."

title: Australia dominate Commonwealth Games medal table
description: Australia dominate the 2026 Commonwealth Games medal table, winning 70 golds and 171 medals overall in Glasgow.
fullText:
After 10 days of action across 10 sports, a grand total of 215 gold medals have been handed out at Glasgow 2026.

Australia have dominated the medal table, winning 70 golds - 16 more than the combined total of England, hosts Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland put together - and 171 medals overall.

England finished second with 29 golds, ahead of Canada and India, while Scotland (13 golds) were fifth, Wales ninth (nine golds - four of them belonging to cyclist Emma Finucane) and Northern Ireland 12th (three golds).

In all, 45 nations or territories out of 74 won medals.

Australia won a staggering 37 gold medals and 76 in total in the swimming pool, with Meg Harris leading the way with six individual golds.

They also finished top of the athletics, track cycling and 3x3 basketball medal tables.

"We just really love the Commonwealth Games," said Sam Short, who won four swimming golds. "That and the Olympics is what Australia seems to live for.

"We've just been flogging ourselves in training all year. This is the target. We've got Pan Pacs (Pan Pacific Swimming Championships) in a couple of weeks but the general public in Australia don't really care about that, it's all Commonwealth Games.

"Representing the Green and Gold is a big honour."

Selfies, signatures & social media - how Kerr embraced Glasgow Games

South Africa swimmer Chad le Clos became the most successful athlete in the history of the Games when he won his 21st Commonwealth medal with bronze in the men's 4x100m medley relay.

The 34-year-old, who made his Games debut at Delhi 2010, moved one clear of fellow swimmer Emma McKeon of Australia.

"Looking back on the whole Commonwealth Games journey, from India through to now, I never thought I'd be standing here," Le Clos said.

"To stand alone in history is unbelievable."

Another record-breaker was 76-year-old Louise Hoskins who became the oldest Commonwealth Games gold medallist, winning the Para-bowls women's pairs title at the age of 76 years and 173 days.

Partnered by 44-year-old Serena Bonnell, Hoskins broke the record held by Scotland's George Miller, who was 75 when he won Para-bowls mixed pairs gold at Birmingham 2022.

"It just goes to show anyone can do it ," said Hoskins. "Young, old - bowls is for anyone."

Hoskins' gold was one of a record 141 Para-sport medals awarded in Glasgow.

title: Shiho Kuwaki rallies to win AIG Women's Open on second playoff hole
description: She beats Esther Henseleit, who had made a 40-foot birdie putt to force overtime.
fullText:
Shiho Kuwaki overcame a five-shot deficit and a competitor's miracle shot to win the 50th AIG Women's Open, the first LPGA major tournament victory of her career.

The 23-year-old from Japan won on the second playoff hole over Esther Henseleit, who had made a 40-foot birdie putt on the final hole of the fourth round to force overtime at Royal Lytham & St. Annes Golf Club in Lancashire, England.

Henseleit had a chance to win on the first playoff hole but missed a 15-footer for birdie on the 18th hole. On the second playoff hole, which also was played on the 18th, Henseleit hit an errant drive and made bogey, while Kuwaki got on the green in two shots and made two putts for par.

It's only the second time there's been a playoff at the AIG Women's Open since the tournament became a major in 2001.

What a moment! 

Esther Henseleit forces a play-off with this huge putt on 18.

 https://t.co/WmL2h6e9ZE pic.twitter.com/M5AooVmkSU

— AIG Women’s Open (@AIGWomensOpen) August 2, 2026

Yealimi Noh finished third as the latest leader to collapse in the tournament. She had entered the final round with a four-shot lead but suffered three bogeys in the first four holes. Noh lost the lead for good after bogeying the 12th while Kuwaki birdied the 13th.

"I will be taking away a lot more than I thought this week," Noh told Cara Banks on the NBC Sports broadcast. "It stings just being one short. But very happy with the week. I told myself no matter what happens, I’m just really happy to be in this position again."

We have a new leader!

Shiho Kuwaki birdies 13 and Yealimi Noh bogeys 12, meaning that Kuwaki has the solo lead.

 https://t.co/WmL2h6e9ZE pic.twitter.com/YCaDd61lF6

— AIG Women’s Open (@AIGWomensOpen) August 2, 2026

Kuwaki becam the sixth Japanese player in the past eight years to win an LPGA major tournament.

Her previous best finish in an LPGA major was a tie for 14th in the U.S. Women's Open this year. She had won two of her past four starts on the LPGA Tour by winning her first major tournament.

After bogeying the fifth hole, Kuwaki was five shots behind the lead, but she was steady with 11 pars and two birdies over the final 13 holes.

Nelly Korda (tied for fourth at 2-under) and Haeran Ryu (tied for sixth at 1-under) each came up short in their bids for a third major tournament victory this year.

Ryu had taken a one-shot lead over Kuwaki after the second round but shot 6-over over the final 36 holes.

title: Dolphins’ Jacob Rodriguez ‘has a magnet for the ball’; rookie LB packs a punch to force fumbles
description: MIAMI GARDENS — Former Chicago Bears cornerback Charles “Peanut” Tillman, who was known for forcing fumbles, had the “Peanut Punch.” Pretty soon, we’re going to have to start coming up with a nickname for Miami Dolphins rookie linebacker Jacob Rodriguez getting the ball out on unsuspecting ball carriers. Whether it’s the “Jacob Jab,” the “Rodriguez Rip” or take your pick at the best one you ...
fullText:
MIAMI GARDENS — Former Chicago Bears cornerback Charles “Peanut” Tillman, who was known for forcing fumbles, had the “Peanut Punch.”

Pretty soon, we’re going to have to start coming up with a nickname for Miami Dolphins rookie linebacker Jacob Rodriguez getting the ball out on unsuspecting ball carriers.

Whether it’s the “Jacob Jab,” the “Rodriguez Rip” or take your pick at the best one you can come up with, he has a propensity to force fumbles.

“It’s violent,” coach Jeff Hafley said ahead of Sunday’s fourth practice of Dolphins training camp. “He’s got a really good knack for getting the ball out. A lot of guys throw punches and miss and hit ribs and hit the back and hit shoulder pads and they’re trying to get the ball out. He’s got a really good feel and he’s got really good timing and very instinctual.”

That was one of his top traits in college, leading the NCAA with seven forced fumbles as an All-American linebacker at Texas Tech last season.

It has surfaced in practice with the Dolphins multiple times between offseason organized team activities, minicamp and four practices of training camp.

Hafley recalled Rodriguez dislodging the football once against star running back De’Von Achane. Second-year running back Ollie Gordon II has been victimized, too.

“He has a magnet for the ball. It’s actually great to watch,” Gordon said. “I think he got one from me, honestly. I feel like, on Sundays, we’ll have a bunch of possessions that come back to us because of things like that.”

For Rodriguez, it all happens within the flow of the game on any given snap.

Chris Perkins: These are the players to watch when Dolphins put on pads

Dolphins camp: Big-play passing game, led by QBs Malik Willis and Quinn Ewers; plus stock up, stock down

‘It becomes way more real’: Dolphins prepare to get physical when pads come on in camp

Here’s what we learned in Week 1 of Dolphins camp

Chris Perkins: Dolphins’ success in trenches depends largely on their draft-and-develop success

“Just trying to play the game the right way,” he said after Sunday’s session. “Football is a physical game, and it’s meant to be played that way. You have to be physical when you do it, whether attacking the ball carrier or the ball, specifically. It really doesn’t matter, as long as you do it violently, with the right technique and proper form.”

And it doesn’t surprise him that his college success has been translating early on as a professional on the practice field.

“I think it’s more so something that you work on, and now’s the time to work on it, in practice and OTAs,” Rodriguez said. “If I want to take chances in a game of taking the ball away, I want to put myself in all the different positions that I can be in a game.”

If Rodriguez ends up producing anywhere near as many forced fumbles as Tillman, who had 44 in his career, the Dolphins will surely welcome that over the next decade. Rodriguez actually got to pick Tillman’s brain once.

“We talked a little bit about how he does it,” Rodriguez said. “You always watch guys like (San Francisco 49ers linebacker) Fred (Warner) who play the game the right way and they punch on opportunity. It’s like anything else. You study it on film, and then you try to practice it and bring it to a real-life situation.”

It’s situational, too, when to decide to go for the punch-out, instead of just always doing it aimlessly.

“There are opportunities that you want to take advantage of if you can when you’re punching the ball out,” Rodriguez said. “if it’s third down, I don’t want to take a shot at the ball, because if we make the tackle, they’ll punt, we’ll get the ball back. So, you want to be smart with the opportunities you have.

“If you’re in the right position, you have the right leverage and you’re owning, then take a shot at the ball and do so getting the ball carrier down. Don’t just take a shot and let him run for 30 more.”

Under Hafley, the Dolphins have a period of practice each day where defenders drill forcing the football out and offensive players work on protecting the football.

“That being one of our main goals, to take the ball away on defense, I’m glad that we take a little bit of time to work on that, specifically,” said cornerback Chris Johnson, who had an interception of Quinn Ewers at Sunday’s practice.

Rodriguez will likely be a starter and leader for the Dolphins defense for years to come. In his rookie season, he’s pushing veteran middle linebacker Tyrel Dodson, a starter last season, for the job, and the defense may get both of them on the field in three-linebacker packages.

He’s had several different scenarios thrown at him in practice, like lining up across from Achane on the boundary in man coverage when the running back goes out wide, or coming through on an up-the-middle blitz.

“Just being able to get a good skill set of everything,” Rodriguez said. “We’ll be out on the boundary covering a back man to man, or we’ll be blitzing up the middle, blitz on the outside, we’ll be hook-dropping. It really doesn’t matter what we’re doing, but we’re doing a lot of it, so that way, we get as much work on everything as we can. … A lot of the stuff they tell us now is just try it. If you’re hesitant about doing something, do it.”

Johnson, as a fellow rookie, appreciates that Rodriguez, already exhibiting his leadership qualities that showed at Texas Tech, could call the defense without issue.

“He’s really calm within himself,” Johnson said, “and he understands what to do on the defense, give us the play call, help lead the defense.”

title: Haeran Ryu ready to 'rest in my bed' after bid for third-straight major falls short
description: Haeran Ryu didn’t win a third consecutive major at the AIG Women’s Open, but she left Royal Lytham and St Annes with a smile.
fullText:
Haeran Ryu didn’t win a third-consecutive major at the AIG Women’s Open, but she left Royal Lytham and St Annes with a smile.

“I think this week is pretty much (my best play) in the British Open,” she said Sunday, “so I'm so happy right now to be done.”

It was a long, exhausting weekend in England, one that finished with a tie for sixth in the season’s final major.

Ryu was looking to become the fifth player in LPGA history – the first since 2013 – to win three consecutive majors. She captured the KPMG Women’s PGA five weeks ago and followed that with a victory in the Amundi Evian Championship.

Ryu shot 5-under 66 Thursday morning and held the clubhouse lead before being passed later in the day by Jeeno Thitikul. A Friday 69 gave her a one-stroke lead entering the weekend and a great start Saturday buoyed thought of a runaway.

Ryu led by four shots after six holes in Round 3, before making five bogeys in an eight-hole stretch. She shot 3-over 74 to drop three back of 54-hole leader Yealimi Noh.

A birdie at the first Sunday offered some hope, but Ryu bogeyed the third and doubled the fifth (she played that par 3 in 4 over for the week). While no one was able to separate from the field, Ryu couldn’t make her own move. She shot another 74 to finish four out of the Esther Henseleit-Shiho Kuwaki playoff.

Though Ryu didn’t match fellow South Korean Inbee Park from 13 years ago, she did – as she mentioned – earn her top finish in this major. Her best result in three previous editions was a tie for 21st in her 2023 debut.

As for what’s next? The LPGA is off this coming week before resuming at the Standard Portland Classic. Ryu said she will likely play there but, “Next week, just off week, and then just go back to home and just rest in my bed.”

title: Who are Zyhir Hope, River Ryan and Brady Smith? What to know about prospects traded for Tarik Skubal
description: Here's the background on each of the three names heading to the Motor City in exchange for one of the best pitchers in all of baseball.
fullText:
Who are Zyhir Hope, River Ryan and Brady Smith? What to know about prospects traded for Tarik Skubal originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Late Saturday night, the MLB world learned that Tarik Skubal, one of the best pitchers in baseball, was heading west to join the reigning World Series champion Los Angeles Dodgers.

While a move always seemed possible given the Dodgers' recent success and their wealth of talent in the farm system, many MLB fans were still shocked that a deal actually came together. Now, Los Angeles' dynasty has somehow gotten even stronger and appears to be on a collision course with another World Series run.

Many fans want to know which players Detroit received in exchange for Skubal. While losing an ace is never ideal, the Tigers managed to land a significant haul for their former star.

Here's a look at the background of the three players heading to the Motor City in exchange for one of the best pitchers in all of baseball.

MORE: LIVE tracker for the MLB trade deadline

Hope is a 21-year-old center fielder who was the Dodgers' No. 5 prospect in their farm system, along with the No. 25-ranked prospect across the MLB, per MLB Pipeline. He will transfer over to join Detroit's Double-A affiliate, the Erie SeaWolves.

The Chesapeake, Va., native was originally selected by the Chicago Cubs in the 11th round (No. 236 overall) of the 2023 MLB Draft. In January 2024, Hope was part of the trade that sent current Cubs first baseman Michael Busch to Chicago.

While Busch has already established himself as a key contributor in the majors, Hope is now receiving increased attention early in his career after becoming a centerpiece of the return for Skubal.

Ryan is a 27-year-old right-handed pitcher who was the Dodgers' No. 7 prospect in their farm system, and No. 68-ranked across the MLB. He will join Detroit's Triple-A affiliate, the Toledo Mud Hens.

In 2021, Ryan was taken No. 340 overall in Round 11 by the San Diego Padres. He started his career as a versatile two-way player in college and was acquired by the Dodgers from the Padres in March 2022 in a trade for Matt Beatty. Just two seasons later, he made his MLB debut with four starts and had a 1.77 ERA in that big league stint. In August 2024, he fell victim to Tommy John surgery and missed the entirety of the 2025 season.

We will never forget River Ryan before his injury. 🙏 pic.twitter.com/ECLDiJNTt9

The final player sent to Detroit in the Skubal trade was Brady Smith. Like Hope, Smith is only 21 years old. He was ranked as the No. 17 prospect in the Dodgers' farm system and will join Detroit's High-A affiliate, the West Michigan Whitecaps.

Smith originally joined Los Angeles in the third round (No. 95 overall) of the 2023 MLB Draft. In Low-A this season with the Ontario Tower Buzzers, before earning a promotion to High-A, Smith went 0-6 with a 3.88 ERA, 104 strikeouts and 27 walks over 65 innings. He also recorded a career-high 11 strikeouts in June against the Visalia Rawhide, the Arizona Diamondbacks' affiliate.

According to MLB.com scouts, Smith's changeup has continued to develop throughout his career, while his fastball consistently sits in the mid-90s.

title: Grady Jarrett shares Bears' mindset going into 2026
description: Grady Jarrett explained the Chicago Bears have a mindset of being the hunters going into the 2026 season.
fullText:
The Chicago Bears were not expected to win the NFC North last season. Ben Johnson was in his first season as the head coach, and Chicago's 2024 season was not very promising. The Bears brought in a lot of new pieces going into 2025 to turn things around, including defensive tackle Grady Jarrett.

Jarrett is heading into his 12th season, having spent the first decade of his NFL career with the Atlanta Falcons and last season with the Bears. In his first year in Chicago, the two-time Pro-Bowler played in 14 regular season games and had eight quarterback hits.

His numbers have never been the best, but Jarrett brings an energy to the team that cannot be quantified. His mindset is contagious and he is going into this season as the hunter, hunting down every opponent.

“We’re always the hunters and that’s the mindset. Because it doesn’t really matter about what anybody else is doing,” Jarrett said. “It’s about how we’re going about our process and what we do.  We’re always the hunters.  That’s the mindset we’ve taken.”

While the Bears may have the mindset of being hunters, they are also the hunted. After winning the division last season, every team in the NFC North will be looking to take them down. The Minnesota Vikings may not be the most competitive given their quarterback situation, but the Detroit Lions and Green Bay Packers have rosters capable of winning the division.

Jarrett and the rest of the defense will be key to Chicago winning another division title. Turnovers helped carry the Bears defense last season, but they will need to be more consistent against the run and the pass to win back-to-back NFC North titles for the first time since the 2005 and 2006 seasons.
