title: Sri Lanka star recalls biggest Gautam Gambhir 'regret' from India's 2011 World Cup final, match-winning six by MS Dhoni
description: 15 years from that fateful day when India won the 2011 World Cup, one former Sri Lankan star remembers Dhoni's match-winning six and his regret for dropping Gautam Gambhir's catch.
fullText:
Sri Lanka star recalls biggest Gautam Gambhir 'regret' from India's 2011 World Cup final, match-winning six by MS Dhoni originally appeared on Cricket News. Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Former Sri Lanka pacer Nuwan Kulasekara still regrets dropping Gautam Gambhir in the 2011 World Cup final.

MS Dhoni's match-winning six off his bowling sealed India's title at the Wankhede.

Kulasekara later played under Dhoni at CSK and admired his calm nature.

Nuwan Kulasekara remains haunted by the defining moments of the 2011 World Cup final, a match in which he was on the wrong end of one of cricket's most iconic images. The former Sri Lanka pacer, now bowling coach of Lanka Premier League franchise Colombo Kaps, revisited the painful memories in a candid interview.

Speaking exclusively to RevSportz at the team hotel in Kandy, Kulasekara reflected on a night that ended in heartbreak for Sri Lanka. India chased down 275 at the Wankhede Stadium on April 2, 2011, with Gautam Gambhir's 97 laying the platform before Dhoni finished the job in emphatic fashion.

For Kulasekara, the defeat still stings, not least because of a costly moment in the field involving the man who would top-score for India. He was refreshingly honest about the part he played in a result that went the hosts' way.

MORE: Bhuvneshwar Kumar breaks silence on India comeback after R Ashwin backs him for World Cup

Kulasekara pinpointed a dropped chance as a moment he cannot forget. He said:

"Yes, at one stage we definitely believed we could win. I dropped an important catch off Gambhir, and naturally there is regret."

"But these moments happen in big matches. Ben Stokes experienced something similar in the 2016 T20 World Cup final before going on to play a match-winning role in England's 2019 World Cup triumph."

But Kulasekara hasn't let these moments sour his memories. He believes such is the nature of the sport. He also reflected on the six that sealed India's win, which he hit off his own bowling. Kulasekara said, "In cricket, especially during the powerplay and the death overs, such things can happen to any bowler."

He continued, "I tried my best to dismiss him, but he still hit me for a six. The positive memory is that we came back and won the 2014 T20 World Cup in a similar fashion. That is how this beautiful game works." Ironically, that wasn't the end of the dance between Dhoni and Kulasekara. The next time the two met, it was in franchise cricket.

MORE: Delhi Premier League 2026: Fixtures, scores & where to watch

Kulasekara ended up joining Chennai Super Kings and played under the very man (Dhoni) who had denied Sri Lanka a 2011 ODI World Cup title. What struck him most was Dhoni's refusal to dwell on that final.

"I joined Chennai Super Kings immediately after the World Cup, but Dhoni never spoke about that final. That shows the kind of person he is."

"He is incredibly calm and always focused on the present. For him, the past is over. His only concern was winning the next game. That is something I really admired about him," Kulasekara said.

Turning to the present, Kulasekara backed his countrymen to compete in the upcoming Test series against India, which begins in Galle on August 15. He said, "Playing at home in a World Test Championship series gives us the chance to show how competitive we are in Test cricket. I believe we can compete with them, especially because we are playing at home."

MORE: Arshdeep Singh apologises to Ashwin after placing India legend last in bowler rankings

There is something quietly moving about Kulasekara's willingness to own his part in that final rather than bury it. Fifteen years on, he neither hides from the dropped catch nor the six, framing both as the inevitable cruelties of elite sport, a maturity that speaks well of the man.

His admiration for Dhoni adds a further layer to the tale. The captain who inflicted the deepest wound on Sri Lankan cricket became a figure Kulasekara came to respect at close quarters, a reminder that the game's fiercest rivalries often soften into mutual regard once the contest is done.

title: Chelsea sign notorious World Cup star from sister club Strasbourg
description: Barco, who was involved in a viral heated exchange with Jude Bellingham after the World Cup semi-final, has moved to Stamford Bridge on a seven-year deal
fullText:
Chelsea have signed Argentina international Valentin Barco from sister club Strasbourg on a seven-year deal.

The 22-year-old, who played seven times for Brighton including six Premier League appearances during the 2023-24 season, becomes the seventh arrival of new manager Xabi Alonso’s reign.

A versatile player who can be used in central midfield as well as his regular position of left-back, Barco was in the Argentina squad that finished as runners-up at the World Cup, winning his fifth cap in the 3-1 group-stage win over Jordan.

He moved to Strasbourg initially on loan from Brighton in 2024 but signed permanently a year later having helped the club to qualify for the Conference League.

In all he made 53 appearances for the Ligue 1 side.

He was involved in a heated exchange with England’s Jude Bellingham immediately after his side’s 2-1 World Cup semi-final win in Atlanta, with Bellingham appearing to clip Barco around the head. An unused substitute, the Argentinian had earlier run onto the pitch to celebrate after Enzo Fernandez had equalised.

He is expected to join up shortly with his new team-mates on their tour of Australia and Hong Kong.

It continues a busy summer in the transfer market for Chelsea as they look to remodel under Alonso.

On Saturday they confirmed the signing of veteran striker Danny Welbeck from Brighton, following the signings of Crystal Palace’s Maxence Lacroix and Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa.

Marco Palestra, Emmanuel Emegha and Geovany Quenda have also been signed.

title: Sri Lanka complete white-ball double with six-wicket win to clinch women's T20I series
description: Sri Lanka secured a commanding six-wicket victory over Pakistan to clinch the T20I series. Pakistan's strong opening stand failed to produce a match-winning total of 175 runs. Captain Chamari Athapaththu then set the tone with an explosive counterattack for the hosts. The middle order continued the momentum, ensuring a comfortable chase with balls remaining. This victory marked Sri Lanka's fourth straight win against their Asian rivals.
fullText:
Pakistan's blazing start fails to translate into a match-winning total

Asked to bat first, Pakistan made a flying start courtesy of their opening pair, who took full advantage of the Powerplay. Shawaal Zulfiqar led the early charge, smashing five boundaries in a single over as the visitors raced to 63 without loss inside the first five overs.

However, Sri Lanka gradually wrestled back control after the explosive beginning. The scoring rate dipped through the middle overs before Pakistan lost opener Muneeba Ali at the halfway stage.

Chamodi Praboda then struck another crucial blow by dismissing the well-set Shawaal, ensuring Pakistan couldn't fully capitalise on their dominant start. Although Eyman Fatima provided a late boost with an unbeaten 30, the visitors finished on 175, a total that appeared below par considering their explosive opening stand.

Athapaththu sets the tone with explosive counterattack

Pakistan made the ideal start with the ball by removing centurion Imesha Dulani in just the second over. But the breakthrough only brought captain Chamari Athapaththu to the crease, and she immediately shifted the momentum in Sri Lanka's favour.

Athapaththu unleashed an attacking display, tearing into the Pakistan bowling attack with a flurry of boundaries. Her rapid 40 off just 14 deliveries ensured Sri Lanka raced to 51 runs inside four overs, erasing any early pressure from the chase.

Middle order finishes the job in style

Following Athapaththu's dismissal, Sanjana Kavindi seamlessly carried forward the momentum. She kept the scoreboard ticking with regular boundaries before taking apart spinner Nashra Sandhu with back-to-back sixes around the halfway mark of the innings.

Even after Kavindi departed, Sri Lanka never lost control. Harshitha Samarawickrama injected further urgency with a quickfire 24 off 11 balls, while Vishmi Gunaratne also made a useful contribution before being dismissed.

With the required rate well under control, Sri Lanka comfortably crossed the finish line in the 18th over, sealing the T20I series in emphatic fashion and completing another commanding performance against Pakistan.

title: Khabib: Usman Nurmagomedov will make free agency decision 'very soon'
description: Khabib Nurmagomedov says his cousin Usman won't have a drawn-out free agency process.
fullText:
It won't be long before Usman Nurmagomedov decides where his next fight will take place, according to his cousin and coach Khabib Nurmagomedov.

Usman (22-0) completed his PFL contract on Friday with a first-round knockout of Archie Colgan (13-1) at PFL New York to defend his lightweight title and show what a valuable asset he could be to any company that signs him.

Khabib was in the corner with his star pupil and celebrated with Usman following the spectacular finish. He clearly recognized the significance of the moment, and heaped praise on Usman in the aftermath of the fight.

Check out Khabib's complete reaction statement below, where he lays out a timeline of "very soon" for when Usman's future will be decided (via Instagram):

"Usman has shown and proven over the last couple of years that he is the best lightweight outside the UFC. Not with words, but with his performances.

When I said in 2020 that Islam (Makhachev) was the best at that time, there were many people who disagreed. Believe me guys, there are levels to this game.

You will see for yourselves what happens next. There will be negotiations over the next month, and very soon you will find out for yourselves which league he will continue competing in."

Usman, 28, said in the immediate aftermath of his PFL New York win that money will exceed legacy when dictating his next choice. There's much discussion about a potential UFC signing, with UFC CEO Dana White confirming interest following Saturday's UFC Fight Night 283 event Belgrade, Serbia.

title: Aston Villa have discussed signing Jack Grealish again
description: Aston Villa have discussed the idea of signing Jack Grealish again, according to the Sun. The Midlands club are preparing to sell Leon Bailey to Hull City and manager Unai Emery could do with a qualit...
fullText:
Aston Villa have discussed the idea of signing Jack Grealish again, according to the Sun. The Midlands club are preparing to sell Leon Bailey to Hull City and manager Unai Emery could do with a quality replacement. The Villa hero has now emerged as a target after his impressive stint at Everton last seasons. The Villans believe the England international attacker could offer much-needed depth in the wide areas as they prepare to impress in the Champions League next season.

Emery has also lost Morgan Rogers and Youri Tielemans to Chelsea and Manchester United, respectively. The Spaniard needs attacking reinforcements and the fans will be glad to have Grealish back. The Manchester City star played 20 games for Everton last season before injury struck in January. He scored twice and weighed in with six assists, creating 38 chances and completing 573 passes. Villa are not the only ones keeping tabs on the 30-year-old, with the Toffees also keen on signing him on loan again.

Atletico Madrid are also interested in the Englishman, while Al-Hilal, Al-Ahli and Neom want to lure him to the Saudi Pro League. Grealish spent eight seasons at Villa after 11 years as an academy player, and a return could appeal to him. He made 213 appearances for them, scoring 32 goals and bagging 43 assists. The attacker joined Man City for £100 million in the summer of 2021 but has struggled with injuries and form before rediscovering his form at Everton.

title: Royals at Rockies, August 2 live discussion
description: Is Tyler Tolbert the new face of the franchise?
fullText:
As the trade deadline finally shakes up the rosters around baseball, the Royals continue their battle for second-worst team in MLB after the Angels this afternoon. The reason this is a battle is because the Rockies won the first two games of this series and caught back up to KC. It’s that kind of season.

The Royals announced their player and pitcher of the month ahead of today’s game and, well, you’ve got to see this to believe it:

No disrespect to either of these guys. They both played well in the month of July and more than earned the honors. But I don’t think there was ever a point where it crossed my mind that either of them could ever win this award with KC until last night when the Royals’ broadcast pointed out that Tolbert was in line to do it. It absolutely drives home the point that the Royals’ roster has been just absolutely devastated by injuries that these two guys were in a position to succeed like this.

The Royals also announced a couple of roster moves before the game:

Say it with me, everyone: right forearm tightness is often a symptom of a UCL injury and the precursor to elbow surgery. Anyway, it’s fitting that a guy named Bummer will pitch for Kansas City as they barrel towards the final third of what seems to be not only a bad season, but one that likely tanks their chances to try to compete next year as they refuse to trade aging guys and see all of their younger pitchers suffering long-term injuries.

Speaking of aging veterans, Seth Lugo will pitch for KC today. We’re all very familiar with him and his kitchen-sink approach to pitching that he will hopefully soon pass on to Lucas Braun. Lugo still stands as an example of why the Royals shouldn’t be precious about keeping Wacha past tomorrow night’s deadline. That said, he’s pitched better of late. He has a 2.74 ERA over his past four starts. Albeit, he also has an 8.7% K-BB% and a 4.95 xERA. So. Ya know. Don’t hold your breath for him to keep doing it forever.

The Rockies will counter with one of their most accomplished starting pitchers in their franchise’s history, Kyle Freeland. Freeland, a lefty, also has a 7.34 ERA this year. He has a better SIERA than Lugo, but he plays with the Rockies who, beyond just playing in Colorado, seem to have suspect outfield defense if last night’s contest was any indication. So his ERA is that much worse. He hasn’t allowed fewer than four runs in any of his last four starts, five of his last six, and six of his last eight. It’s been a rough go for him. He throws six pitches, and none of them have been particularly effective. Maybe the Royals’ offense will finally go off in this one.

Isbel may be back with the team, but he’s not in the starting lineup, that’ll be John Rave in center. He’ll be batting sixth, just ahead of Royals Player of the Month Tyler Tolbert. Without Bobby Witt Jr. or Lane Thomas, Nick Loftin gets to bat second. If there’s any good news it’s that Witt is primed to return to the lineup on Tuesday when the Royals come come home.

The Royals have all three of their catchers somewhere in today’s lineup facing a left-handed pitcher. It’s safe to wonder if Starling Marte might have to leave in the middle of this game similarly to how Lane Thomas did yesterday, though we probably won’t care as much because if Lane Thomas could only get the return he got, Marte will be lucky to bring back a bag of balls.

fullText:
Patriots Rookie TE Eli Raridon Earns Praise Early in First Training Camp originally appeared on NESN. 

As the Patriots evaluate their roster early in training camp, rookie tight end Eli Raridon has emerged as one of the players who has stood out.

New England selected Raridon in the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft, hoping to add depth to a thin tight end room. In his first few months with the Patriots, Raridon has impressed with his ability to impact the game both as a receiver and blocker.

"New offense, new scheme, new NFL. Capable, willing learner," head coach Mike Vrabel said of Raridon. "We'll see when pads come on, things change. I think he's tried to play with the speed that we feel like he had, but maybe hasn't always shown."

Raridon will continue to get opportunities to work with the first- and second-team units, but his teammates have already noticed his talent level. Here's what Patriots players have said about Raridon.

So far, many Patriots have praised Raridon's performance in training camp as he acclimates to the NFL, a good sign for the team. Of most importance, Drake Maye seemingly is already developing chemistry with the rookie.

"He understands how to play both positions at the tight end spot, and I think he's making plays on the football," Maye said, via the Boston Herald. "That's what you want to see from a young guy, and he's putting the work in. That's the biggest thing with a young rookie. Raridon is sharing the tight end room with veteran Hunter Henry, giving the rookie a valuable mentor to lean on throughout his first NFL season. Henry has already noticed Raridon's growth and believes the young tight end continues to improve each day.

"Eli's doing a great job, man. He's taking the classroom to the field, learning a lot of things," Henry said. "You can see the game slowing down for him a little bit ... he's got a bright future ahead of him for sure."

fullText:
LYTHAM ST. ANNES, England (AP) — Shiho Kuwaki of Japan saved par to stay alive in a sudden-death playoff Sunday and won with a par on the second extra hole to claim the Women’s British Open over Esther Henseleit of Germany for her first major title.

Kuwaki closed with a 1-under 70 and looked like a winner in regulation until Henseleit holed a 40-foot birdie putt on the 18th hole at Royal Lytham & St. Annes for a 70 to join Kuwaki at 5-under 279.

Henseleit then had the advantage in the playoff when the 23-year-old from Japan was in deep grass short of a bunker and had to lay up short of the green. Kuwaki hit wedge to 3 feet to save par and got another chance when Henseleit missed a 15-foot birdie putt for the win.

title: Leeds United Are Back For £42.7m Winger: Should They Pay The Exact Price?
description: Leeds United have gone back into the market for Igor Paixao after losing the race for Julian Brandt, who chose Ajax instead. According to MOT Leeds News, quoting Foot Mercato journalist Santi Aouna, D...
fullText:
Leeds United have gone back into the market for Igor Paixao after losing the race for Julian Brandt, who chose Ajax instead. According to MOT Leeds News, quoting Foot Mercato journalist Santi Aouna, Daniel Farke’s side have already reopened talks with the Brazilian winger’s representatives as they continue their search for greater attacking quality.

Paixao stands third on Leeds’ shortlist of wide forwards. Even so, negotiations won’t be straightforward. Leeds United reportedly value the Marseille player at around £29.9 million, while owner Frank McCourt wants close to €50 million, or roughly £42.7 million, before approving any sale.

That gap presents an obvious obstacle. Leeds United are already pressing ahead with a £45 million move for goalkeeper James Trafford, leaving little room for another premium signing unless outgoing transfers generate fresh funds. Should Marseille refuse to soften their stance, Leeds are expected to shift attention towards cheaper names placed higher on their shortlist rather than forcing an expensive agreement.

ROTTERDAM, NETHERLANDS – FEBRUARY 15: Igor Paixao of Feyenoord celebrates after scoring his team’s first goal during the UEFA Europa League 2023/24 Knockout Round Play-offs First Leg match between Feyenoord and AS Roma at Feyenoord Stadium on February 15, 2024 in Rotterdam, Netherlands. (Photo by Dean Mouhtaropoulos/Getty Images)

Paixao’s output last season explains why Leeds have revived their interest. Across 42 appearances in all competitions during the 2025/26 campaign, the Brazilian collected 12 goals and seven assists. Ligue 1 accounted for six goals and five assists from 30 matches, while he added four goals in eight Champions League appearances against far stronger opposition.

Farke’s squad still lacks genuine width. Harry Wilson arrived without a transfer fee, yet Leeds need another winger capable of unsettling defenders every week. Noah Okafor offers quality, though the depth behind him looks thin after Facundo Buonanotte’s loan ended and Brandt slipped away. Paixao brings pace, directness and proven end product.

T4O believes Leeds should keep negotiating because Paixao answers a clear football problem. Paying Marseille’s full asking price, though, would be a mistake.

Reports have linked Marseille’s willingness to sell with ongoing financial pressure, giving Leeds United more leverage than the current figures suggest. There’s little sense in rushing into a €50 million deal when the French side may eventually need to compromise.

A fee between €32 million and €35 million feels far closer to the player’s current market value. Leeds United have already committed major money to strengthening their defence and are preparing another sizeable payment for Trafford. Overspending on one winger would squeeze flexibility across the rest of the squad. From T4O’s perspective, Paixao deserves serious interest, but smart recruitment means knowing exactly where the limit sits and refusing to cross it.

So far this season, he has a 2.70 ERA, 3.88 FIP, and 88 strikeouts in 93 1/3 innings pitched. He has had four consecutive starts allowing one run or fewer, with the last of those coming Monday against the Astros. In that start, he allowed just one run in six innings while striking out five.

title: Nanocodex: Building blocks for frontier OpenAI agents in Rust
description: Building blocks for frontier OpenAI agents in Rust. Nanocodex empowers you with Codex-level performance anywhere. - gakonst/nanocodex
fullText:
Building blocks for frontier OpenAI agents.

Install · Agent API ·
Thesis · Components ·
VM-backed tools · Documentation

Install the Nanocodex CLI on macOS or Linux:

Or add the Rust SDK to an application:

Switch the installed CLI between builds:

Downloaded builds are retained under ~/.nanocodex/versions. Running
nanocodex update 0.2.0 again switches to the cached binary without another
download. A stable launcher keeps nanocodex update available even while an
older binary is active, and ~/.nanocodex/current points to the selected
version.

PR artifacts require an authenticated gh CLI and an already completed
on-demand artifact workflow for that PR.

The first await accepts and orders the prompt. The second waits for its typed
TurnResult. Follow-on prompts automatically reuse the agent's retained
history, WebSocket, tools, shell sessions, and prompt-cache identity.
agent.clone() is a cheap handle to that same session; the independently
returned AgentEvents stream is the session-wide event firehose.

Nanocodex supports gpt-5.6-sol (the default) and gpt-5.6-luna. Select the
model with .model(Model::Luna) when creating an agent. The model is fixed for
that thread: switching later would invalidate the provider checkpoint and
require an inefficient replay of the complete retained context.

The non-TUI desktop example owns the default microphone and speaker directly
in Rust, using the same VoiceSessionBuilder as the production TUI:

The lower adapter leaves device and media ownership outside Nanocodex. It reads
24 kHz mono PCM16 little-endian audio from stdin, writes the same format to
stdout, and keeps transcripts and agent events on stderr:

Both retain one coding-agent session. A spoken request starts work while idle;
a follow-up received during that work atomically steers the active turn at its
next safe model boundary. Both use shared Codex/ChatGPT subscription auth, not
an API key. Set NANOCODEX_AUTH_FILE to override the normal Codex credential
path.

Agent infrastructure is easier to understand and reuse when each piece has a
sharp owner and a useful API of its own. An OpenAI client should work without
an agent loop. Tools should work without a CLI. The high-level agent should
compose those pieces rather than hide another implementation of them.

Nanocodex makes a small number of deliberate choices—Rust, Tower, typed
protocols, owned lifecycle state, and builder APIs—then keeps the boundaries
boring.

We do not try to outsmart behavior that frontier models and Codex already make
explicit. Context management, AGENTS.md, compaction, cache identity, tool
shapes, continuation, reconnect replay, cancellation, and process cleanup are
parts of the model-facing contract.

Nanocodex carries those invariants into a smaller, library-first API while
leaving application policy with the caller.

Representative cargo bench workloads, OpenTelemetry traces, differential
tests, and end-to-end evals keep the harness honest. The goal is simple: normal
agent turns should be model- and network-latency bound, with token usage and
estimated USD cost visible at the same typed boundary as the result.

The facade provides the canonical common imports. Each lower crate is also
designed to be useful directly, without importing the higher orchestration
layer.

The thin facade reexports the golden agent path at the crate root and keeps
detailed APIs under nanocodex::agent, nanocodex::oai, and
nanocodex::tools. Its prelude contains only the common types needed to build
an agent.

Facade guide ·
API documentation

The batteries-included lifecycle: an owned private driver, a cheap cloneable
Nanocodex handle, typed Turn and TurnResult values, and an optional event
stream. It owns prompt ordering, the tool loop, AGENTS.md discovery,
compaction timing, cancellation, snapshots, and branching through spawn,
fork, and fork_from.

Callers never pass previous messages, response IDs, or tool results back into
the agent.

Agent guide ·
API documentation

The complete OpenAI boundary: API-key and ChatGPT authentication, typed
Responses protocol values, a persistent WebSocket transport, client-owned
context, continuation and replay, automatic pricing, and a generic Tower
client.

Its standalone OpenAi -> Session -> ResponseTurn -> Response path provides a
managed conversation without taking on agent policy. Custom Tower layers and
services remain concrete and nameable—no boxing or global client is required.

OpenAI API guide ·
API documentation

The model-facing tool runtime: the Tool contract, heterogeneous Tools
registry, standard workspace tools, shell and process lifecycle, Code Mode,
deferred tool_search, remote dispatch, and MCP. MCP is always available on
native targets.

Applications can implement Tool directly or use the reexported #[tool]
macro. The separate nanocodex-tools-macros package exists only for Rust's
procedural-macro boundary.

Tools guide ·
API documentation

Application-owned tracing and OpenTelemetry setup for the data already flowing
through the agent. It provides structured lifecycle, model, tool, usage, cost,
cache, and latency telemetry without changing the core runtime path.

Enable the facade's observability feature or depend on the component
directly.

Observability guide ·
API documentation

Components whose public contracts are still maturing live under
crates/experimental/:

The CLI is a consumer of these crates. Voice and VM-backed tools remain thin,
opt-in adapters over the stable library contracts.

The CLI/TUI, Python package, Node/browser package, React bindings, and examples
are thin consumers of the same owned session API. They do not define a second
agent protocol.

Examples · JavaScript ·
Python · Web

Normal TUI and one-shot sessions keep host workspace tools by default. They can
instead route exec_command, write_stdin, apply_patch, and view_image
through one retained VM:

Directory roots may instead contain
/usr/local/bin/nanocodex-vm-guest. See the
VM guide for image preparation, lifecycle, egress, Linux
requirements, and macOS signing.

title: Arch Linux disables AUR package adoption to stop malware flood
description: The Arch Linux project has temporarily disabled adoption of Arch User Repository (AUR) packages after a surge in malicious takeovers of existing packages.
fullText:
The Arch Linux project has temporarily disabled adoption of Arch User Repository (AUR) packages after a surge in malicious takeovers of existing packages.

The decision was announced on the distribution's mailing list by contributor Robin Candau, who said that the situation is temporary until a solution is found.

“Due to the current influx of malicious package adoptions and follow-up commits made via the AUR, package adoption is currently disabled while we are handling the situation,” announced Candau.

“We will send a follow-up once we're able to. In the meantime, feel free to report suspicious adoption events or commits that haven't been dealt with yet, and stay vigilant!”

Independent Federated Intelligence Network (IFIN) conducted a technical analysis of the malware and reported that the campaign began on July 29 with the package ‘openconnect-sso.’

IFIN reports that the campaign bears many similarities to the last campaign, including the use of the Tor network for staging.

In June, a separate campaign hit AUR via more than 400 packages, distributing a Linux rootkit and info-stealer malware to unsuspecting users.

In the latest attack, the researchers identified a two-stage infection, with the first stage acting as the loader, and the second one being a Linux x86_64 payload described as stealer malware with remote administration (RAT) and SSH worm features.

Further analysis showed that the first-stage loader evades detection by checking for debuggers, sandboxes, virtual machines, and CI/CD environments before installing systemd services and cron jobs to ensure persistence.

It then downloads and launches a Tor client disguised as dbus-daemon to retrieve the second-stage payload from an ‘.onion’ server.

The second stage is a Rust-based infostealer that targets browser credentials, cryptocurrency wallets, password manager data, cloud and developer secrets, AI service API keys, SSH keys, and messaging platform tokens.

It also provides the attacker with remote command execution over an encrypted Tor channel and can spread laterally by using stolen SSH keys to copy and execute itself on other systems.

A Reddit user tracking the campaign alleges that it has expanded to over 200 AUR packages, either through compromised maintainer accounts or by adopting orphaned packages.

According to the same researcher, the campaign has spread to fairly popular AUR packages such as boringssl-git, icloudpd, windscribe-cli-v2-bin, stirling-pdf-desktop-bin, openconnect-sso, arduino-language-server-noclang-bin, and pgadmin4-server.

The compromised status of these packages has not been independently confirmed, and a list of all 200 AUR packages believed to be malicious has not been made available as of publication.
