description: Lucas Philips became a CEO at 26 and now finds himself getting up at 4:30 am to commute from Manhattan to Newark. He doesn't have a foosball table.
fullText:
Not all of the lessons in the Walker Deibel playbook fit between its covers. One of the first bolt-on acquisitions Lucas Philips tried to close was a tiny shop in rural Oregon — a guy who had spent decades fabricating custom interiors for Porsches. Philips flew to Portland, grabbed a brand-new convertible Mustang on a free upgrade from his shiny new Hertz President's Circle card, and spent three-and-a-half hours driving south through "the most beautiful" Oregon landscape toward the seller's property. The owner had originally quoted $40,000 for the operation. Two days later, after watching Philips pull up in a gleaming convertible and spend time on site, he decided the price should be more like $320,000.

What is entrepreneurship through acquisition and how does it work?

What are the key differences between SBA loans and search funds?

How did Philips grow Newark Auto's revenue after acquisition?

What challenges come with running a blue-collar manufacturing business?

"I regret that so much to this day," Philips said. "I should have just taken the Camry."

Lucas Philips grew up watching his father do something increasingly rare among his generation: own a small business outright and still make it home in time for school drop-offs and hockey practice. At 26, he decided to do the same — acquiring a niche manufacturer of custom automotive interiors in Newark, N.J. Now 29, Philips told Fortune that he's glad he did it, but "it's really not for the faint of heart."

Since acquiring Newark Auto, Philips has pushed annual revenue from "a little over a million" at purchase to more than $3 million this year, in roughly five years of operating time. He's done it with bolt-on acquisitions, long commutes, and a roster of hourly workers who have never seen the perks of startup life — Philips jokes about the proverbial ping-pong table in the office — but he's also learned that in the world of small business, the smallest details can derail a deal.

Like: don't rent a convertible when you're making a business trip to try to acquire a new subsidiary.

Philips traces his entrepreneurial drive to something older than Northwestern. His family immigrated to New York in the Ellis Island era a little over 100 years ago and, frankly, nobody wanted to hire them. He's from several generations of Jewish small business owners, so it was only natural for him to think this way, he said.

The list of businesses is somewhat endless. One grandfather sold paper goods — boxes, plastic wrap — to the Jewish bakeries of New York. His father sold sunglasses imported from China before anyone was importing anything from China, then hair accessories, then bought a high-end custom furniture business that now has a showroom in the B&B building on Madison Avenue and a factory in Christiansburg, Virginia.

title: New Mexico woman's bodycam confession about hiding newborn baby in hospital garbage tossed by state court
description: Body camera footage shows Alexee Trevizo confessing to hiding her newborn in a hospital trash can, but New Mexico's Supreme Court ruled it inadmissible.
fullText:
The New Mexico Supreme Court ruled that the body camera footage of a woman confessing to hiding her newborn baby in a hospital trash can in an attempt to conceal her pregnancy cannot be used by prosecutors in her murder case because of doctor-patient confidentiality.

Alexee Trevizo, who was 19 when she was arrested and charged with first-degree murder and tampering with evidence in 2023, was captured on police body camera admitting to hospital staff and her mother that she dumped the baby boy in the trash after workers reported the incident to authorities.

But the court ruled in a unanimous decision that all statements made in front of a police officer in the hospital room cannot be used at trial because her confession was protected under doctor-patient confidentiality, People reported. The state's high court also upheld the Fifth Judicial District Court's ruling that surveillance video showing Trevizo inside the hospital and any body camera footage captured by police were also not admissible in court.

Trevizo's doctor entered the room with two officers and informed the then-high school cheerleader and her mother that a dead newborn was found in the trash and had to be reported, the body camera footage shows.

New Mexico Woman Charged With Murder After Dead Newborn Found In Trashcan

"I'm sorry, it came out of me. I didn't know what to do," Trevizo was heard saying in the footage after a doctor told her the baby was found in the trash.

"I was scared," she continued, claiming that the child "was not crying or nothing."

After learning that a newborn had been found in the trash can, Trevizo's mother asked: "How big is the baby?" A nurse told her that the baby appeared to be full term, to which Trevizo responded that "nothing was crying."

Trevizo's mother then asked her: "Where did you put the baby at? Tell me the truth. You put it in the bag?" Trevizo confirmed that she did put the newborn in the trash bag.

Police had not read Trevizo her Miranda rights before making the confession, but prosecutors argued that she did not need to be Mirandized since she was speaking to hospital staff in front of officers and not directly to any police.

The young woman was also receiving medical treatment when officers entered the room with body cameras.

"Despite her unresolved medical crisis, Dr. [Heather] Vaskas, without authorization, ambushed Defendant, bringing with her two armed officers who stood in the doorway of her hospital room, and disclosed her personal medical information to all persons in the room without warning," the court said in an opinion written by Justice Michael E. Vigil.

Since Trevizo was "not given the opportunity to exclude anyone from the room before Dr. Vaskas discussed her condition in the presence of others" and in a "compromised medical condition," the justices said that they "cannot conclude that Defendant's waiver of her physician-patient privilege was voluntary."

Trevizo, now 22, arrived at Artesia General Hospital for severe back pain on Jan. 27, 2023, when hospital staff began running tests and giving her morphine for the pain as they waited for her results.

The teenager repeatedly denied to hospital staff that she was pregnant before running out of her hospital room and holding her backside on her way to the bathroom. Her mother followed her toward the bathroom and knocked several times on the locked door, waiting with hospital staff for around 20 minutes before the high school senior opened the door just as a nurse was about to unlock it.

After she opened the door, Trevizo was found cleaning up a heavy amount of blood on the floor. Hospital staff originally suspected the blood was from the woman attempting to terminate her pregnancy.

The bathroom had blood splattered on the wall, so hospital staff asked a janitor to clean it.

As the janitor was cleaning the bathroom, they noticed the trash felt heavier than expected and dug around until they discovered the newborn baby that was no longer breathing hidden inside. The janitor then told nurses of the discovery, and police were notified as required by law.

The New Mexico Office of the Medical Investigator later determined the newborn died by homicide, finding that the child died from entrapment after being placed and tied inside a plastic trash bag beneath bloody paper towels and other garbage. The autopsy report also said the child had air in his lungs and that there was evidence of a hemorrhage consistent with hypoxia.

Despite these findings, Trevizo has maintained that the baby was stillborn. She has also continued to claim that she did not realize she was pregnant until she gave birth to her child in the hospital bathroom.

New Mexico Teen Accused Of Killing Newborn Faces 'Nonsense' Petition To Ban Her From College: Lawyer

The district attorney's office filed charges against Trevizo based on the conversation captured on body camera footage as well as video taken from hospital security cameras that showed her in the hospital hallway entering and later leaving the bathroom. But that evidence is now inadmissible.

After her arrest on May 10, 2023, Trevizo was released from jail and allowed to finish her senior year of high school without an ankle monitor or house arrest while waiting for trial.

Trevizo attended prom and had planned to walk at her high school graduation while awaiting trial, but the school asked her not to attend.

She then attended New Mexico State University, where students launched a petition that received more than 30,000 signatures demanding she be banned from campus.

Original article

title: SNAP recipients, some middle-class families get $60 monthly for produce in new bill. Who qualifies?
description: The "Fresh Bucks for Fresh Produce" Act would establish a pilot program that awards grants to states so they can give the extra grocery money to lower-income and moderate-income people.
fullText:
(NEXSTAR) – Some families could start getting $60 a month in extra food assistance, a new bill introduced in July proposes.

The "Fresh Bucks for Fresh Produce" Act would establish a pilot program that awards grants to states so they can give the extra grocery money to lower-income and moderate-income people. To qualify for increased benefits, households would need to earn 80% or less than the median income of their area.

SNAP recipients would qualify for an added monthly benefit, but those who don't receive SNAP money could also apply.

Eligible households would then get an additional $60 on top of their usual monthly SNAP benefits loaded onto their EBT cards, or a new EBT card if they aren't receiving food assistance already.

The $60 would need to be spent on fruit or vegetables, which can be fresh, frozen or dried.

The bill proposes establishing a new grant program that would give certain states the extra funding to establish the pilot program. States would have to apply for the extra funding, and preference will be given to states that "prioritize food insecure communities," the bill says.

If your state were to participate in the pilot program, then your household would be eligible to receive the extra $60 per month if you earn less than 80% of the area's median income.

That income cap would vary greatly from place to place, from around $63,000 in Bismarck, North Dakota, to something like $113,000 in San Francisco, California. The exact income limits would be determined by the Departments of Agriculture and Housing and Urban Development.

The legislation was inspired by a pilot program in Seattle, which led to higher food security and participants having better access to produce, according to Rep. Pramila Jayapal (D-Wash.), who introduced the bill in Congress.

The bill has quite a few hurdles to overcome before it becomes law. It was referred to the House Committee on Agriculture after being introduced on July 2. Members of that committee now have the opportunity to review the bill and make changes before potentially introducing it to the whole House for a vote. Then it would be up to the Senate to pass it and the president to sign it.

Rep. Jayapal urged Congress to take swift action. "We must pass this legislation to expand the program nationwide and get families in every corner of the country healthy produce they can afford."

An estimated 37 million Americans receive benefits under SNAP, previously called the Food Stamp Program. Recent changes have cut the number of people who qualify for food assistance, and more cuts could be on the way.

title: Ukrainian drones kill eight in Russia and strike Wildberries warehouse, governors say
description: Aug 2 () - Ukrainian drone strikes killed at least eight people in Russian regions overnight and on Sunday, hitting targets including a warehouse belonging to Wildberries, Russia's largest online reta...
fullText:
Aug 2 (Reuters) - Ukrainian drone strikes killed at least eight people in Russian regions overnight and on Sunday, hitting targets including a warehouse belonging to Wildberries, Russia's largest online retailer, ‌regional officials said.

Russia's Defence Ministry said it had downed 635 Ukrainian drones during the night.

Kyiv's ‌drones attacked a Wildberries warehouse in the Samara region, around 800 km (500 miles) from Ukraine's most advanced military positions, Samara Governor ​Vyacheslav Fedorishchev said. He said there were no casualties and that a fire that had broken out as a result of the attack was being put out.

Ukrainian forces have been hitting deeper inside Russia as they expand strikes on economic and energy targets, aiming to undermine Moscow's ability to wage its more than four-year-old war in ‌Ukraine.

They have attacked about a dozen ⁠Wildberries sites since July 18 in an attempt to disrupt the operations of the company, a linchpin of the consumer economy often described as Russia's version of ⁠Amazon.

A strike on a residential building in the neighbouring Saratov region killed two people in the city of Engels, Governor Roman Busargin said. Civil infrastructure was damaged both in Engels and in the city of Saratov, he said.

Both ​Saratov city, ​which hosts a major oil refinery, and Engels, home ​of a military airbase, have come under ‌repeated Ukrainian attack in recent years.

Kyiv's military said on Sunday that Ukrainian forces had attacked the Saratov refinery and the Engels airbase, sparking fires at both facilities. It said its forces had also struck an oil depot in the western Kaluga region.

Three people were killed and two injured in a drone attack on the Udmurtia region of Russia, acting governor Olga Abramova said. In the border region of Belgorod, three people ‌were killed and five injured in Ukrainian strikes, the local ​task force reported.

The governor of Russia's Bashkortostan region, Radiy Khabirov, ​said air defence units had repelled a ​massive drone attack on industrial facilities. One of the drones was shot down over ‌the industrial area of the regional capital of ​Ufa and a fire ​was being put out, he said.

Russia's Defence Ministry said its forces had struck infrastructure and two vessels with military cargo in the Ukrainian port of Mykolaiv, as well as a vessel carrying ​military supplies in the Black Sea.

In ‌the southeastern Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia, regional governor Ivan Fedorov said Russian-launched glide bombs killed ​one person and injured 21.

title: Body of famed international climber Nirmal Purja and 3 more found after Pakistan avalanche
description: The remains of renowned British-Nepali climber Nirmal Purja and three other climbers have been found by a ground team on Broad Peak, one of the world’s highest mountains, where a 10-member internation...
fullText:
ISLAMABAD (AP) — The remains of renowned British-Nepali climber Nirmal Purja and three other climbers have been found by a ground team on Broad Peak, one of the world's highest mountains, where a 10-member international expedition was swept away by an avalanche, officials said Sunday.

The Alpine Club of Pakistan identified the recovered climbers as Purja, Wang Zhong, Nima Sherpa and Kili Pemba Sherpa. The club praised military and civilian rescuers and volunteers involved in the recovery effort.

On Friday, rescuers located four other bodies but were able to recover only three — Omani Nathira Ahmed, American Mallory Geis and Nepalese Bahadur Gurung — because harsh weather grounded search-and-rescue helicopters.

Military-backed rescue teams resumed the search Sunday for the two remaining climbers, while efforts continued to bring down the bodies of Purja and the three others found by the ground team, local officials said.

On Saturday, Purja's expedition company said the world had lost one of mountaineering's greats. The company described him as "a leader who inspired millions through his courage, humility and unwavering belief that human potential is far greater than we often imagine."

Alpine Club of Pakistan President Irfan Arshad Khan said the tragedy was "an immeasurable loss to the global mountaineering fraternity." He paid tribute to military and civilian rescuers and Sherpas who took part in the search mission.

The expedition was led by Purja, the Nepal-born former British Army soldier widely known as Nims Dai.

He climbed the world's 14 highest peaks in a record 189 days in 2019, an achievement featured in the Netflix documentary "14 Peaks: Nothing Is Impossible." His record was broken in 2023.

A statement from Geis' family said, "Mallory was a bright light who was loved deeply by her family and friends. She will be profoundly missed."

The expedition was expected to be the last one for Pakistani guide Sohail Sakhi, who worked with Moving Mountains, a Pakistan-based adventure travel company. Sakhi also was a geographer and high-altitude photographer who had climbed some of the world's major peaks, according to the company's website. His body remained missing on Sunday.

Accidents are common on climbing expeditions in northern Pakistan because of avalanches, falling ice and rock, extreme altitude and rapidly changing weather.

Riaz Khan reported from Peshawar, Pakistan.

title: A school shooter’s mother helped him reach his ‘fans’ from prison. Here’s why she wasn’t charged.
description: Georgia school shooter Colt Gray was sentenced to life in prison and his father to 15 years for providing the gun. Some victims and their families wish his mother would be charged, too.
fullText:
For two days, she had mostly held her tongue as one witness after another laid out the horror of the Apalachee High School shooting in Winder, Georgia, in excruciating detail. But as the topic turned to the relationship school shooter Colt Gray had with his mother Marcee – the allegations of abuse and neglect and her chummy jail conversations with him after the shooting – Breanna Schermerhorn could no longer stay silent.

"She should be in jail now," she said quietly but firmly to family members seated next to her in the second row of the court gallery.

The statement from the mother of Mason Schermerhorn, one of the four people shot to death by Colt Gray in school on September 4, 2024, is one that had been raised before, when Colt's father, Colin Gray, was charged with second-degree murder in his own landmark case after buying his son the AR-15-style rifle used in the shooting.

Barrow County District Attorney Brad Smith said at the time they had considered charges against Marcee Gray, but couldn't tie her criminally to the killings.

"At the end of the day, she did not have custody of Colt, she did not have proximity to Colt, and she was not the one that provided him the firearms," he said in March.

After Colt Gray received sentences Tuesday totaling life without parole plus 20 years, Smith reiterated he will not be bringing criminal charges against his mother, Marcee Gray. Colt's father, Colin Gray, was sentenced to 15 years in prison two days later, as his lawyer announced plans to appeal.

"She took some steps – not many – but some steps to actually have the firearms removed, or ask the father to do that," Smith said Tuesday. "So we don't believe we have the ability under the proximate cause (law) of Georgia to charge her with what happened at Apalachee."

Allegations of drug abuse and child neglect against Marcee Gray were already well established by the time her son Colt entered guilty pleas on 55 counts. Those allegations had resulted in her losing custody of her children long before the shooting.

But prosecutors spent nearly an hour in court last week playing recordings that had never been heard before publicly – jailhouse calls between Colt and Marcee spanning months, where they chatted casually about mass killers and his online reputation, statements that drew groans and widened eyes from victims' family members who were watching.

"I'm printing out, like, all of these pictures, because seriously, they are extremely cute," Marcee Gray told Colt, referring to drawings posted online to what prosecutors called the True Crime Community, illustrations that pictured him alongside other mass shooters.

As Colt encouraged her to bring him copies of certain pictures and comments he found interesting, Marcee Gray appeared to recognize some of them could cause concern to screeners at the youth detention center where Colt was housed.

"Just looking for any other ones that would not set off the alarm bells," she said.

Colt Gray's jail counselor, Stephen Baker, later confirmed their juvenile inmates are not allowed to have photos of school shooters.

"If a person in your facility was trying to get around that and pick particular photos that wouldn't be as noticeable, would that be trying to skirt the rules?" Smith asked in court.

"It would be," Baker responded.

In another conversation, Marcee Gray brought up an online drawing showing Colt alongside the Columbine shooters and Parkland gunman Nikolas Cruz in the style of a Weezer album cover.

"It's really awesome!" she said.

"Oh, wow, I need that printed out and brung up here," Colt said.

In text messages to CNN, Marcee Gray, who did not attend Colt's hearing, said she didn't understand at first the nature of the Reddit and Discord sites her son wanted her to check and said she only wanted to keep him from shutting her out.

"My tone and enunciation during many of these calls could be described as enthusiastic, encouraging, and animated. It should go without saying that in an even semi-normal parent-child relationship, I would immediately address the extreme inappropriateness of the subject, as well as having him speak to a mental health professional about his extreme interest in mass shootings," she wrote Tuesday. "This situation was as far from normal as humanly possible. I was simply doing whatever I could to keep the line of communication open and keep my son alive. I am beyond remorseful for the pain I caused everyone through my actions and will spend the rest of my life in heartbreaking regret for so, so many things."

When the Department of Juvenile Justice caught on to what Marcee and Colt were discussing and sharing, they cut off their communication, Baker said, and the state eventually terminated her parental rights and placed Colt in foster care while he was in custody.

Marcee Gray told CNN everything she brought to the detention center went through screening.

Even if prosecutors could connect a charge to Marcee Gray's behavior in her calls and visits, they would not be able to tie her to the shooting, said John Acevedo, professor of practice and associate dean at the Emory University School of Law in Atlanta.

"Beforehand, you can be charged with encouraging someone to commit the crime or with aiding them, but she made these comments well after he was in prison," said Acevedo. "They're definitely distasteful, but not criminal."

Marcee Gray already has a criminal record in Barrow County. She pleaded guilty less than a year before the school shooting to trespassing at Colin Gray's home during a period of estrangement and damaging his work truck. She was ordered to stay out of Barrow County as a condition of her probation prior to the shooting.

Colt Gray's defense asked the judge for mercy in sentencing, saying he had a terrible childhood, which prosecutors and even some victims acknowledged in court.

"I know he's had a bad upbringing, but … in this courtroom, we've seen a lot worse," Smith said.

Georgia's Division of Family and Children Services found 12 categories of abuse and neglect of the Gray children connected to Marcee, including inadequate food, shelter and medical care, director Candice Broce said in court. They could find no evidence Colt had ever received been seen by a doctor except for an eye exam.

"I was really surprised by, like, the complete absence of care," said Broce.

What they found instead were signs Colt had been hurt.

"I found enough evidence that she was physically abusing him," Broce said, including a slapping incident that resulted in a swollen lip.

Marcee Gray acknowledged the slap but told CNN it was nothing criminal.

"A slap of a disrespectful teenager who was bigger than I was at the time is a far cry from long-term abuse and neglect," she wrote via text message. "I was never abusive to any of my children. Ever."

Although the investigation by the Division of Families and Children – which is technically still open – could provide evidence of criminal abuse, Smith made clear he does not intend to file charges because it would require the boy who killed four people to be portrayed as the victim.

"He might even have to call Colt in a trial to testify against his mother," said Acevedo. "I don't think that's what the (victims') families are looking for."

The district attorney who put the killer behind bars for the rest of his life and won an unprecedented murder conviction against his father, agreed. Even though Marcee Gray's freedom is unsatisfying to many people hurt by her son's actions, that's one case he has no interest in taking to court.

"I don't know that I have the stomach for a trial where Colt Gray is the victim," Smith said.

CNN's Eric Levenson contributed to this report.

title: Gang of men hurl racist abuse at takeaway owner before violent attack
description: The BBC understands police are treating the attack in Falkirk last month as a hate crime.
fullText:
A business owner has said that a group of men hurled racist abuse at him before punching him and smashing his head into a wall in the street in Falkirk.

Dr Zohaib Arshad said the group approached him on Grahams Road last month when he was visiting one of his takeaway shops and asked him when he was "leaving the country" before launching the unprovoked attack.

The 39-year-old, who practised as a vet in Pakistan, patched himself up with glue stitches rather than wait at A&E. He said his children are now fearful of being attacked in school.

BBC Scotland understands the police are treating the incident as a hate crime.

A spokesperson for the force said inquiries into the attack are ongoing.

Arshad stood as an Alba Party candidate for Falkirk at the 2024 General Election and is now a member of the SNP.

His political connections have resulted in the issue being brought to the attention of the Scottish Parliament - however he fears it would have gone unnoticed had he been any other member of the public.

More stories from Tayside and Central

Listen to news from Tayside and Central on BBC Sounds

Arshad said he had just parked his car and was walking to one of his shops on the evening of Monday 20 July.

He said: "Two or three guys approached me and said 'when are you leaving the country by the way?'"

The businessman said he tried to walk away but one of the group banged his head into the wall.

"I had blood all over my face and in my eyes and when I was cleaning up the blood from my eyes one of the guys punched me on my head a few times," he said.

He told how he then ended up in a fight with one of the men as he tried to defend himself, and that the man threatened to stab him.

Despite there being lots of people around, he said nobody came to his assistance.

"Everybody got their phone at that time instead of helping me or helping that guy to take the situation out. Everybody was just filming us," he said.

The 39-year-old said that after calling the police it took 45 minutes for officers to arrive, by which time the men had left the scene.

When Arshad called for an ambulance, he claims he was told to make his own way to A&E.

"I called A&E and A&E said oh it's 14 hours to get the stitches," he said.

He feared that leaving the wound untreated for that long would leave him with a worse scar, so called some of his friends who work in medicine to see if they had "glue stitches at home" and stitched the wound up in "the back of the shop".

Following the attack, Arshad said his family are "terrified" and he is being "much more vigilant".

"My wee boy, he's nine and said 'dad, if I go to school, can they do it to me as well?'"

He added that despite his wife and his mother urging him to move to France where he lived previously, he has no plans to leave Scotland.

"We cannot leave anything just because of one bad person - defeat is not an option," he said.

It comes at a time of heightened tension over the issue of immigration in Scotland.

Police made several arrests in the opening weekend of the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow after masked demonstrators rampaged through the city and targeted people for the colour of their skin.

Earlier in the day a peaceful anti-racism protest had been taking place at Glasgow Green before anti-immigration protesters arrived at the same location - police estimated 1,700 people had attended.

Later that day a group marching through the city shouted racist abuse and hurled a traffic cone at a delivery driver who was picking up an order.

A video of the attack on Muhammad Jawad Yaqoob circulated on social media - it shows a number of young men shouting "get them out" before one throws the orange cone. They cheer as Yaquoob runs away from them into a nearby restaurant.

Police Scotland said it was investigating the incident.

title: Raising Cane's to open 7 new restaurants. See locations
description: The company plans to open seven restaurants including two in new markets.
fullText:
August marks 30 years of Raising Cane's Chicken Fingers and this year, the company is welcoming the milestone with seven new store openings and some reopenings.

The company plans to open seven new restaurants, including two new markets in eastern North Carolina and southeastern Georgia. There are also plans to reopen four remodeled locations as well, according to a statement the chain sent to USA TODAY.

The restaurant said it is focusing on growth.

The chicken finger chain opened locations on June 16 in Pensacola, Florida and on July 21 in Albany, Georgia, reported the Pensacola News Journal and the Augusta Chronicle, both part of the USA TODAY Network. At the Albany, Georgia opening, the company did a "Lucky 20" drawing where 20 customers won free food for a year.

The company opened its very first location on August 28, 1996, according to the Raising Cane's website. They are known for its chicken fingers and Cane's Sauce, which the company describes as "thick and tangy" and made with multiple spices.

"August is a meaningful month for Raising Cane's as we celebrate our 30th birthday and reflect on how far we've come since opening our first Restaurant in 1996," the company said in a statement. "From opening in new markets like Rocky Mount and Statesboro to welcoming customers back to newly remodeled Restaurants, every opening in August and beyond represents our continued commitment."

title: 'A huge success' - Wales win 31 medals at Glasgow Games
description: Wales' 2026 Commonwealth Games campaign labelled a success after they won 31 medals in Glasgow, with nine gold, 10 silver and 12 bronze medals.
fullText:
Wales' 2026 Commonwealth Games campaign has been labelled a success after they won 31 medals in Glasgow, with nine gold, 10 silver and 12 bronze.

Emma Finucane won the last of her four golds in the Sir Chris Hoy Velodrome on the final day to bring the Team Wales medal haul to a conclusion as they finished ninth in the medal table.

Wales' most successful Games were on the Gold Coast in 2018 when they brought home 36 medals - 10 gold, 12 silver and 14 bronze.

The streamlined Glasgow event meant there were fewer sports and medals to win.

The 2026 medals include 11 in cycling, six in swimming, five in athletics, four in boxing, three in artistic gymnastics and one each in bowls and weightlifting.

Team Wales roll of honour at Commonwealth Games

In Birmingham in 2022, Wales claimed 28 and were eight in the medal table.

Four years on, chef de mission Gethin Jones labelled it a success.

"I'm a bit of a stats man," said Jones. "If you look at it as a percentage compared to Birmingham, we should be winning about 75% of the medals we won there.

"We're closer to more than 100%, so people will quite rightly see it as a huge success.

"Despite the medals - and a lot of people will always judge success by them - the culture and spirit within the team has been incredible.

"If you get that right, set that platform and environment, it gives our athletes the opportunity to be at their very best when they need to be.

"They've taken that opportunity with both hands.

"I'm incredibly proud of all our medallists. They've been amazing. It's brilliant."

Olympic cycling champion Finucane has been the standout star with a record four gold medals in one Commonwealth Games.

"At the end of every year, my mates and I get together for a pint and go through the year's sporting moments because we're sports geeks," said Jones.

"You always end up having that conversation about the best ever.

"Emma is absolutely going to be in that conversation as one of Wales' greatest ever athletes, alongside Anna [Morris] and a few others.

"She's dominated the headlines here in Glasgow, and I'm absolutely delighted for her.

"She's such a nice person and such a team player, and that adds so much to the success she's having.

"With all the gold medals that have come her way, she's still so down to earth, still puts the team first and always appreciates the people around her.

"She's not only a world-class athlete, she's also a brilliant ambassador for Wales."

Jones said any perceived Commonwealth Games success does not halt the challenges that sport faces in Wales.

He said: "Some sports in Wales have struggled this year, and I don't want people to go away thinking, 'they've won loads of medals - everything's fine'.

"These sports still need support. They need investment and backing of businesses that want to get involved.

"Hopefully, those who've watched the Games, whether here in Glasgow or on television over the last week, will see what this team is capable of and think they can help.

"Then we can have even more moments like this. Look how everyone feels when we win here, it's amazing.

"If we want more of that, we need everyone to get behind Team Wales over the next four years."

title: Why the Commonwealth Games are important to NI athletes
description:
The slimmed down version of the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow are over and Northern Ireland athletes will return home with 16 medals.
It's the second biggest haul in history, behind only the 18 won in Birmingham four years ago but this time with fewer sports.
But why are the Commonwealth Games so important to athletes from Northern Ireland, especially in the bigger sporting picture?
fullText:
The slimmed-down version of the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow is over and Northern Ireland athletes will return home with 16 medals.

It's the second-biggest haul in history, behind only the 18 won in Birmingham four years ago but this time with fewer sports.

The build-up to the 2026 Games had been dominated by a change of host, a scaled-down schedule and a number of big-name withdrawals.

Yet, after 10 days of competition in Scotland, the performances leave the lasting impression.

But why are the Commonwealth Games so important to athletes from Northern Ireland, especially in the bigger sporting picture?

McKeown and Kelly win men's pairs gold after tiebreak

From Love Island to Commonwealth gold for McConnell

Milestone moment for O'Connor with Glasgow gold

The Commonwealth Games fall at the halfway point of the Olympic cycle and, in the case of Glasgow, just months before qualification in many sports gets underway for Los Angeles 2028.

It's an opportunity to take stock of where you are as an athlete moving forward, or for young athletes to gain a first experience of a multi-sport event.

The Commonwealth Games have always been an important bridge to greater things.

Lady Mary Peters won Commonwealth medals before the Olympic pentathlon title in 1972, while boxers Wayne McCullough and Aidan Walsh also became Commonwealth medallists before they stood on an Olympic podium.

More recently, Rhys McClenaghan's first major title on the pommel horse was a Commonwealth gold in 2018. Meanwhile, four years ago swimmer Daniel Wiffen won a silver medal at the Commonwealths.

Both men are now Olympic and world champions.

Northern Ireland's golden girl in Glasgow, Kate O'Connor, was a silver medallist from four years ago and went on to finish second at the World Championships in-between Games.

This was her third Commonwealths having competed as a 17-year-old in the Gold Coast in 2018, and she says the competition "has been so good to me".

"Having that opportunity whenever I was a 17-year-old to travel across the world and compete against senior athletes on an international stage, and compete against that many people, not many 17-year-olds get that experience," O'Connor told BBC Sport NI.

"Then in 2022 and I was in with a chance of a medal, I'd had that experience from the previous Games."

O'Connor said that winning gold in Glasgow was part of her journey, and charted her progress from a junior athlete into regular medal contention on the world stage.

"This year I was in a really privileged position where I'd come in and I was the favourite, but that obviously comes with its own pressures and I think I navigated it very well.

"I'm really proud of how I managed to deal with the last three Games and how I've grown as an athlete.

"The Games have definitely stood to me. I'm so thankful that I've had the opportunity to compete in them."

The Commonwealth Games also has its own progression pathway.

The boxing team produced six medals, another impressive haul from a much less experienced team than in recent editions of the Games.

Jon McConnell, 23, is now Commonwealth champion, defending the title won last time by Aidan Walsh.

Can he now go on to win an Olympic medal like Walsh did? He might, if he stays off Love Island….

Kaci Rock is also 23 and a silver medallist and is already looking ahead to Olympic qualification.

"I've such a hunger now to move forward and the next big thing is the Olympics in Los Angeles and I'm going to do everything I can to get there. I've stood on the podium at the Commonwealth Games and now I want to stand out he podium at the Olympics," she said.

Swimmer Ellie McCartney won a magnificent bronze medal in the 100m breaststroke.

Three years ago, the Enniskillen swimmer's potential was noticed after winning two golds at the Youth Commonwealth Games.

Since then the 21-year-old has reached a first senior world final and taken a medal in Glasgow.

There were other notable achievements from some of the youngest members of Team NI and, like O'Connor, this experience will hopefully help them in the future.

Athlete Nick Griggs was sixth in the final of the men's 5000m while in the pool, 16-year-old Emily Hughes, the youngest member of Team NI, was a member of the 4x100m freestyle relay squad that set a new Irish Senior record.

A pair of 18-year-olds, Matthew Hamilton and Adam Bradley, also set Irish Junior records.

Another athlete waiting on A-Level results, weightlifter Harrison McGrogan, was fifth.

Then there was the emotion. The scream that judoka Rachael Hawkes let out on winning bronze after losing the same fight four years ago was almost primal, it meant so much to her.

There were the tears of bowler Chloe Wilson after winning bronze with Shauna O'Neill in the women's pairs.

Wilson, 23, and O'Neill, 26, have put to bed forever the myth that bowls is only played by pensioners.

Winning a medal is one thing but doing it with your best friend is something special.

"Words can't even describe how much it means. Just to be standing up there with Shauna, it's something really special," Wilson said with tears in her eyes.

O'Neill said the moment "is going to live with me for the rest of my life".

Gary Kelly had won bronze in the men's singles bowls in Delhi in 2010 and a silver four years ago.

In Glasgow it was another bronze in the singles but that elusive gold would finally come in the men's pairs with Adam McKeown, himself now a two-time Commonwealth Games champion.

Bowls isn't an Olympic sport so the Commonwealth Games is the pinnacle.

"The Commonwealth Games is the biggest opportunity for us, for media exposure, and for people that maybe wouldn't normally view our game and our sport," said Kelly

"It's incredibly important, and it's been fantastic for it to be part of this and for it to be respected as one of the six core sports of the Commonwealth Games. I think it deserves that."

Chef de Mission of Northern Ireland, Conal Heatley, believes strongly that the Commonwealth Games have prepared athletes for future successes.

"It was a very important part of their program," Heatley said on the 65 NI athletes in Glasgow.

"Whether it's Commonwealth Games, that's their pinnacle, or whether they will look to go on to Olympics, but each and every one of them strove to do their best here for Team NI."

The Indian city of Ahmedabad has already been announced as hosts for 2030.

Two years ago the future of the Commonwealth Games was uncertain when Victoria in Australia pulled out of hosting.

Glasgow stepped in, and while smaller and cheaper, they've provided competitive sport and enjoyment for spectators and athletes alike.

History shows how important the Commonwealth Games have been for athletes from Northern Ireland in building for the future while still winning medals at this level.

"Many, many of our athletes who have gone on to win Olympic medals have come through Commonwealth Games," Heatley added.

"It gives them an incredible opportunity to gain experience and prepare for the future."

title: 'Gutted' Graham settles for cycling silver after 'goalposts change'
description: Fin Graham was "gutted" to claim silver in the men's C1-C3 3km individual pursuit final, setting his sights firmly on gold. He was also a bit perplexed at how this race was staged.
fullText:
Fin Graham couldn't kid anyone. He didn't come for silver on Sunday.

The Scottish Para-cyclist upgraded Friday's bronze from the men's C1-C3 1000m time trial final, but he was going for gold in the C1-C3 3km individual pursuit final.

However, he was stood a step down from England's Matthew Robertson when Jerusalem bellowed round the velodrome, as he was denied what he called a "once in a lifetime" experience.

The 26-year-old was desperate to hear Flower of Scotland on home soil. Even more so given he felt a tang of injustice with the running of this race.

"I'd be lying if I said gold wasn't what I wanted," Graham told BBC Sport Scotland, after he was presented his second medal of these Games.

"It's a once in a lifetime opportunity to hear the national anthem here in Scotland, so I'd be lying if I said I was not gutted.

"As athletes, we've got hurdles to get over and goalposts do change, for whatever reason. But, the decision was made, you can't dwell on it."

Fachie survives painful crash to take another gold after Wales 'poke bear'

Teenage cyclist Boothman stars as Scotland bag three bronzes

Free-spirited Stewart avoids melee on way to Scottish silver

The decision in question, surrounds how this event was staged.

In layman terms, Graham had prepared to be racing head-to-head against an opponent in an individual pursuit, rather than hurtling round the track on his own in a time trial against the clock.

Earlier in the week, Graham posted on social media, external, sharing his confusion and anger about what he felt was a late change.

However, it emerged that a long-standing policy by the UCI - cycling's governing body - dictates that when riders are competing across classifications, as they are here, then a time trial is run instead to avoid big mismatches.

It's still the same distance, just solo. However, Graham still feels aggrieved.

"As racers, we want to be racing someone else on the track," he said. "For one reason or another, they've changed that at the start of the week.

"You have to come to terms with that and adjust.

"I think the crowd as well, it's better for them to see a race, but for some reason they've made the decision not to have that.

"We've done all we can do but it wasn't quite enough to take the gold today. Matt raced a good ride to take it, I just didn't quite have the legs to do that."

title: Satellite images show evidence of oil leak spreading from sanctioned vessel near Oman
description: The Caroline Bezengi, reportedly carrying over 800,000 barrels of Russian crude, is leaking oil into a marine reserve home to endangered wildlife off Oman's coast.
fullText:
A sanctioned tanker loaded with crude is leaving a growing trail of oil in protected waters off the coast of Oman, according to newly reviewed satellite images, as experts warn the stranded vessel could break apart during the region's rough monsoon season.

Satellite images reviewed by The Associated Press show an oil sheen covering roughly 20 square kilometers, or about 8 square miles, around Dhofar's Qibliyah Island, part of Oman's protected Hallaniyat Islands. Dark patches of crude have also reached the shoreline. Experts say the leak has worsened in recent days, fueling fears that rough weather could trigger a much larger spill.

"The last few days, the imagery indicates an increase in oil coming out, as the size of the sheen is growing," Wim Zwijnenburg, an environmental expert with the Dutch peace organization PAX, told the AP.

Report Warns Russia Using Shadow Fleet To Probe Nato Drone Defenses

He said the biggest risk is that the vessel could break apart as strong winds and rough seas during the annual monsoon season continue to pound the ship's hull.

The 899-foot, Cameroon-flagged Caroline Bezengi has been stranded off Oman's southern coast since June after its crew reported an onboard explosion, according to maritime news outlets. Reuters, citing maritime security sources, reported the vessel first ran into trouble on June 8 near the Yemeni port of Mukalla, where initial assessments suggested a blast may have occurred. The cause has not been confirmed.

Ship-tracking data reviewed by Reuters showed the tanker had loaded Russian crude at the Black Sea port of Novorossiysk before its latest voyage. The vessel has been sanctioned by the United Kingdom, the European Union, Canada and Switzerland for allegedly transporting Russian oil as part of Moscow's so-called "shadow fleet" — a network of aging tankers used to bypass Western sanctions imposed after Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

Hundreds Of Russian Shadow Tankers Trigger Military Alarm Transiting Nato Waters: Report

Zwijnenburg estimated the tanker is carrying more than 800,000 barrels of crude oil and said recent imagery suggests at least one section of the hull has been breached. Other maritime specialists who reviewed the images told Reuters the vessel also appears to be listing, adding to concerns that it could eventually break apart.

The spill threatens a protected marine reserve in the Arabian Sea that is home to endangered petrels and other rare wildlife. Greenpeace Germany warned that oil has already polluted stretches of coastline and damaged the area's fragile ecosystem.

"With oil apparently continuing to leak and the tanker stranded in a difficult location, there is a serious risk of a much larger oil disaster, with even more devastating consequences for the region's coastlines and marine ecosystems," Greenpeace Germany's Nina Noelle told the AP.

The U.N.'s International Maritime Organization said earlier this week it is monitoring the situation, adding that while the vessel has not broken apart, authorities are continuing to assess the safety and environmental risks.

Oman's Ministry of Transport, Communications and Information Technology ordered the vessel's owners to remove the ship and its cargo by July 23. It is unclear whether that deadline was met or whether the owners have responded.

title: Trump just invoked a 1930 tariff law no president has ever used — against Canada
description: The administration’s evidence supporting the tariffs is weak at best.
fullText:
President Donald Trump announced a new round of retaliatory tariffs on July 20 against Canada, invoking the Depression-era Smoot-Hawley Tariff Act in a game of tit for tat that can have no winner.

The administration argues that the new tariffs are necessary to address Canada's harmful discrimination against the United States auto industry, and are justified by Section 338 of Smoot-Hawley. But Section 338 has never been used to impose tariffs before this year. Section 338 was designed to deter foreign retaliation by allowing the President to increase tariffs against a country that had discriminatory tariffs or trade restrictions on American goods.

What evidence supports Trump's new retaliatory tariffs?

What is the Smoot-Hawley Tariff Act Section 338?

How have Canadian auto imports changed since tariffs?

What are the potential economic consequences of escalating tariffs?

While there can be no doubt that Canada's 25% tariffs on U.S. autos are discriminatory because they target American goods without putting similar burdens on goods from other countries, the administration's evidence supporting the tariffs is weak at best.

In its Proclamation announcing the new tariffs, the administration claimed that Canada's 25% tariff on U.S. autos and auto parts—enacted days after Trump's April 2, 2025 "Liberation Day" Executive Order announcing new U.S. tariffs on Canada and virtually every other country in the world—unfairly discriminates against the American auto industry, thus "disadvantaging the commerce of the United States compared to the commerce of other countries."

In support of this view, the administration claims that Canadian imports of U.S. autos "fell precipitously" by more than $5 billion, or "approximately 22%," while Canada's imports from Mexico, Japan, Korea, and Germany increased by nearly $3 billion.

A closer look at actual trade flows tells a different story, however. As the chart below shows, Canadian imports of U.S. autos historically have far exceeded those from the other listed countries. Since April 2025, Canada's auto imports from the other countries have increased slightly or stayed the same, while Canada's imports of U.S. autos have bounced around, falling sharply late last year, rebounding sharply during the first quarter of this year, then trending downward again—ending up, most recently, around the level they were in April '25.

Moreover, it's not clear that the tariffs are the cause of the modest decline in American auto exports to Canada. A more likely explanation is that Canadians, like Americans, are holding on to their existing cars longer, resulting in fewer new car purchases overall, which would affect both U.S. and foreign imports.

Indeed, a recent survey for Toyota Canada indicated that 56% of Canadians were delaying major purchases, including auto purchases, because of "affordability concerns." Mid-year data from the Automotive News Research and Data Center, showing a modest 1% decline in overall new car sales in Canada—with General Motors "once again" leading "all manufacturers in Canadian sales," and Ford ranked second—would seem to support this.

title: RFK Jr. says parents should vaccinate children against measles as U.S. cases hit a 35-year high
description: Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. said parents should get their children vaccinated against measles in a CNN interview, as U.S. cases reached a 35-year high.
fullText:
Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. said Sunday that parents should get their children vaccinated against measles, as the United States records its highest number of cases in 35 years.

Speaking on CNN's "State of the Union," Kennedy was asked by host Dana Bash, with the school year approaching, whether he would tell parents who have not vaccinated their children that they should do so because the vaccine is safe.

"We tell people ... that parents should get their children vaccinated for measles," Kennedy said. "A measles vaccine is effective. It stops measles in about 97% of the cases. People should get vaccinated."

Kennedy also said, "I've never questioned the efficacy of the MMR vaccine."

Kennedy is a longtime critic of vaccine policy who founded Children's Health Defense, an anti-vaccine advocacy group. He has generally acknowledged that the MMR vaccine prevents measles but has repeatedly raised concerns about vaccine safety and has said the decision to vaccinate should be a personal one.

The measles, mumps and rubella vaccine is about 97% effective at preventing measles after two doses, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

The comments came as measles spreads at levels not seen in decades. The CDC had recorded 2,371 confirmed cases as of July 30, surpassing last year's total and making 2026 the worst year for the disease since 1991. Cases have been reported in 45 states, and about 93% of those infected were unvaccinated. Officials have warned the country could lose its measles-elimination status this fall.

The surge has been driven by large outbreaks in several states, including South Carolina, Utah and Arizona, with Pennsylvania among the latest hot spots. Measles was declared eliminated in the United States in 2000, and public health officials have warned the country could lose that status this year. The Pan American Health Organization is expected to decide in the fall.

Measles can cause serious complications, including pneumonia and swelling of the brain, and can be fatal. Two unvaccinated children died during a 2025 outbreak in West Texas, the first measles deaths in the United States in a decade.

Kennedy first publicly urged people to get the measles vaccine in April 2025, during a deadly outbreak in West Texas.

title: Wiebes claims back-to-back Tour de France Femmes stage wins
description: Dutch sprinter Lorena Wiebes claims stage two for back-to-back victories at the Tour de France Femmes.
fullText:
Dutch sprinter Lorena Wiebes claimed stage two for back-to-back victories at the Tour de France Femmes.

Last year's green jersey winner, Wiebes, who is widely considered the fastest female sprinter in the peloton, burst clear of the pack with 250 metres to go to win by several bike lengths and extend her overall lead.

Her victory came after a hilly 147.9km route from Aigle to Geneva in Switzerland, much of it by the lakeside.

The charging peloton had chased down Lidl-Trek rider Riejanne Markus, who had broken away on her own, inside the final kilometre.

"The girls were chasing full gas to bring back Riejanne Markus, so it is even more beautiful to finish it off in the yellow jersey," Wiebes said.

"Every sprint is quite exciting - one small mistake and it is over.

"It will be hard to keep it [the yellow jersey] tomorrow, but we will try our best."

The 27-year-old Team SD Worx-Protime rider has now claimed seven Tour de France Femmes stage victories, extending her record as the rider with the most stage wins since the race returned to the World Tour calendar in 2022.

Italy's Elisa Balsamo finished second, while Netherlands veteran Marianne Vos, 39, crossed the line in third.

Great Britain's Josie Nelson and Zoe Backstedt finished sixth and seventh.

The 2026 Tour de France Femmes features 147 riders battling across nine stages - with the event including a first ascent of the famous Mont Ventoux climb on stage seven.

Stage three on Monday takes in a steep 11km climb just outside Geneva but ends with a flat 15km stretch to the finish line at Poligny.

The climb will not favour sprint specialist Wiebes, but the flat distance might give SD Worx-Protime the opportunity to organise a chase.

title: Selfies, signatures & social media - how Kerr embraced Glasgow Games
description: Gold medallist Josh Kerr has revelled in the Commonwealth Games and in competing for Scotland in Glasgow this week.
fullText:
Josh Kerr didn't get much sleep last night. "There's no time for that. Glasgow on the weekend, mate, it's bouncing," the Scot said with a slight croak in his voice.

The response - 11 hours after his Commonwealth Games mile victory - was entirely in keeping with the way Kerr has conducted himself this week. Embedded with Team Scotland, back home among his own people, and absolutely revelling in it.

Look at his social media. Reels of the 28-year-old running around the streets of the city. In its parks and on its tracks. Pictures of him loosening off under a Kingston Bridge flyover in a hotel car park. Images of him engaging with the crowd.

His crowd, the people who came to see the mile world record holder on Saturday night.

Among them were Kerr's grandparents and nephews, his first ever coach, and his training partners from when he was 11 or 12.

There were hundreds of awestruck kids, too. Some of them budding athletes themselves. Others who might now want to be. Just like Kerr was when the Games came to Glasgow in 2014, with dreams of emulating those he saw race at Hampden.

That memory was in mind as the Edinburgh athlete slowly worked his way back down the home straight from the podium after his emotional medal ceremony.

It's why every fan who asked for a selfie got one. Why he signed his name over and over again. Why he gave them his time and his attention. Sure, Kerr was soaking up his moment of glory, but he was giving something back too.

"I'm just trying to create a moment for them," he told BBC Sport Scotland.

"There is absolutely nothing stopping any of them going out and doing what I've just done.

"I believe if you grow up in Scotland, you can be one of the best runners in the history of these distances. I'm not doing anything outrageously special."

Saturday scrap ends with emotional Kerr winning fight

Kerr on why Commonwealth mile glory matters to him

Britain's Kerr breaks 27-year mile world record in London

Plenty would quibble with Kerr on that. After all, covering four laps and change in three minutes 42.66 seconds to set a new world record - having told people exactly when and how you're going to do it - seems both outrageous and special.

He was nowhere near as quick as that at a blustery Scotstoun but, even though he took just over 11 seconds more to complete the 1,609m, the Scot still put on a show on a track where he used to race - and regularly lose - as a child.

Having been enjoyably candid about his goals for the summer - smashing a 27-year-old standard and winning Games gold - Kerr concedes there is relief about following word with deed. But the expectation has also been infused with enjoyment, too.

"This whole experience has been really fun for me, too, actually," he said. "I used to come to Glasgow quite a lot to hang out with friends I made through athletics and, it's funny, we're staying pretty close to where we'd meet up and walk around town.

"The city is buzzing with the Games and it's just nice to be a part of that and really feed off the city."

It all culminated for Kerr with listening to Flower of Scotland playing while he stood, bottom lip twitching, on the podium. Several times he had to stop singing to compose himself and, when the music stopped, he had to wipe tears from his eyes.

Scotland matters to him in a way that those many natives who have lived outside the country will recognise. Albuquerque in New Mexico is his base now - something his accent and phraseology sometimes betray - but Edinburgh will always be home.

"It's everything to me," Kerr said of his nationality. "It's the way I present myself and the way I was built. I grew up in Edinburgh until I was 17 and I'm very proud to be Scottish. I'm back four times a year right now, which I feel pretty good about."

With that said, how does he feel about being considered a sporting standard bearer for his country? As a successor to the likes of Sir Chris Hoy and Sir Andy Murray?

"Um, yeah, that, that sounds, yeah, I mean, it's an honour to be, to be spoken in the same sentence as those two legends," said the loquacious Kerr, for once struggling for words as the notion takes hold.

"Sir Chris Hoy went to my school, actually, and spoke a few times during assemblies and that just closed the gap between me and him for when I was sitting there as a pupil. It made it seem possible.

"Hopefully I can do that too, but those two guys are absolute legends of the game and I've got a lot of work to do to keep up with them."

Keeping up, as Kerr has proved this summer, is not something he tends to struggle with.

title: Super Giants win comfortably against lowly MI
description: MI London remain without a win as Manchester Super Giants complete a comfortable six-wicket win at the Oval, while Trent Rockets hold off a late assault from Annabel Sutherland and Lauren Winfield-Hill to beat Sunrisers Leeds by five runs.
fullText:
The Hundred women's competition, The Oval

MI London 92 all out (99 balls): Chatli 18 (16); MacDonald-Gay 3-19

Manchester Super Giants 95-4 (72 balls): Lanning 43 (31); Gordon 2-14, Kerr 2-21

Manchester Super Giants won by six wickets

MI London remain without a win in the Hundred after Manchester Super Giants completed a comfortable six-wicket win at the Oval.

The competition's bottom side were bowled out for 92, while visiting captain Meg Lanning struck 43 as her side sealed victory with 28 balls to spare.

MI had a shocking start after being put into bat, with openers Hayley Matthews and Alice Davidson-Richards both bowled by Sophie Ecclestone for ducks.

The next four batters all reached the teens but failed to push on, while the last four MI wickets fell for five runs over the course of eight deliveries as the innings concluded with a ball to spare.

Ryana Macdonald-Gay took the final of wicket of Kirstie Gordon to finish with figures of 3-19, while Ecclestone and Maitlan Brown closed on 2-7 and 2-18 respectively.

The Super Giants opening pairing of Smriti Mandhana and Lanning took their side most of the way to their low target, putting on 73 before Mandhana was caught by Hollie Armitage off Gordon for 34.

Melie Kerr then dismissed Richa Ghosh (4) and Paige Scholfield (0) with successive deliveries, while Gordon trapped Lanning lbw with only four runs required for victory.

Mady Villiers wrapped the game up, hitting Gordon for four to condemn MI to a fourth defeat from five matches.

Third-placed Super Giants move back within two points of Trent Rockets in second, while MI remain bottom with their only points coming from a tie against London Spirit.

The Hundred women's competition, Trent Bridge

Trent Rockets 139-7 (100 balls): Dunkley 56 (33); Jonassen 2-20

Sunrisers Leeds 134-5 (100 balls): Sutherland 59* (30); Phillips 1-10

Trent Rockets held off a late assault from Annabel Sutherland and Lauren Winfield-Hill to beat defending champions Sunrisers Leeds by five runs and extend their winning streak to three matches.

Defending 139 at Trent Bridge after failing to capitalise on Sophia Dunkley's 29-ball half-century, economical bowling helped Rockets reduce Sunrisers to 76-4.

However, with 55 runs required off the final 20 balls, Sutherland dispatched Georgia Elwiss for 23 runs, including sending two full tosses away for six, to drag Sunrisers back into the match.

She and Winfield-Hill reduced the equation to 17 off five but when the latter was run out with three deliveries remaining, she took Sunrisers' hopes of victory with her.

Sutherland finished the match with a six to end unbeaten on 59 (30), with her partnership with Winfield-Hill (15) worth 50 off just 27 deliveries.

Earlier, Rockets had appeared well set for a sizeable total after Dunkley backed up her 57 against Manchester Super Giants on Friday with a knock of 56 (33), including nine fours, before being bowled by Sutherland.

Nat Sciver-Brunt and Ashleigh Gardner briefly maintained the pressure, including taking Dani Gibson's second set for 18 to carry Rockets beyond three figures off just 65 balls, but Sunrisers fought back with the ball.

Jess Jonassen and Hannah Baker took two wickets apiece as Rockets slumped from 105-2 to 118-6, with the hosts also failing to hit a boundary for 32 deliveries as their hopes of a 150-plus total faded.

A trio of fours from Bess Heath in the final set proved crucial, putting Rockets' total just out of Sunrisers' reach.

Trent Rockets' fourth victory of the tournament moves them to within four points of unbeaten Southern Brave at the top of the table. Sunrisers Leeds, who are without a win since their opener, slip to seventh.

title: Trump beats Wilson to clinch second Shanghai crown
description: World number one Judd Trump beats Kyren Wilson 11-6 to win the Shanghai Masters for the second time.
fullText:
World number one Judd Trump beat Kyren Wilson 11-6 to win the Shanghai Masters for the second time.

Trump, 36, led 7-3 after the final's opening session before taking four of the next seven frames to clinch the first big event of the 2026-27 season.

Wilson won the 2025 competition with an 11-9 victory over Ali Carter and moved into an early lead on Sunday. But Trump responded well and took a 4-2 advantage, helped by breaks of 73, 62 and a 67 clearance in the sixth frame to take it on the black having trailed 66-0.

World number seven Wilson pulled one back, but Trump, who also won the tournament in 2024, took three frames in a row to hold a four-frame advantage after the first session.

He stretched that to five by winning the first frame after the restart before Wilson made a break of 103, the first century of the final, to pull it back to 8-4.

Wilson won the next too, but Trump took the 14th frame on the black and the 15th on the pink to move one away from the title.

An excellent clearance of 134 from Wilson kept his hopes alive, but Trump sealed the 17th frame to lift the trophy once again.

"He's beaten me in the last few finals," Trump told the WST website. "It was nice to start the season in that kind of manner and get one over on him. This tournament is amazing. I love coming to Shanghai. It is the first tournament of the year and it is a bit unknown how you are going to play.

"The last time I won Shanghai I had a great season after that. You need to win tournaments like this to test yourself against the best. It was important to get off to a good start. I've done that, I just need to do the rest now."

The Shanghai Masters is a non-ranking event, but one of the most lucrative on the World Snooker Tour (WST), with Trump collecting £210,000 and 34-year-old Wilson £105,000.

The tournament featured 24 players - the top 16 in the world rankings, the next four Chinese players as well as four Chinese wildcards.

It was Trump's first main tournament since a disappointing performance at the World Championship in April when he lost 13-12 to Iranian qualifier Hossein Vafaei in the last 16.

But in China he beat Barry Hawkins, John Higgins and reigning world champion Wu Yize before his victory over Wilson.

The first main ranking tournament of the season begins on Saturday when the China Open returns to the calendar for the first time since 2019.

It will take place in Taiyuan from 8-16 August, replacing the Saudi Arabia Snooker Masters, which was cancelled after only two years of a 10-year deal.

Trump will begin his campaign next Sunday against Thailand's Noppon Saengkham before Wilson plays his first-round tie against Ireland's Aaron Hill the following day.

title: Duckett and Amir star as leaders Rockets see off Sunrisers
description: Ben Duckett strikes a half-century and takes a sharp diving catch to remove England team-mate Harry Brook as Trent Rockets beat Sunrisers Leeds by five runs.
fullText:
The Hundred men's competition, Trent Bridge

Trent Rockets 146-4 (100 balls): Duckett 64 (47); Carse 2-20

Sunrisers Leeds 141-4 (100 balls): Brook 46 (33); Amir 2-20

Ben Duckett struck a half-century and took a sharp diving catch to remove England team-mate Harry Brook as The Hundred leaders Trent Rockets beat Sunrisers Leeds by five runs.

The 31-year-old smacked Liam Patterson-White for five consecutive fours to bring up his fifty off 35 balls, but it was an otherwise measured innings from the opener, who made 64 (47), including nine boundaries, to help Rockets post 146-4.

A 71-run third-wicket stand between Mitchell Marsh and Brook put Sunrisers in control of their chase, with just 35 runs required from 20 deliveries.

However, Mohammad Amir only conceded five runs off the next four balls before Brook found a leaping Duckett in the covers to depart for 46 (33).

Amir had Marsh (41 off 35) caught behind by Sam Billings five balls later, finishing with figures of 2-20, and an equation of 25 runs from 10 deliveries proved too much for Dan Lawrence and Tom Alsop.

Duckett had earlier anchored his side's innings, with his knock in stark contrast to Trent Rockets debutant Aneurin Donald.

Introduced early in the powerplay after Brydon Carse (2-20) bowled Finn Allen, Donald thrashed three sixes and dominated his 63-run second-wicket stand with Duckett, hitting 40 runs off 19 deliveries.

Carse also accounted for Donald, whose free-scoring was unmatched on either side, while Duckett was bowled by Nathan Ellis with five balls remaining.

Tim David was laboured for his 24 (22) but struck a crucial six off the penultimate ball of the innings.

A fourth consecutive victory moves Trent Rockets four points clear at the top of The Hundred table. Sunrisers Leeds remain fifth, with two wins and two defeats.

title: Chelsea sign Strasbourg midfielder Barco
description: Chelsea complete the signing of Argentina and Strasbourg midfielder Valentin Barco on a seven-year deal.
fullText:
Chelsea have completed the signing of Strasbourg midfielder Valentin Barco on a seven-year deal.

The 21-year-old becomes Chelsea's sixth signing of the summer after the arrivals of Morgan Rogers, Danny Welbeck, Emmanuel Emegha, Maxence Lacroix and Marco Palestra.

The midfielder will join the remainder of Chelsea's pre-season tour, with the Blues set to face Italian side Juventus in Hong Kong on 5 August.

Chelsea did not disclose the fee.

The Argentine appeared once for his country at the 2026 World Cup, where they finished runners-up to Spain.

A product of Boca Juniors' academy, Barco joined Brighton in 2024 for a fee of £7.9m.

But he spent just a year on the south coast, and joined Strasbourg the following summer after a successful loan spell.

He comes the second player this summer to join Chelsea from Strasbourg, with both clubs owned by Todd Boehly and Clearlake Capital.

It is the 13th deal between the two clubs since the start of last season.

title: Finucane creates Games history with fourth gold
description: Welsh star Emma Finucane creates history by becoming the first sprint cyclist to win four track gold medals at the same Commonwealth Games.
fullText:
Welsh star Emma Finucane has created history by becoming the first sprint cyclist to win four track gold medals at the same Commonwealth Games.

Finucane added keirin success to the golds she had already won in the team and individual sprints and 1,000m time trial.

Olympic champion Ellesse Andrews finished second when defending her Commonwealth keirin title.

In Birmingham in 2022, New Zealand cyclist Aaron Gate won four gold medals with three on the track and one in the road race.

Finucane has achieved her quartet of successes in four successive days in the Chris Hoy Velodrome in Glasgow.

Australian legend Anna Meares and New Zealander Andrews had previously won three track titles in 2010 and 2022 respectively.

The 23-year-old has also become the first Welsh woman to collect four golds at a single Commonwealth Games.

Finucane is also Wales' most successful female athlete in Games history after overtaking Para-sprinter Olivia Breen, who held the record for two days.

Weightlifter David Morgan remains Wales' most successful Commonwealth Games athlete with nine golds and three silver.

Finucane won Wales' 31st medal of the Games with nine gold, 10 silver and 12 bronze.

The Carmarthen star has also been chosen to be the Team Wales flag bearer for the closing ceremony tonight.
