nobody should assume a human reviewed every line. The engineering is real and
every finding was verified by running the thing rather than reasoning about it.
It has still only existed for two days.

Roblox does not support third-party clients and operates automated systems that
ban accounts for using them, up to permanent termination. Those systems have
produced false positives against innocent players.

Roblox has not approved this project, and has not been asked to. There is
no green light, no arrangement, and no reason to assume tolerance. Treat every
claim below as our reasoning about risk, not as permission.

Cordial does not modify the Roblox client — it runs the official Android build,
does not touch the engine's process, and any asset overlay you enable is
non-destructive and off by default — but it necessarily presents a synthesised
Android environment, and a heuristic detector does not owe you that
distinction. Alternate accounts are not a shield; Roblox's Terms reserve the
right to terminate those too.

Enforcement at this scale is automated and runs in waves, and accounts sharing
an address get associated with each other. If you test, use a throwaway account
on a different IP — see CONTRIBUTING.md.

If your account matters to you, do not use it here. If you use Cordial and
get banned, that is on you, and the maintainers cannot get it reversed.

Cordial is a compatibility runtime, not a cheat tool, and we do not endorse or
support using it to exploit Roblox or any experience running on it.

That is not only a position, it is a property of the build. Cordial has no
script executor, no hooking, no memory access to the Roblox process and no API

is no primitive in the binary to extract or re-enable in a fork. Plugins run in
a separate process behind a capability broker and cannot read Cordial's memory,
let alone Roblox's. The reasoning is in
ADR-001 and
ADR-003, and it is deliberately load-
bearing: a restriction can be lifted in a fork, a capability that was never
built cannot.

If you want an executor, this is the wrong project, and pull requests adding one
will be declined.

Frame rate measured with pointer motion driven for the whole run, because
presents drop to exactly 1/s when nothing is happening and every earlier figure
in this repository was that idle throttle integrated: a flat 60.0 on MAILBOX
against a variable 35–50 on FIFO, four runs of 120 s.

What is left is polish and two real gaps. Text fields take the characters
and do not draw them until focus leaves, because on Android a transparent
EditText draws a focused box and there is none here. And Roblox is never told
it may capture the pointer, so in first person the cursor walks off the window —
the native that says so is exported and has never been called.

The keyboard took a week and the answer was one number.
nativePassKeyEvent wants Linux evdev codes; it was being handed Android
keycodes. Exactly one key worked — D, because AKEYCODE_D and KEY_D are
both 32 — and Alt made the character jump, because AKEYCODE_ALT_LEFT is 57 and
so is KEY_SPACE. Four theories were measured and disproved first, every one of
them assuming a number was wrong somewhere. The numbers were fine; the
vocabulary was.

Two accounts at once, and it was not built as a feature. A profile is
storage and an instance is a window (ADR-012),
with an flock so one profile cannot be opened twice — which leaves nothing
stopping two different profiles running side by side, each with its own
session, settings and plugin grants. On Windows this traditionally needed a
second desktop session. Each instance is a whole engine, so budget around 1.5 GB
of memory apiece.

Install it expecting rough edges. It plays; it is not finished.

Cordial is early. You can sign in, load a game and play it with a keyboard and
mouse — but text fields do not draw what you type, first person cannot capture
the pointer, and there is no sound yet. See the status table.

From an installed APK you need the lib/x86_64/ objects and the base APK.

Flatpak is the intended way. There is no hosted remote yet, so it builds from

A window opens, the engine comes up, and it renders Roblox's logged-out landing
page at about 27 fps. --run is how many seconds to stay up.

cordial-run --help lists the rest.

Roblox is configured by FastFlags, and Cordial lets you override any of them.
Create ~/.local/share/cordial/profiles/<profile>/flags.json (or point
CORDIAL_FLAGS at another file) with a flat object:

Values may be written as booleans, numbers or strings — Roblox stores them all
as strings and Cordial converts. The overrides are merged into the settings
document the engine is given at startup, and the launch log reports how many
were applied.

FFlag, FInt and FString are read once at startup, so changing them
needs a relaunch. Only the DFFlag/DFInt/DFString family is re-read while
the client is running. That distinction matters if you are building anything
that changes flags dynamically — a plugin loaded part-way through a session
cannot change a startup flag, whatever it writes.

Flags come from more than one place, and each source owns its own file:

Your overrides live in the profile, so a flag you set while testing something on
one account is not silently still set on the account you play. A file left at
the old ~/.config/cordial/flags.json is moved into the first profile that goes
looking for one — see ADR-013.

A plugin never writes to your file. That keeps three things true: a plugin
cannot silently overwrite a value you chose, removing a plugin removes its
flags, and "why is this flag set to that?" has an answer. Conflicts are reported
rather than resolved quietly:

Two plugins disagreeing is a real disagreement, so both are named. The later one
wins so the outcome is deterministic, but nothing is hidden.

If the interface looks coarse, it is being laid out for a low-density phone.
Raise both — the render resolution is 720p by default and dpiScale is 1.0,
which is what Roblox treats as a cheap handset:

Roblox's graphics-quality FastFlags (DebugFRMQualityLevelOverride and the MSAA
overrides) were tested and change nothing here, because they govern 3D scene
rendering and the logged-out landing page is a 2D interface. Resolution and
density are the levers that apply to it.

Read the engine's own log first. Roblox writes it to
<files>/appData/logs/*.log and it names subsystems, stages, paths and
exceptions in its own words. It is the best diagnostic in the project and most
questions are answered by the newest file in that directory.

To check whether input is reaching the engine, run with
CORDIAL_ANDROID_TRACE=1 and look for onTouchEventNative(...) -> true.

Start with docs/NEXT.md. The rest is reference.

Roblox ships a complete x86-64 Android build. split_config.x86_64.apk
carries lib/x86_64/libroblox.so — 116 MB of x86-64 machine code built by NDK
r28c. Cordial executes it natively and needs no CPU architecture translation,
only CPU feature emulation. That is the difference between a tractable systems
project and one an order of magnitude larger.

The runtime surface is bounded: 13 Android libraries linked, 644 undefined
symbols, GLES2 + EGL mandatory with Vulkan dlopened as an optional upgrade.

Roblox's game surface is AGDK GameActivity, which is Apache-2.0 open
source — so the activity, surface, input and IME contract can be read rather than
inferred.

No in-process code execution against the Roblox process: no hooking, no memory
patching, no injected script environment. Not "disabled by default" — absent from
the API vocabulary, so there is no injection primitive in the binary to extract.
Reasoning in ADR-001.

Also out: client-side integrity flags or watermarks, and obfuscation-as-security.

Third-party components keep their own licences and notices, reproduced in
THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md and installed alongside the
binary by the Flatpak:

MIT and Apache-2.0 are satisfied while the combined work is offered under the
GPL, provided those notices travel with it. That is a condition, not a

title: There Are Only Four Billion Floats–So Test Them All (2014)
description: A few months ago I saw a blog post touting fancy new SSE3 functions for implementing vector floor, ceil, and round functions. There was the inevitable proud proclaiming of impressive performance an…
fullText:
A few months ago I saw a blog post touting fancy new SSE3 functions for implementing vector floor, ceil, and round functions. There was the inevitable proud proclaiming of impressive performance and correctness. However the ceil function gave the wrong answer for many numbers it was supposed to handle, including odd-ball numbers like ‘one’.

The floor and round functions were similarly flawed. The reddit discussion of these problems then discussed two other sets of vector math functions. Both of them were similarly buggy.

Fixed versions of some of these functions were produced, and they are greatly improved, but some of them still have bugs.

Floating-point math is hard, but testing these functions is trivial, and fast. Just do it.

The functions ceil, floor, and round are particularly easy to test because there are presumed-good CRT (C RunTime) functions that you can check them against. And, you can test every float bit-pattern (all four billion!) in about ninety seconds. It’s actually very easy. Just iterate through all four-billion (technically 2^32) bit patterns, call your test function, call your reference function, and make sure the results match. Properly comparing NaN and zero results takes a bit of care but it’s still not too bad.

Aside: floating-point math has a reputation for producing results that are unpredictably wrong. This reputation is then used to justify sloppiness, which then justifies the reputation. In fact IEEE floating-point math is designed to, whenever practical, give the best possible answer (correctly rounded), and functions that extend floating-point math should follow this pattern, and only deviate from it when it is clear that correctness is too expensive.

Later on I’ll show the implementation for my ExhaustiveTest function but for now here is the function declaration:

Typical test code that uses ExhaustiveTest is shown below. In this case I am testing the original SSE 2 _mm_ceil_ps2 function that started the discussion, with a wrapper to translate between float and __m128. The function didn’t claim to handle floats outside of the range of 32-bit integers so I restricted the test range to just those numbers:

Note that this code uses the Float_t type to get the integer representation of a particular float. I described Float_t years ago in Tricks With the Floating-Point Format .

_mm_ceil_ps2 claimed to handle all numbers in the range of 32-bit integers, which is already ignoring about 38% of floating-point numbers. Even in that limited range it had 872,415,233 errors – that’s a 33% failure rate over the 2,650,800,128 floats it tried to handle. _mm_ceil_ps2 got the wrong answer for all numbers between 0.0 and FLT_EPSILON * 0.25, all odd numbers below 8,388,608, and a few other numbers. A fixed version was quickly produced after the errors were pointed out.

Another set of vector math functions that was discussed was DirectXMath. The 3.03 version of DirectXMath’s XMVectorCeiling claimed to handle all floats. However it failed on lots of tiny numbers, and on most odd numbers. In total there were 880,803,839 errors out of the 4,294,967,296 numbers (all floats) that it tried to handle. The one redeeming point for XMVectorCeiling is that these bugs have been known and fixed for a while, but you need the latest Windows SDK (comes with VS 2013) in order to get the fixed 3.06 version. And even the 3.06 version doesn’t entirely fix XMVectorRound.

The LiraNuna / glsl-sse2 family of functions were the final set of math functions that were mentioned. The LiraNuna ceil function claimed to handle all floats but it gave the wrong answer on 864,026,625 numbers. That’s better than the others, but not by much.

I didn’t exhaustively test the floor and round functions because it would complicate this article and wouldn’t add significant value. Suffice it to say that they have similar errors.

Several of the ceil functions were implemented by adding 0.5 to the input value and rounding to nearest. This does not work. This technique fails in several ways:

The 3.03 version of DirectXMath’s XMVectorCeiling used a variant of this technique. Instead of adding 0.5 they added g_XMOneHalfMinusEpsilon. Perversely enough the value of this constant doesn’t match its name – it’s actually one half minus 0.75 times FLT_EPSILON. Curious. Using this constant avoids errors on 1.0f but it still fails on small numbers and on odd numbers greater than one.

The fixed version of _mm_ceil_ps2 comes with a handy template function that can be used to extend it to support the full range of floats. Unfortunately, due to an implementation error, it fails to handle NaNs. This means that if you call _mm_safeInt_ps<new_mm_ceil_ps2>() with a NaN then you get a normal number back. Whenever possible NaNs should be ‘sticky’ in order to aid in tracking down the errors that produce them.

The problem is that the wrapper function uses cmpgt to create a mask that it can use to retain the value of large floats – this mask is all ones for large floats. However since all comparisons with NaNs are false this mask is zero for NaNs, so a garbage value is returned for them. If the comparison is switched to cmple and the two mask operations (and and andnot) are switched then NaN handling is obtained for free. Sometimes correctness doesn’t cost anything. Here’s a fixed version:

With this fix and the latest version of _mm_ceil_ps2 it becomes possible to handle all 4 billion floats correctly.

Conventional wisdom says that you should never compare two floats for equality – you should always use an epsilon. Conventional wisdom is wrong.

I’ve written in great detail about how to compare floating-point values using an epsilon, but there are times when it is just not appropriate. Sometimes there really is an answer that is correct, and in those cases anything less than perfection is just sloppy.

So yes, I’m proudly comparing floats to see if they are equal.

After the flaws in these functions were pointed out fixed versions of _mm_ceil_ps2 and its sister functions were quickly produced and these new versions work better.

I didn’t test every function, but here are the results from the final versions of functions that I did test:

Exhaustive testing works brilliantly for functions that take a single float as input. I used this to great effect when rewriting all of the CRT math functions for a game console some years ago. On the other hand, if you have a function that takes multiple floats or a double as input then the search space is too big. In that case a mixture of test cases for suspected problem areas and random testing should work. A trillion tests can complete in a reasonable amount of time, and it should catch most problems.

Here’s a simple function that can be used to test a function across all floats. The sample code linked below contains a more robust version that tracks how many errors are found.

My test code misses one subtle difference – it fails to detect one type of error. Did you spot it?

The correct result for ceil(-0.5f) is -0.0f. The sign bit should be preserved. The vector math functions all fail to do this. In most cases this doesn’t matter, at least for game math, but I think it is at least important to acknowledge this (minor) imperfection. If the compare function was put into ‘fussy’ mode (just compare the representation of the floats instead of the floats) then each of the ceil functions would have an additional billion or so failures, from all of the floats between -0.0 and -1.0.

The original post that announced _mm_ceil_ps2 can be found here – with corrected code:

http://dss.stephanierct.com/DevBlog/?p=8

This post discusses the bugs in the 3.03 version of DirectXMath and how to get fixed versions:

http://blogs.msdn.com/b/chuckw/archive/2013/03/06/known-issues-directxmath-3-03.aspx

This post links to the LiraNuna glsl-sse2 math library:

https://github.com/LiraNuna/glsl-sse2

The original reddit discussion of these functions can be found here:

http://w3.reddit.com/r/programming/comments/1p2yys/sse3_optimized_vector_floor_ceil_round_and_mod/

Sample code for VC++ 2013 to run these tests. Just uncomment the test that you want to run from the body of main.

https://www.cygnus-software.com/ftp_pub/test4billion.zip

The reddit discussion of this post can be found here, and then here.

The hacker news discussion of this post can be found here, and then here. And again in 2020 it can be found here.

I’ve written before about running tests on all of the floats. The last time I was exhaustively testing round-tripping of printed floats, which took long enough that I showed how to easily parallelize it and then I verified that they round-tripped between VC++ and gcc. This time the tests ran so quickly that it wasn’t even worth spinning up extra threads.

title: China's free Kimi K3 AI model shakes up global tech market
description: Governments can now deploy top-tier AI locally, bypassing costly U.S. cloud rentals.
fullText:
The best artificial intelligence technology any country can own is now available for free.

On July 27, China’s Moonshot AI put its most powerful chatbot on the internet for anyone to use. The AlibabaiAlibabaAlibaba, founded in 1999 by Chinese entrepreneur Jack Ma, is one of the most prominent global e-commerce companies that operates platforms like AliExpress, Taobao, and Tmall.-backed developer released the software behind its AI model Kimi K3, allowing any government, company, or individual to run it on their own computers without paying Beijing-based Moonshot. Users can also retrain the chatbot to fit their own language and laws.

Nations are spending billions of dollars to run sovereign systems or AI on their own soil so that citizen data stays within their borders and can’t be accessed by foreign companies or governments. Most countries own the machines but lease the computing power and software from U.S. companies such as Microsoft, Google, and Amazon, which count on the rent continuing for years. Kimi K3 offers those governments a way out.

An open, high-quality model like Kimi K3 does change the calculation for governments.” Mohammed Soliman, senior fellow, Middle East Institute

“An open, high-quality model like Kimi K3 does change the calculation for governments that have been investing heavily in hardware while paying for access to American models,” Mohammed Soliman, a senior fellow at Washington-based think tank Middle East Institute, told Rest of World. “If a competitive model becomes freely available, the return on those hardware investments increases because governments can reduce or eliminate ongoing licensing costs.”

Kimi K3 ranks third on Artificial Analysis’s index of the best AI systems, behind Anthropic’s Claude Fable 5 and OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol Max, both of which charge users. Every free model in the world, including China’s DeepSeek and Meta’s Llama, sits below Kimi K3.

Kimi K3 reads images as well as text, so it can work through scanned records, forms and photographs, and it can be reshaped to answer in Hindi, Arabic or Swahili, among other languages, as easily as in Chinese or English.

The chatbot has closed China’s gap with the best U.S. AI systems from months to weeks, according to a July report by researcher Ryan Fedasiuk of the American Enterprise Institute, a public-policy think tank.

“Chinese open-weight models are growing in popularity around the world as free and customizable alternatives to the closed U.S. frontier,” Vivek Chilukuri, program director for technology and national security at the Center for a New American Security, told Rest of World. “That’s true not only in more cost-sensitive emerging markets but in developer communities from Bangalore to San Francisco.”

The savings from free models like Kimi K3 can be largest in the countries that have already bought the hardware. Microsoft, Google, and Amazon have committed to building data centers and cloud services worth more than $30 billion across the Gulf, and more than $45 billion in India, among other regions.

India signed a deal with United Arab Emirates-backed G42 to deploy an AI supercomputer made of 64 U.S.-made systems on Indian soil, while continuing to pay U.S. companies for AI software. For India and every government in the same position, a model of Kimi K3’s rank is an option to run on machines inside their own borders.

Still, being free is no guarantee that governments will adopt it.

Free Chinese models have been available for more than a year, yet no government has built its national AI project on one, as countries also judge the manuals, the legal terms, how well the software handles their languages, and where it comes from.

The Sovereign AI Index, which follows 139 state-backed AI projects across 56 countries and regions, found that where governments disclose the software underneath their AI, four in 10 chose Meta’s free U.S. model Llama, and not one chose DeepSeek or Moonshot’s earlier chatbots, even though those were free and highly rated.

Whether Kimi K3 breaks that pattern will likely depend partly on the support Moonshot provides and partly on government wariness about adopting Chinese models due to concerns of trust and surveillance, Pablo Chavez, an adjunct senior fellow at CNAS, which publishes the index, told Rest of World.

“That tells me benchmark position alone doesn’t change what sovereign builders do,” Chavez said. “Instead, governments appear to choose base models the way they choose other infrastructure — documentation, licensing, language coverage, capability, and so forth.”

Countries should encourage open source, Chinese President Xi Jinping told the World AI Conference in Shanghai on July 17, pledging AI cooperation centers with the Arab League, the African Union and ASEAN. Alibaba has since announced Qwen 3.8 with a promise to give it away, while Nvidia, Google and OpenAI have all released free models this year.

While software like Kimi K3 may cost nothing, the machines that run it come at a price. A chatbot of Kimi K3’s size runs only on the most advanced chips, and the U.S. decides which countries can buy those chips. The Commerce Department went further last year and considered cutting off Chinese AI labs from U.S. technology altogether.

“U.S. export controls continue to confer enormous leverage on Washington, because the world desperately wants cutting-edge AI chips, which you need regardless of whether you’re running a U.S. or Chinese model,” Chilukuri said.

China has yet to fill that gap, as its chipmakers are unable to produce their most advanced processors in quantities large enough to export, Chilukuri said. A country that downloads Kimi K3 gets the software and nothing else, while the chips it runs on, the data centers that house it, and whatever model comes after it remain in other hands, Chavez said.

“A government can hold a model’s weights and still depend on others for chips, data centers, and future models,” Chavez said. “Open weights address the risk of losing access, but they don’t remove the dependencies upstream.”

title: Bhuvneshwar Kumar breaks silence on India comeback after R Ashwin backs him for 2027 ODI World Cup
description: After a stellar IPL season in 2025 and 2026 with RCB, veteran pacer Bhuvneshwar Kumar has broken the silence on his Team India comeback after support from R Ashwin.
fullText:
Bhuvneshwar Kumar breaks silence on India comeback after R Ashwin backs him for 2027 ODI World Cup originally appeared on Cricket News. Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Bhuvneshwar Kumar says he has made peace with life outside the India team.

The comments follow Ravichandran Ashwin backing him for the 2027 World Cup.

The 36-year-old insists he now plays purely for the love of the game.

Bhuvneshwar Kumar has broken his silence on the growing clamour for an India recall, striking a notably measured tone even as pundits push his case for the 2027 ODI World Cup. The veteran seamer, whose stellar IPL 2026 campaign reignited the debate, insists he has made peace with his life away from the national team.

His remarks come days after Ravichandran Ashwin publicly backed him for a place in India's World Cup plans. Speaking on his YouTube channel, Ashwin said, "Bhuvneshwar Kumar is a yes. I would tell him to do all the tournaments - first class, the Vijay Hazare - everything. And get him ready for South Africa. I think we would require him there."

Yet Bhuvneshwar, who last played for India in 2022, made clear that another cap is no longer the force driving his career. The right-armer credited his home environment for helping him move on without bitterness, having been a mainstay of India's attack for the best part of a decade before sliding out of the reckoning.

MORE: Abhishek Sharma scores 233 in 91 balls in district match

Bhuvneshwar was candid about how he has come to terms with his exclusion. Speaking on the RCB Podcast, he said, "I am at peace, and I give credit to my family. At home, we never talk about cricket. We never talk about whether I'll get back into the Indian team, why I wasn't selected, or what went wrong. That played a big role, and there is no regret."

He acknowledged the difficulty of accepting such a transition after years as a central figure. Bhuvneshwar said, "When you're a core member of a team, everyone says: 'Team comes first.' But when you're no longer in the team, naturally you feel: 'Maybe I should still be there.'"

For all that, he framed his situation as a natural part of the sport. Bhuvneshwar said, "I understand that transitions are a part of sport. I understand that generations change. I'm not the first player to experience this, and I certainly won't be the last. Family plays a big role. I am happy being where I am."

MORE: Jasprit Bumrah ruled out of Sri Lanka Tests! Front-runners to replace the Indian pacer listed

Bhuvneshwar was clear that his motivation now stems from enjoyment rather than ambition. He said, "I've already played for India. That's not something I have to achieve now. If I get another opportunity, that's great, but I've been there. Everything I'm doing now is because of my love for the game."

He added that experience had given him a deeper appreciation of the sport's well-worn wisdom. Bhuvneshwar said, "When you're young and playing for India, you say you love the game. But only now do I actually understand phrases like 'control the controllables', 'don't overthink' and 'play for the passion of the game'. I can genuinely feel those things."

His form has certainly not dipped, having finished as the second-highest wicket-taker in IPL 2026 with 28 scalps in 16 matches at an economy of 7.95, integral to another RCB title.

MORE: Why Bhuvneshwar Kumar could make it to India's 2027 ODI World Cup squad?

There is a quiet wisdom in Bhuvneshwar's response that reflects well on him. Rather than fuel the speculation or lobby for a return, he has taken the pressure off himself, and his emphasis on peace over ambition suggests a man unlikely to be destabilised by the noise around his name.

The irony is that this contentment may be exactly what makes him a viable option. A bowler with nothing to prove, playing freely and taking wickets in bulk, is often more dangerous than one straining for recognition.

Whether the selectors share Ashwin's enthusiasm remains to be seen, but Bhuvneshwar has answered the question in the only way he sensibly could, by refusing to let it define him.

title: Kelsey Plum trade grades: Mercury make bold playoff gamble as Sparks begin another rebuild
description: The Mercury acquired five-time All-Star Kelsey Plum from the Sparks in a blockbuster deadline deal. Here is what the trade means for both teams.
fullText:
Kelsey Plum trade grades: Mercury make bold playoff gamble as Sparks begin another rebuild originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The biggest name available before the WNBA trade deadline is officially on the move. The Los Angeles Sparks are trading five-time All-Star guard Kelsey Plum to the Phoenix Mercury, according to ESPN’s Shams Charania and Kendra Andrews. Los Angeles will receive guard Monique Akoa Makani, a 2027 first-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick in the deal.

The trade was completed late Saturday night, just hours before Sunday afternoon’s deadline. According to ESPN, Plum becomes only the fourth All-Star in WNBA history to be traded during a season. Plum has not played since June 21 because of a lower left leg injury, but she had returned to practice and was expected to be available for the Sparks’ game against the Portland Fire on Sunday. It remains unclear whether she will be ready to make her Mercury debut Monday against the Chicago Sky.

When healthy, Plum gives Phoenix one of the league’s most dangerous offensive guards. She is averaging career highs of 23.9 points and 6.4 assists through 12 games this season.

Here are the early grades for the blockbuster trade.

Phoenix is taking a major swing despite facing a difficult path to the playoffs. The Mercury entered Sunday with an 11-19 record, six games behind the New York Liberty for the eighth and final postseason spot. Adding Plum does not guarantee Phoenix will close that gap, especially with only a limited portion of the regular season remaining.

It does, however, make the Mercury significantly more dangerous. Plum joins an experienced core featuring Kahleah Copper, Alyssa Thomas and DeWanna Bonner. She should provide the perimeter scoring, shooting and playmaking Phoenix needs after reaching the WNBA Finals last season.

The two-time WNBA champion has also demonstrated that she can thrive alongside other stars. Plum helped the Las Vegas Aces win consecutive championships in 2022 and 2023 before being traded to Los Angeles ahead of the 2025 season. Phoenix did not acquire Plum merely to improve its regular-season record. The Mercury are betting that their veteran roster can reach the postseason and become a matchup no contender wants to see in the opening round.

The cost is substantial for a team sitting 12th in the standings. First-round picks carry increased value as the WNBA continues to add talent and expand, while Akoa Makani is a promising young guard. Plum’s contract situation also creates long-term uncertainty. Still, Phoenix needed an offensive difference-maker, and no player available at the deadline offered more immediate upside than Plum.

Trading Plum signals another change in direction for a Sparks organization that has struggled to establish a clear plan. Los Angeles acquired Plum before the 2025 season in exchange for the No. 2 overall pick, hoping she could accelerate a rebuild centered around Cameron Brink and Rickea Jackson. The Sparks then made another aggressive move this past offseason, trading Jackson as part of a deal for veteran guard Ariel Atkins.

Those moves have not produced a playoff contender. Los Angeles entered Sunday at 10-17 after losing six consecutive games. The Sparks have gone 2-9 during Plum’s current absence and are in danger of missing the postseason for the sixth straight year. Plum also signed only a one-year deal worth $999,999 to return to Los Angeles during the offseason. The Athletic reported that she was not interested in re-signing with the Sparks, leaving the team at risk of losing its leading scorer without receiving anything in return.

Considering those circumstances, Los Angeles did well to acquire a first-round pick, a second-round pick and a young player.

Akoa Makani gives the Sparks another developmental option in the backcourt. The 24-year-old guard entered the league as a third-round selection by Phoenix in the 2025 WNBA Draft after playing professionally in France. The 2027 first-rounder is the centerpiece of the return. Its eventual value will depend on Phoenix’s record and any protections attached to the selection, but it gives Los Angeles another important asset as the franchise reevaluates its roster.

The trade does not fix the Sparks’ larger problems. General manager Raegan Pebley was fired in July, and interim assistant GMs Zach Knowlton and Nate Nielsen are now responsible for determining the organization’s direction. At least Los Angeles avoided compounding its mistakes by keeping Plum through the deadline and potentially losing her for nothing.

MORE: Sky rookie Sydney Taylor stuns Aces with game-winning 3-pointer at the buzzer

The deal carries considerable risk on each side. Phoenix is surrendering future assets for a 31-year-old guard who has appeared in only 12 games this season. Even if Plum returns immediately, the Mercury have significant ground to make up in the standings.

Los Angeles, meanwhile, is moving on from a player it acquired less than two years ago to help lead the franchise back into contention. The Sparks are once again collecting future assets without a clearly established timeline for returning to the playoffs.

Plum is the unquestioned winner. She leaves a team on a six-game losing streak for a veteran Mercury roster willing to make an aggressive push.

If Phoenix can reach the postseason, Plum’s scoring ability and championship experience could make the Mercury far more dangerous than their record suggests. If the rally falls short, the franchise may regret sacrificing a first-round pick for such a narrow window.

For now, the WNBA’s biggest deadline move has given both teams something they needed: The Mercury have another star, while the Sparks have a chance to start over again.

title: Takeaways: Brais Mendez steps up in Crew debut to earn draw vs. Miami
description: Newcomer Brais Mendez scored in his debut to help the Columbus Crew secure a 2-2 draw against Inter Miami.
fullText:
Inter Miami's Lionel Messi, one of the greatest soccer players of all time and a former FC Barcelona superstar, entered the game after occupying the bench for 52 minutes against the Crew Aug. 1. Miami forward Luis Suarez, another former La Liga star, recorded a goal and an assist in the first half while former Real Madrid midfielder Casemiro made his home debut for Miami.

But it was a former La Liga player on the Crew side who came up big late.

Making his MLS debut after the Crew acquired him during the summer transfer window, former Real Sociedad attacking midfielder Brais Mendez helped Columbus earn a point in a 2-2 draw by scoring a free kick roughly 20 minutes after he took the field in the 61st minute.

"I am very happy about my debut and the goal," Mendez said after the game via a translator. "... We want to keep this strong run going and earn wins to continue to move up in the table.”

The Crew matched their best result against a Messi-led Miami team and prevented him from scoring in his World Cup return. The Crew will enter Leagues Cup play with solid performances in their last two games, including a 2-1 victory over rival FC Cincinnati last week.

Here are three takeaways from the Crew's late comeback and earned point against Miami.

The Crew had an obvious missing piece entering the match against Miami: Max Arfsten.

Against Miami, Mendez filled the void.

A Spanish attacking midfielder who signed a designated player contract on July 2, Mendez answered the call when defender Sekou Bangoura earned a free kick for Columbus just outside the right corner of the penalty area in the 84th minute. Mendez hooked the shot to the low part of the left post, which ricocheted into the net for the equalizer.

“We just saw glimpses of what he's capable of doing with his left foot but also with his IQ," said Crew coach Laurent Courtois. "He just needs to build his fitness up, be aware of the system and get to know his compañereos, his teammates. Just class.”

Méndez made his debut count 🙌 

No. 10 is getting off to a strong start with the Black & Gold 🖤💛 pic.twitter.com/BFGMiwbDo3

— The Crew (@ColumbusCrew) August 2, 2026

Though he signed at the beginning of July, Mendez did not touch down in Columbus until July 22 due to visa issues. He began training with the team two days later and made his first appearance against a strong Miami team a week after he began conditioning.

“From the start, the team has made me feel like I am part of the family. They have received me well since the first day, even before the transfer was done," said Mendez. "I am very happy to be here, and I hope to achieve big things for this club.”

Ironically, Mendez became the first Crew player to score in their MLS debut since Max Arfsten in 2023. Mendez finished with three shots, two of which were on target.

Pick any synonym for "messy," and it would appropriately describe the first half between the Crew and Miami. In the 16th minute, Luis Suarez stunted the Crew's possession play by sending a high-looping arc shot over goalie Patrick Schulte's head for the lead.

When Suarez took the shot from near the half-line after defender Andre Gomes lost possession, Schulte lurked near the front of the penalty area, placing him too far from position to run back and attempt a save chance.

Luis Suarez from long range! 😱

Seven goals in four games from the @InterMiamiCF striker. pic.twitter.com/NFkU26vjDJ

— Major League Soccer (@MLS) August 2, 2026

"We know [Suarez's] savviness, cheekiness. He is a world-class player, and any type of mistakes, he already has the next play in his head," Courtois said. "I asked my guys to try a lot of things and obviously we were aware of not losing the ball in those areas. But that's also the style of play we want to have, so we can't have it both ways."

Suarez may be in the late stages of his lengthy soccer career, but the 39-year-old forward still has gas left in the tank. His long-range goal made him the fifth player in MLS history to record at least 10 goals and five assists in three consecutive MLS seasons.

Then, during extra time of the first half, Suarez perfectly timed a run into the penalty area while seeking a through ball. Instead of attempting to score, he looped a pass to the head of defender Noah Allen for a creative assist and the 2-1 advantage entering the second half.

It was Casemiro redirecting a cross from Taha Habroune into Miami's net for an own goal that kept the Crew within a goal entering the second half.

Mendez's debut might've been the most consequential, but two other players debuted for the Crew against Miami: midfielder Lautaro Giaccone in the 72nd minute and defender Brooks Lennon in the 86th minute. Their not-so-simple task was to defend against eight-time Ballon d'Or winner Messi, who returned to the MLS for the first time since his eight-goal campaign in the 2026 World Cup.

Though he did not appear for the first 52 minutes, Messi entered and immediately took a barely off target shot in front of an energetic home crowd. Regardless of his entrance and 43% possession in the second half, the Crew locked down Messi and his teammates.

"We were struggling," said Courtois, "They were pushing hard. We had a little bit of tightness in the legs. It's a lot of minutes for some guys that still need to be back to their full level."

Past the 89th minute, Miami fired five shots, two of which Schulte saved, including a shot by Messi In the 93rd minute. Messi's last shot sailed over the center of the net.

The Crew will take the momentum from their late effort into three Leagues Cup games beginning on Aug. 4.

This article originally appeared on The Columbus Dispatch: Takeaways: Brais Mendez steps up in Crew debut to earn draw vs. Miami

title: Five key selection decisions England must make ahead of Pakistan series
description: Replacing Ben Stokes is just one of a number of conundrums for England’s new hierarchy
fullText:
A curious summer for England will continue in August as Pakistan arrive for a three-Test tour with Marcus Trescothick in interim charge of the hosts.

Stephen Fleming has been installed as Brendon McCullum’s successor with the Test team, but will not take up his role until September, leaving Trescothick to join a reappointed Joe Root in trying to set a new direction after a bruising series against New Zealand earlier in the year.

While Fleming will have some say in selection, the indications are that Trescothick and Root will be prominent voices, too, alongside selector Marcus North – who is set to speak after the squad is unveiled next week.

The retirement of Ben Stokes leaves a significant hole with England apparently lacking a like-for-like replacement as a seam-bowling all-rounder, with the knock-on impacts perhaps significant for the composition of the rest of the attack.

There may be batting places to think about, too, with Jacob Bethell a slight injury doubt. Here are five key decisions to be made:

The first question is one without a straightforward answer. Stokes’ batting powers may have, statistically, been on the wane, but he remained a force with the ball and a vital balancing figure within any XI. England looked uneasy during the second New Zealand Test when without their then-captain – better solutions must be found.

It feels likely that England search for a spinning all-rounder to replace Stokes at No 7. Rehan Ahmed has long been liked though lacks the bowling volume and, perhaps, consistency that England might desire; Will Jacks has not featured in a Test squad since the Ashes and similarly has a way to go with his second skill. More left-field, to some extent, options could include James Coles, the Sussex batting all-rounder, or Calvin Harrison, so impressive for Northants in all three facets over the last couple of years.

Could Sam Curran come under consideration? The left-armer worked closely with Fleming at the Chennai Super Kings a few years ago, and also under Root during the skipper’s first stint. A lack of recent red-ball experience may count against him, but Curran would appear keen for consideration.

The retirement of Stokes may be bad news for Shoaib Bashir, who is now tough to see being squeezed in, even if Curran is seen as a seam-bowling replacement. England have put a lot of time into their pet spin project, though Bashir hasn't maybe kicked on in the way that he, and they, would have liked. The tweakers could well be crucial at the end of a dry, hot summer, mind – will North et al. explore alternative specialists, or even consider playing two in the same team? That may bring Bashir back in, though the time may have come for a look elsewhere.

Jacob Bethell’s withdrawal from the Hundred came with a warning that further assessment was required for a knee injury that could put his place against Pakistan in peril. No further information has yet been forthcoming, but England will want their No 3 in situ to continue to build experience and form in Test cricket after a couple of bad dismissals against New Zealand.

Can Emilio Gay be said to be totally sure of his place at the top of the order? Gay was a victim of the Stokes-instigated chaos at the end of the Trent Bridge Test, eventually coming in at No 6, and has made a solid-if-unspectacular start to life at international level. It would be mightily harsh to not give him at least another series, though any potential Bethell absence could necessitate a reshuffle.

When speaking after the Fleming and Root appointments on Friday, Rob Key was eager to point out his excitement about England’s seamers, noting the way Gus Atkinson, Sonny Baker and Josh Tongue had been bowling in the Hundred as evidence of their fulfilling of all-format potential. Key, rightly, also noted the consistency that Jofra Archer has found since being rested for the first of the New Zealand Tests. Brydon Carse is back bowling, too, after a long lay-off and may come into the thinking when the squad is named for Pakistan – though is maybe a more limited bowler than others.

If a spinner is selected at No 7, there may be room for four quicks but ensuring complementary skillsets will be key. Ollie Robinson had a strange series with his ability still not in question, and a lack of accurate alternatives with the new ball may see him feature again. Archer is a virtual certainty to start but will probably not play all three Tests. Pakistan struggled against the West Indies’ high-class seamers in the first Test in Trinidad and England appear to have an array of options to try to trouble them.

A fresh era can bring with it fresh perspective on the construction of a cricket team. With North still new to his role, Fleming arriving and Root returning, it may be that the trio seek a departure in some ways from the McCullum/Stokes axis that has gone before. Both Fleming and Root have, in the past, shown a predilection for adaptability – Fleming’s CSK sides would regularly bat deep and mix up multifaceted orders, while Root enjoyed success with an England team of all-rounders in the past.

To enact something similar would require a significant shift, though it may be that new eyes see individuals differently – where does Jamie Smith best fit? What is the messaging to Harry Brook? Does the style need to change? While Fleming may not yet be in England, the next few weeks could say a lot about the side he wants to build.

title: Tarik Skubal breaks silence on Dodgers trade with so much emotion
description: Tarik Skubal had to fight back tears when it came time for him to talk about the Dodgers and Tigers trade.
fullText:
Of course Tarik Skubal was going to be emotional after the trade that sent him to the Los Angeles Dodgers (check out our trade grades of this one). The Detroit Tigers have been his Major League home since 2018, when the franchise took him in the ninth round of the 2018 MLB Draft.

He's pitched seven seasons with the big club and won two Cy Youngs, and it seemed like the Tigers were moving into contention last year. Sadly, it wasn't the same this season, and with Detroit not giving him a well-earned contract extension, the Tigers had to get something back before he headed into free agency.

As you'll see, he spoke to reporters early on Sunday morning and talked about the various emotions he was going through. Although he was excited to head to the Dodgers, Skubal talked about the failure to bring a World Series to the organization.

Then, he spoke about his now-former teammates whom he's best friends with, and you could hear his voice waver. Then, he needed a moment to collect himself before moving on to talk about his excitement surrounding joining the Dodgers.

Tarik Skubal GETS EMOTIONAL after trade to the Dodgers (📹ESPN) pic.twitter.com/Heo0egmQs0

— Darren M. Haynes (@DarrenMHaynes) August 2, 2026

A reminder that trades don't happen in a vacuum. There are people involved who have a mix of emotions.

title: Arteta Confirms Striker’s Arsenal Future After Transfer Speculation
description: Mikel Arteta appears to have put an end to speculation surrounding Viktor Gyokeres’ future by confirming the Swedish striker will remain at Arsenal this season.The 28-year-old only arrived from Spor...
fullText:
Mikel Arteta appears to have put an end to speculation surrounding Viktor Gyokeres’ future by confirming the Swedish striker will remain at Arsenal this season.

The 28-year-old only arrived from Sporting CP last summer, but recent reports had suggested he could be included in a potential swap deal involving Atletico Madrid forward Julian Alvarez.

However, speaking to journalist Victor Llebaria Escutia, Arteta dismissed any uncertainty over Gyokeres’ future.

When asked about Alvarez, Arteta refused to comment on a player contracted to another club.

“I’m not going to talk about a footballer who isn’t ours.”

The Arsenal boss was then pressed on Gyokeres’ future and gave a straightforward response.

Those comments appear to bring an end to recent speculation linking the Swedish international with a move away from the Emirates.

(Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images)

Gyokeres endured a difficult start following his move from Sporting CP, but his form improved significantly as the campaign progressed.

The striker finished the season with 21 goals in all competitions, establishing himself as an important attacking option for Arteta during the second half of the campaign.

Gyokeres’ first campaign in north London was something of a tale of two halves. After arriving from Sporting CP last summer, the Swedish international initially found it difficult to build chemistry with his new teammates and adapt to Arteta’s system. However, as the season progressed, his confidence and performances steadily improved. His physical presence caused problems for opposition defenders, while his goalscoring return of 21 in all competitions demonstrated why Arsenal remained patient with their summer signing.

With Arsenal preparing to defend their Premier League title, Arteta’s comments suggest Gyokeres remains firmly part of his plans heading into the new season. After ending last season on a high, the striker will now be hoping to carry that momentum into the new campaign and further establish himself as a key member of Arteta’s attacking options. Supporters will undoubtedly be pleased to hear the manager publicly backing the striker after weeks of transfer speculation.

title: How the Washington Commanders might utilize 12 and 13 personnel this season
description: What will David Blough’s offense look like this year using TEs Chigoziem Okonkwo, John Bates, and Ben Sinnott?
fullText:
During the early days of training camp, ESPN reporter John Keim caught up with Ben Sinnott to discuss how offensive coordinator David Blough plans to utilize the Commanders tight ends this season. Clearly, Sinnott was excited about the possibilities in Washington’s new offense.

“It’s not even close,” Sinnott said. “So many different variations. Today we’re lining up at number one, we’re running five-step ins, we’re running corners, we’re running options, we’re running flat [routes]. We’re just doing everything. It’s so much fun. It’s a breath of fresh air for this offense and how it uses tight ends.”

Head coach Dan Quinn has also detailed to reporters the role they see for free agent addition Chigoziem Okonkwo.

“Long play-action passing, over routes, pylon routes, things that are down the field, crossing routes that are catch-and-run to use some of his speed,” Quinn said. Previously, we examined how much the Washington Commanders might run heavy personnel this season, but today we look at a couple of examples of what it might look like on the field.

Likely the personnel grouping most utilized by the Commanders offense this year, 12 personnel involves one running back, two tight ends, and two wide receivers. The team has emphasized the need for multi-dimensional running backs while adding Okonkwo as a big receiving threat. To gain an understanding of how Blough might use Chig out of 12 personnel, we take a look at an All-22 breakdown of Sam LaPorta with the Lions in 2023. Ben Johnson was Detroit’s offensive coordinator and then-Lions quarterback David Blough was on the practice squad that year.

LaPorta showed promise when lined up as a WR in 2023, as well. This gave Ben Johnson and the Lions opportunities to use 12 Personnel groupings to create 11 Personnel formations.#Lions #DetroitLions pic.twitter.com/9wWqUCeRnh

— All 22 Films (@All_22_NFL_Cuts) June 19, 2024

There is nothing too flashy about LaPorta’s deployment; Johnson essentially uses his size and agility in 11 personnel formations to create mismatches against cornerbacks and linebackers. Okonkwo has already been utilized as a receiving threat by the Titans last year, with 56 receptions on 79 targets for 560 receiving yards. However, according to Next Gen Stats, Okonkwo functioned primarily in the short area of the passing game, with 62 targets coming in the first 10 yards of the line of scrimmage. Blough will likely get him more work in different areas of the field as detailed by Quinn. After being named Chicago’s head coach, Johnson continued to use 12 personnel with the Bears in a decidedly run-heavy scheme. The Commanders offense is expected to do the same.

Chicago Bears running Duo in 12 Personnel with an extra OL pic.twitter.com/zl5JJ8QgiA

— Last of the Fullbacks (@TheLastFullback) November 5, 2025

We start our look at 13 personnel with a detailed breakdown of a play by The Athletic’s Ted Nguyen. He analyzes the Los Angeles Rams in 13 personnel on second down with four yards to go. Receiving tight end Terrance Ferguson is split out wide, and Davis Allen is the H-back, with Davante Adams on the opposite side. The defense loads up to stop the run, but Sean McVay calls a passing play out of the look. Allen goes into inside motion and when the ball is snapped, he runs a vertical sail route. Ferguson runs a deep fade, and Adams a deep dig. Nguyen explains how the coverage dictated by the defense playing the run allows Allen to clear the safety and provides space for the completion to Adams.

Rams running 11 personnel pass plays with 13 personnel pic.twitter.com/eLoLdXptJV

— Ted Nguyen (@FB_FilmAnalysis) August 1, 2026

For the Commanders, Okonkwo would be split outside with Sinnott in the H-back role and Bates in-line. The goal would be to create an opportunity for Terry McLaurin, but Okonkwo is a viable threat on the outside and Sinnott operates well in the seam and would also be one. A multidimensional running back in the backfield keeps the defense honest and adds additional ways to attack the defense.

Here is another look at 13 personnel used by Ben Johnson and the Bears for a 2-point conversion in the NFC wild-card game last season. Chicago lines up in a 13 personnel look with Colston Loveland in-line on the left, Cole Kmet in-line on the right next to a third offensive tackle, and Durham Smythe at fullback. Before the snap, all three tight ends motion out, creating a spread formation as described here by Chicago Bears analyst Coach Usayd Koshul.

The #Bears will be using more 13 personnel in 2026 and this 2-point conversion playcall from the Wild Card win against #Packers serves as an example of why Ben Johnson made such a push to draft Sam Roush. 

The most underrated part of this play is that Green Bay is expecting run,… pic.twitter.com/saqVdjCqxk

— Coach Usayd Koshul (@usaydkoshul) May 4, 2026

The end result is Loveland one-on-one with a linebacker on the outside and an easy conversion. Again, you can see how Washington’s current personnel could fit the same play call, with Chigoziem in Loveland’s role, Bates in Kmet’s, and Sinnott shifting out from the fullback position. Blough might also opt to keep the formation the same and run the play as presented with a power back like Kaytron Allen running behind the heavy look.

In order to run these personnel groupings, the team needs players that are versatile and effective in multiple roles. Currently, the Commanders have three such players in Okonkwo, Sinnott, and Bates and while they may be more specialized in one aspect or another, each can function in multiple roles. Roster depth will also be key, and with blocking specialist John Bates on the shelf with an injury, the team will give Colson Yankoff and Lawrence Cager extended looks. Yankoff saw additional time last year when Ertz went out for the season and ended up playing 12% of the team’s total offensive snaps, both in-line and at fullback. The converted quarterback had the catch of the day during Thursday’s session training camp session. Undrafted free agent Quentin Moore will also get a longer look while Bates is recovering. Their continued development will be something to monitor as training camp ramps up this week.

title: Newcastle express interest in Italy and Atalanta defender Scalvini
description: Reports in Italy claim that Premier League side Newcastle United have reached out to request information from the agents representing 22-year-old Atalanta and Italy defender Giorgio Scalvini.Newcastle...
fullText:
Reports in Italy claim that Premier League side Newcastle United have reached out to request information from the agents representing 22-year-old Atalanta and Italy defender Giorgio Scalvini.

According to reports from Sky Sport Italia expert Gianluca Di Marzio, Newcastle have registered an interest in picking up Scalvini from Atalanta this summer. The Magpies have reportedly been in contact with the player’s representatives, but not yet with his current club.

Scalvini has two years remaining on his current contract with Atalanta, running until the summer of 2028, and has recently changed agents to join Ali Barat of Epic Sports. He had previously been represented by Tulio Tinti of TMP Soccer.

Recent reports claim that Atalanta value Sclavini in the region of €40m. Newcastle had also expressed an interest in signing the Italian centre-back last summer.

At the age of 22, Scalvini has already racked up 137 competitive appearances at senior level, including 113 in Serie A. He made his breakthrough with Atalanta at the age of 17 and made his senior debut for the Italy national team at the age of 19.

NEW YORK, NEW YORK – MARCH 23: Giorgio Scavini of Italy arrives before Italy training session at NY Red Bulls TG on March 23, 2024 in New York, New York. (Photo by Claudio Villa/Getty Images)

Widely regarded as one of Italy’s brightest prospects at centre-back, Scalvini’s progression took a significant knock when he suffered a cruciate ligament tear on the final day of the 2023-24 Serie A season. And, with other injury issues since then, Scalvini was limited to just six appearances in Serie A in 2024-25 and 24 in 2025-26.

title: We’re Looking For New Writers And Video Creators
description: We’d love more of you to join the TTE team - on written or video content.
fullText:
We’re almost at the start of a new season, one that’ll hopefully be a lot of fun to cover on this site, and we’d love some new faces to join the team here at The Tilehurst End.

First and foremost, writers. One of my favourite things about this gig as editor is getting to work with a range of contributors who offer a variety of perspectives and areas of focus on the site, whether it’s (for example) Alex’s opinion pieces, Steven’s Opposition Lowdown articles, Dixey’s columns or Pete’s coverage of Reading Women.

There’s an awful lot of people I could mention, to whom I’m massively grateful. It’s humbling knowing there are so many people willing to contribute! Not just on a regular basis, but also with standalone articles, such as Niall’s take on the price of junior kits or Oliver’s on Reading’s 2026/27 ambitions.

We’re always open to new ideas, whether it’s a regular feature, guest piece or anything else. There are no bad suggestions (within reason!). Perhaps something from the following takes your fancy…

“Ah, I’d be interested but I’ve never written anything before,” some of you may say. Experience is no issue. As long as you’re passionate about Reading FC and would be interested in writing about it, our door is open.

In fact, writing for us is particularly good for young, budding writers. It’s an opportunity to gain experience and put something on your CV, and we can offer valuable feedback.

We’re also after new video creators for our social pages (Twitter, Facebook, Bluesky and YouTube).

Ben does a great job with his post-match summaries (such as this one from the 4-0 win at Newport County) and we’d love more of the same for away games specifically. If you have an alternative suggestion for what to cover in a regular video feature, we’re open to that too.

The key thing we’re looking for here however is consistency. Videos don’t have to be too long or high-tech (a couple of minutes recording opinion/summary/analysis to camera works really well), but we would like to be putting them out regularly.

Even if you wouldn’t like to contribute, we’d love to hear your feedback on TTE – the site, video/podcast output, social media coverage or anything else – if you’ve got something to share.

Is there a gap in our coverage that should be filled? Is there something we can do better? What are we doing that you like and wish we did more often? All ideas, critiques and suggestions are more than welcome as it’s so useful for us knowing what we should be doing and where we can improve.

The best way to reach out is to drop us an email on thetilehurstend@gmail.com.

title: Angel Reese reveals what she still misses about Chicago after trade to Dream
description: Angel Reese has found a comfortable new home with the Atlanta Dream, but there is one part of Chicago she has not forgotten.
fullText:
Angel Reese reveals what she still misses about Chicago after trade to Dream originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Angel Reese appears to be enjoying nearly every part of her fresh start with the Atlanta Dream. Nearly four months after the Chicago Sky traded Reese to Atlanta, the two-time WNBA All-Star is producing the best season of her young career. She has also joined a winning team after spending her first two years in the league with a rebuilding Sky franchise.

Reese recently described Atlanta as “perfect” for her, praising everything from the Dream organization to the city’s culture. However, there is still one thing about Chicago that she wishes she could have brought with her.

“I think the Southern hospitality is something that you just can’t beat,” Reese told Cosmopolitan when discussing the differences between Atlanta and Chicago. “But I do miss the food in Chicago. But the food in Atlanta is pretty good, too.”

Reese has plenty of reasons to feel good about her move. The 24-year-old forward is averaging career highs of 15.8 points and 1.8 steals per game while adding 11.6 rebounds and 2.4 assists. Her production has helped the Dream emerge as a playoff contender with an 18-10 record, good for fifth place in the WNBA standings.

Winning has been one of the biggest changes for Reese.

The Sky selected her with the No. 7 overall pick in the 2024 WNBA Draft, but Chicago never established itself as a serious contender during her two seasons with the franchise. The Sky finished 13-27 during her rookie year and missed the playoffs again in 2025.

Atlanta has offered Reese a chance to play meaningful basketball while continuing to develop her offensive game.

She has also quickly built relationships with her new teammates away from the court. Reese told Cosmopolitan that Dream players have been looking for activities they can enjoy together, including a recent interest in escape rooms.

“We’re trying to find things for us to do,” Reese said. “We just started going to little escape rooms.”

That chemistry appears to be carrying over into games. Reese has become a central piece of an Atlanta roster attempting to make a deep postseason run.

MORE: Kelsey Plum trade grades: Mercury make bold playoff gamble as Sparks begin another rebuild

Reese’s time in Chicago came to an end in April when the Sky traded her to the Dream. The deal represented a significant change for both sides. Chicago moved on from one of the league’s most recognizable young stars, while Atlanta added an elite rebounder who had already established herself as a nightly double-double threat.

Reese later made it clear that she welcomed the opportunity to leave, saying she “wanted to go” and considered Atlanta an ideal fit. Her comments about missing Chicago’s food do not suggest any regret over the trade. Instead, they show that Reese can appreciate what she left behind while embracing her next chapter.

Chicago’s culinary scene is famous for much more than deep-dish pizza and Italian beef. The city’s wide range of neighborhood restaurants makes food an understandable part of life there for Reese to miss.

Still, Atlanta has given her the Southern hospitality, team culture and winning environment she wanted.

Chicago may have an advantage at the dinner table in Reese’s eyes, but Atlanta has become home.

title: 6-minute solar eclipse is coming Aug. 2, 2027. Where to see it
description: The total solar eclipse will be visible in these parts of the world. See where.
fullText:
Sky gazers are gearing up for the "eclipse of the century," penciled in for August 2027.

A total solar eclipse lasting up to six minutes and 23 seconds at its peak is expected on Aug. 2, 2027, according to NASA. The total solar eclipse, in which the moon moves perfectly between the sun and Earth, effectively casting a shadow on Earth, will be one of the longest in several decades.

In comparison, the total solar eclipse on April 8, 2024, lasted four minutes and 28 seconds at its peak. The solar eclipse of 1991, however, lasted six minutes and 53 seconds. Space.com reports that the solar eclipse on Aug. 2, 2027, will be the longest eclipse totality until 2114.

The eclipse will be visible in parts of Africa, Europe and the Middle East. However, the vast majority of the United States won't have a view of it.

Here's what to know about the solar eclipse expected on Aug. 2, 2027.

Space: Two eclipses happen in August. Here's who can see them

A partial solar eclipse will be visible in parts of Maine between 5:14 and 5:19 a.m. ET on Aug. 2, 2027, according to Time and Date. Unfortunately, this may be the only view of the phenomenon in the United States.

The solar eclipse's path of totality will cross over parts of Africa, Europe and the Middle East, according to National Eclipse and NASA.

Parts of the following countries are within the path of totality.

Other countries in Africa, Europe and the Middle East will have a partial view of the eclipse.

The Aug. 2, 2027, phenomenon isn't the next total solar eclipse. On Aug. 12, 2026, a solar eclipse will be visible in Greenland, Iceland, Spain, Russia and parts of Portugal, according to NASA.

Greta Cross is a national trending reporter at USA TODAY. Story idea? Email her at gcross@usatoday.com.

title: WATCH: Democrats admit when they'd eliminate the filibuster as SAVE Act fight heats up
description: Trump urges John Thune to eliminate the Senate filibuster or cancel August recess until lawmakers pass the SAVE Act election integrity bill.
fullText:
As President Donald Trump intensifies his push to eliminate the Senate filibuster to pass the SAVE America Act, lawmakers are exposing familiar fault lines over when the chamber's 60-vote rule should, and shouldn't, apply.

Democratic senators avoided endorsing an outright elimination of the filibuster. Some defended exceptions for certain legislation, with several arguing it should stay in place while Republicans push to pass the SAVE Act through the Senate.

"I would want to know what specific measure it covered," Sen. Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn., told Fox News Digital. "I'm in favor of eliminating the filibuster for specific measures, not across the board."

Trump's Voter Id Bill Catches Unlikely Break As Mcconnell Remains Sidelined

"When we wanted the Voting Rights Act passed, I was willing to do it," Sen. Maria Cantwell, D-Wash said.

"It depends on constitutional issues," she said. "If there are people that are overriding the Constitution and not following the Constitution, that would be an area where I would think about [eliminating the filibuster.]"

Democrats previously pushed to create exceptions to the filibuster for legislation including voting rights bills after Republicans repeatedly blocked those measures during President Joe Biden's administration.

As the SAVE Act stalls in the Senate, Trump has repeatedly urged Senate Majority Leader John Thune and other Senate Republicans to eliminate the filibuster to pass the election integrity bill.

"I think we have to be really careful," Sen. Angela Alsobrooks said. "The filibuster is what's preventing President Trump from his SAVE Act."

Trump took to Truth Social urging Thune not to allow the Senate to leave for August recess until lawmakers either pass the Save Act terminate the filibuster. He also insisted that Senate Democrats would do it to advance their own legislation if they regained the majority.

Watch: Elissa Slotkin Says Save America Act Would Make It 'Hard For Any Democrat' To Win An Election

"I think that the Democrats would absolutely eliminate the filibuster," Sen. Roger Marshall said. "Every Democrat senator that's here now, that was here when they had the chance, voted to end it."

Marshall explained that his position switched on this, with him now having newfound support for eliminating the filibuster as he claims the Democratic party has become unwilling to cooperate.

"Democrats don't want to cooperate," Marshall said.

He continued, "They want to do everything they can to make life miserable in America, thinking it's going to help them politically. Always putting their political goals ahead of what's best for America."

Trump Demands Thune Keep Senate In Session Until Save America Act Passes

Sen. John Kennedy, R-La., acknowledged the same argument that Thune has defended himself to the president for not passing the SAVE Act: the votes in the upper chamber are not there to remove the filibuster.

"[Trump] knows the votes aren't there to do what he wants to do, in the way he wants to do it," Kennedy said. "The House has passed a budget resolution to get reconciliation started. We can pass the SAVE Act with the right… the correctly crafted bill."

Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., is working to craft that bill to pass certain elements of the SAVE Act through the budget reconciliation process — dropping the need for Senate Democrats to vote in favor of the bill to get it passed to Trump.

"There comes a time when you got to stop talking and just vote," Kennedy said.

" I'm ready to vote, and I'm gonna vote yes. And I'll stay here as long into August or September as I need to for us to get our work done."

title: Democratic Socialists awarded $5.2M in inheritance dispute despite family's objections
description: A judge awarded the Democratic Socialists of America $5.2 million in an inheritance dispute, nearly doubling the organization's typical annual revenue.
fullText:
The Democratic Socialists of America just won $5.2 million in an inheritance dispute, according to a new legal filing, handing the organization a major financial boost as it seeks to expand its influence within the Democratic Party.

The $5.2 million award is serious money for the Democratic Socialists of America, amounting to nearly an entire year of revenue for the organization, according to its tax filings.

For a little over a year, the Democratic Socialists of America had been embroiled in a legal dispute over the will of New York University professor David Greenberg, who died in July 2024. Greenberg stipulated in his will that the contents of his New York University retirement account should be transferred to the New American Movement, a now-defunct left-wing activist group, or "any successor thereof" upon his death.

Bernie Sanders, Dsa Reveal Demands For Dem Party After Socialists Sweep New York Elections

The New American Movement merged with the Democratic Socialist Organizing Committee to form the Democratic Socialists of America in 1982, according to contemporary coverage in left-wing media outlets.

Greenberg, a sociology professor, spent much of his life involved with left-wing movements, and his NYU obituary described him as "a prominent figure in America's radical criminology movement."

Martin Hecht, Greenberg's nephew, contended that the Democratic Socialists of America failed to file the proper paperwork to be considered the legal successor and that New York University failed to fulfill its fiduciary duty to Greenberg by not making sure his will accurately reflected his wishes before his death.

The judge presiding over the case ultimately sided with the Democratic Socialists of America, handing it the multimillion-dollar sum. Hecht initiated his lawsuit in April 2025, and the case was ultimately decided Monday.

The $5.2 million constituted the majority of Greenberg's wealth, with a separate account worth $1.3 million being transferred to his estate without dispute, according to a legal filing.

Far-left Surge: Mamdani-backed Candidates Oust Dem Establishment Incumbents

This cash comes at an opportune time for the organization.

Candidates affiliated with or backed by the Democratic Socialists of America have enjoyed a string of victories in recent months, beginning with Zohran Mamdani's election as New York City mayor in 2025 and continuing with 2026 primary wins by candidates such as Claire Valdez and Darializa Avila Chevalier, who bested establishment-backed opponents in New York's congressional primaries.

Socialist candidates have also won primary races in Philadelphia, the District of Columbia and Colorado.

Republicans Sound Alarm Over Far-left Group's Push To Transform America Into 'Cuban Dictatorship'

The victories, several of which came against Democratic incumbents, have expanded the Democratic Socialists of America's foothold in government and given the group greater influence over the party, particularly in heavily Democratic urban districts.

What the Democratic Socialists of America ultimately will use its newfound wealth to do has not been disclosed, but its past spending behavior may provide some clues.

The organization, for instance, regularly spends big on advertisements meant to convince people to vote for Democratic Socialists of America-backed candidates. In an August 2024 blog post, one New York Democratic Socialists of America member floated paying for advertisements to support the organization's recruitment efforts.

Tax documents filed by the Democratic Socialists of America in November 2025 show that the organization distributes cash to its local chapters and aligned groups while also spending big on community mobilization and messaging campaigns.

These efforts appear to have borne some fruit. In early July, the Democratic Socialists of America announced that it had grown to 120,000 members, claiming that it had become the "largest socialist organization in United States history."

The Democratic Socialists of America and Hecht's attorneys did not respond to a request for comment when reached by Fox News Digital.

title: Here’s when you’ll get your Social Security check in August
description: No separate SSI check goes out in August since it landed early — the next payment for SSI recipients won't go out until Sept. 1.
fullText:
(NewsNation) — Social Security beneficiaries can expect a mostly normal payment schedule in August, though Supplemental Security Income recipients already received their August payment on July 31 because Aug. 1 fell on a weekend.

Aug. 3: Beneficiaries who began receiving Social Security before May 1997 or who also receive SSI

Aug. 12: Beneficiaries with birthdays between the 1st and 10th of the month

Aug. 19: Beneficiaries with birthdays between the 11th and 20th

Aug. 26: Beneficiaries with birthdays between the 21st and 31st

Because SSI payments were issued early, no separate SSI payment will be sent in August. The next SSI payment is scheduled for Sept. 1.

The Social Security Administration continues to encourage beneficiaries to use direct deposit or other electronic payment methods as it phases out paper checks. Fewer than 1% of beneficiaries still receive paper checks, according to the agency.

Anyone who does not receive an expected payment should first contact their bank. If the payment still has not arrived, beneficiaries are advised to contact the Social Security Administration or their local SSA office.
